2026-07-06.summary: FOMC minutes, Canada jobs, and PepsiCo/Delta earnings lead a quieter post-holiday week.

events.whatItIs: Eurostat's flash estimate of euro-area retail sales volume for May 2026, measuring the monthly change in consumer spending at brick-and-mortar and online retailers across the 20-member currency bloc.
events.whyItMatters: Eurozone retail sales have been persistently weak -- April fell 0.4% MoM as elevated ECB rates and above-target inflation squeezed household budgets. The May reading, the first data release of the week, sets the tone for European consumer demand and ECB policy expectations. A genuine recovery would ease stagflation fears; another decline would deepen the argument that the bloc is heading for a consumer-led contraction even as inflation runs hot.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.5% MoM: consumers adjusting to lower inflation and showing resilience. EUR firms modestly, relief bid in European equities, ECB cut expectations ease.
events.ifLower: Below -0.5% MoM: spending deteriorating further under restrictive policy. EUR softens, ECB cut bets firm, European equities under pressure.

events.event: ISM Services PMI (June 2026) -- delayed from July 3 holiday
events.whatItIs: The Institute for Supply Management's monthly composite index of business conditions across the US services sector, surveying purchasing managers on activity, new orders, employment, and supplier deliveries -- a reading above 50.0 signals expansion.
events.whyItMatters: Services account for roughly 80% of US GDP and employment, making the ISM the most comprehensive monthly read on the non-factory economy. Released one day late due to the July 3 holiday, it is the first major US data point after last Thursday's jobs report and before Wednesday's FOMC minutes. The prices-paid sub-index is the most market-sensitive component: it is a real-time read on services inflation, the stickiest part of the PCE basket the Fed is fighting to cool.
events.ifHigher: Above 53.0 with hot prices-paid: services demand holding and inflation sticky. Reinforces the Fed's no-cuts-in-2026 stance; USD firms, gold softens, short-end yields tick up.
events.ifLower: Below 49.0: services sector contracting. Revives recession and rate-cut speculation; gold firms, USD softens, stocks whipsaw on growth-scare vs. cut-hope tension.

events.event: JOLTS Job Openings (May 2026) -- delayed from July 3 holiday
events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for May 2026, reporting the number of unfilled job vacancies plus monthly hiring, quit, and layoff rates -- the most comprehensive snapshot of US labor demand and worker confidence available on a monthly basis.
events.whyItMatters: JOLTS was deferred from the holiday-shortened prior week and lands Tuesday in this quieter calendar. The ratio of job openings to unemployed workers (the Beveridge Curve position) is one of the metrics Chair Warsh cited in justifying the Fed's higher-for-longer stance. After last Thursday's NFP print, JOLTS will either confirm or undercut the labor demand picture -- a drop in openings below 7.0M would signal that employers are pulling back ahead of any slowdown, softening the Fed's 'still-strong labor market' argument for keeping rates elevated.
events.ifHigher: Openings above 7.5M: labor demand still robust. Supports the 'no 2026 cuts' stance; USD firms, short-end yields edge up, rate-cut bets fade.
events.ifLower: Openings below 6.5M: employers significantly pulling back on hiring intentions. Dovish case strengthened; gold firms, USD softens, markets price in a 2026 cut.

events.whatItIs: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand's Monetary Policy Committee decision on the Official Cash Rate -- New Zealand's benchmark short-term interest rate, announced at 02:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The July 8 hold at 2.25% is priced as near-certain by markets, but the real action is in the forward guidance. Major NZ bank economists at ASB, Westpac NZ, and ANZ NZ all forecast the RBNZ will begin raising the OCR from September 2026 as NZ inflation has rebounded. The accompanying Monetary Policy Review statement will reveal how close the committee is to triggering that hiking cycle -- lower fuel costs have removed urgency for July, but the tone on September will drive NZD and set expectations for the tightening trajectory.
events.ifHigher: Surprise hike to 2.50%: NZD surges 1-2%, global rate expectations recalibrated upward. Extremely unlikely but would ripple into AUD and EM FX.
events.ifLower: Surprise cut to 2.00%: NZD tumbles 2%+, hiking cycle expectations collapse. Extremely unlikely and would represent a sharp u-turn.

events.event: FOMC Meeting Minutes (June 16-17, 2026 -- Chair Warsh's first meeting)
events.whatItIs: The verbatim record of the Federal Open Market Committee's June 16-17 policy meeting, released three weeks after the decision -- the only public window into the committee's internal debate, dissenting views, and the economic conditions that underpinned Chair Warsh's hawkish pivot.
events.whyItMatters: The June 17 FOMC statement delivered Warsh's hawkish debut: stripping the cutting bias and guiding for no rate changes in 2026. But the statement was terse. The minutes reveal HOW divided the committee was (were there members leaning toward a hike or still favoring a cut?), WHAT specific data would reopen the door to a policy shift, and what the balance-sheet discussion looked like. After last Thursday's jobs report updated the labor-market picture, traders will use the minutes to calibrate whether any dovish minority remains relevant or whether the committee is unified behind Warsh's restrictive stance.
events.ifHigher: Minutes show unanimous hawkish consensus with elevated inflation thresholds for cuts: USD spikes, gold drops, 2-year yields rise, 2026 cut is dead.
events.ifLower: Minutes reveal a large dovish minority or explicit low unemployment thresholds that trigger cuts: gold rallies, USD softens, rate-cut bets snap back to life.

events.previous: CPI: +1.2% YoY (May 2026); PPI: +2.8% YoY (May 2026 -- near four-year high on Iran-war energy costs and AI/tech investment boom)
events.whatItIs: China's National Bureau of Statistics monthly consumer price index and producer price index for June 2026, measuring inflation at the retail level (CPI) and at the factory gate (PPI) -- the primary gauges of China's price dynamics and a key read on global input-cost trends.
events.whyItMatters: China's CPI has remained subdued near 1.2% YoY, but the PPI has rebounded to near four-year highs on Middle East oil supply disruptions and the AI/tech capex boom driving up industrial demand. Together they matter globally: a still-elevated PPI signals rising manufactured-goods input costs that can feed through to global consumer prices, while CPI tells the PBoC whether it has room to ease further or must hold. With the Fed higher-for-longer and the dollar firm, PBoC easing would deepen the US-China rate differential, weighing on CNY and lifting commodity-linked assets.
events.ifHigher: CPI above 1.5% or PPI above 3.5% YoY: inflationary pressure building. PBoC easing bets fade, CNY firms, modest lift for commodity-linked assets on China demand narrative.
events.ifLower: CPI approaching 0% or PPI turning negative: deflation risk returning. PBoC easing bets firm, CNY softens, gold and oil come under mild pressure on demand concerns.

events.whatItIs: PepsiCo's second-quarter 2026 earnings report covering April through June 2026 performance across its global beverage (Pepsi, Gatorade, Tropicana) and snack food (Lay's, Doritos, Cheetos, Quaker) segments, posted at 10:00 UTC with analyst Q&A at 12:15 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: PepsiCo is one of the first major consumer staples companies to report Q2 results, making it a bellwether for how US and global consumers are handling persistent inflation and whether tariff-driven input-cost increases are being absorbed by margins or passed on via price hikes. As a large US-listed multinational, PEP's results also surface FX headwinds from the stronger dollar. Guidance language on H2 2026 volume and pricing power will set the tone for the entire consumer staples sector.
events.ifHigher: Revenue and EPS beat with raised full-year guidance: consumer staples resilient. Defensive sectors get a confidence boost; broader market views pricing power as intact.
events.ifLower: Volume miss or lowered guidance: tariff and inflation pressure biting consumer spending more than expected. Consumer discretionary and staples under pressure; soft demand narrative firms.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of new unemployment insurance claims filed for the week ended July 4 -- the most frequent real-time read on US labor-market conditions, released every Thursday at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: With NFP released last Thursday and FOMC minutes on Wednesday, Thursday's claims update the labor picture in real time before Friday's Canada jobs report and the weekend. The July 4 holiday week almost always produces a distorted print as some state offices close and workers delay filing -- so any spike toward 250K should be treated with caution. But a sustained upward trend in coming weeks would begin to shift the narrative toward labor softening, which would revive cut expectations in a market currently priced for zero 2026 moves.
events.ifHigher: Above 260K: claims spiking beyond holiday distortion, possible genuine labor deterioration. Gold and bonds rally, USD softens -- apply holiday-week caveat.
events.ifLower: Below 185K: labor market extremely tight even through holiday noise. Reinforces the higher-for-longer narrative; USD firms, gold softens.

events.whatItIs: The Destatis final confirmation of Germany's consumer price index for June 2026, incorporating complete data from all German states -- typically matches the preliminary estimate published on June 30 but the detailed breakdown of services, food, and energy components is new.
events.whyItMatters: Germany's June preliminary CPI came in at 2.3% YoY on June 30 -- a full 0.3 percentage point below May's 2.6% and well below the 2.6% consensus, suggesting euro-area inflation may be cooling faster than expected. The final reading confirms or revises that print and, crucially, provides the component breakdown that tells the ECB whether the disinflation was broad-based (goods and services) or concentrated in energy. A confirmation of broad-based cooling would strengthen the case for another ECB easing step in the second half of 2026.
events.ifHigher: Final revised up to 2.5%+ YoY or with hot services component: preliminary understated price pressure. EUR firms, ECB cut bets pared, bunds under mild pressure.
events.ifLower: Final confirmed at 2.2-2.3% with cooling services: disinflation genuine and broad-based. EUR softens modestly, ECB easing expectations strengthened.

events.whatItIs: Delta Air Lines' second-quarter 2026 earnings report covering April through June 2026 -- the peak travel season and traditionally the airline's strongest quarter, released before the US market open on Friday.
events.whyItMatters: Delta is the first major US carrier to report Q2 results, making it a sector-wide read on whether the premium travel demand that drove airline stocks higher in late 2025 is holding into 2026. Investors are focused on unit costs (CASM) under tariff-driven fuel and maintenance inflation, international vs. domestic revenue trends, capacity guidance for H2 2026, and whether elevated borrowing costs are finally cooling consumer appetite for discretionary travel. How Delta frames the macro backdrop will set the tone for the rest of Q2 airline earnings.
events.ifHigher: Revenue beat with raised full-year guidance: travel demand robust despite cost pressures. Airlines sector rallies; oil demand outlook implied-positive.
events.ifLower: Revenue miss or lowered guidance: consumers pulling back on discretionary travel spend. Airlines sell off; consumer discretionary pressured, oil demand outlook softens.

events.previous: Employment Change: +87.8K; Unemployment Rate: 6.6% (May 2026 -- strongest monthly gain of 2026, unemployment down from 6.9% in April)
events.whatItIs: Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey for June 2026, measuring net employment change, the unemployment rate, full-time vs. part-time job creation, and labor-force participation rate -- Canada's equivalent of the US nonfarm payrolls report, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The Bank of Canada holds its next rate decision on July 29. After May's blowout +87.8K surge sent unemployment down to 6.6% from 6.9% -- the sharpest monthly improvement of 2026 -- June data will determine whether that was a genuine turning point or a temporary one-month spike. Consensus expects a sharp payback to just +10K. A miss below 0 or a jump in unemployment would revive BoC cut bets ahead of July 29; a second strong month would cement the case for a hold or even tightening.
events.ifHigher: Jobs above +50K with unemployment steady or falling: labor market momentum confirmed. CAD firms, July 29 BoC cut bets fade, oil-correlated assets get a mild lift.
events.ifLower: Jobs below 0 or unemployment rises to 6.8%+: May was a fluke, labor market deteriorating. CAD weakens, BoC July 29 cut bets firm, oil softens on Canada macro weakness.

2026-07-20.summary: Alphabet and Tesla earnings, the ECB decision, and July flash PMIs headline a big week.

events.event: China PBoC Loan Prime Rate (1Y & 5Y, July 2026)
events.whatItIs: The People's Bank of China's monthly fixing of the 1-year and 5-year Loan Prime Rates -- the benchmark reference rates that price most Chinese corporate loans (1Y) and mortgages (5Y), published on the 20th of each month.
events.whyItMatters: The LPR is China's main conventional policy lever, and with the Fed higher-for-longer the PBoC has limited room to cut without pressuring the yuan and widening the US-China rate gap. A surprise 5Y cut would target the still-fragile property sector and signal Beijing prioritising growth over currency stability; a hold keeps the easing bias measured. Commodity-linked assets and the Australian dollar are the cleanest read-throughs.
events.ifHigher: Both rates held with hawkish guidance: PBoC prioritising CNY stability. Mild headwind for industrial metals and China-demand plays.
events.ifLower: Surprise 5Y cut: Beijing stepping up property support. Copper, iron-ore proxies and AUD firm on the China-stimulus narrative.

events.whatItIs: Alphabet's second-quarter 2026 results, covering Google Search, YouTube, and Google Cloud, released after the US close with the analyst call to follow -- the first Magnificent Seven mega-cap to report this season.
events.whyItMatters: Alphabet is the market's first hard data point on whether the AI-capex boom is translating into revenue rather than just spending. Google Cloud's growth rate and operating margin and any update to the multi-hundred-billion-dollar cloud backlog will be scrutinised for signs the hyperscaler AI build-out is paying off. After last week's semiconductor round-trip, guidance on 2026 capex is as market-moving as the print itself -- it feeds directly into Nvidia and the entire chip complex.
events.ifHigher: Cloud reaccelerates and capex guidance is disciplined: AI-monetisation narrative validated. Lifts the Nasdaq, chips, and risk sentiment broadly.
events.ifLower: Cloud decelerates or capex balloons without revenue: 'AI spend without return' fears resurface. Chips and megacap tech sell off, dragging the tape.

events.whatItIs: Tesla's second-quarter 2026 results, with the earnings webcast at 21:30 UTC, covering vehicle deliveries and margins, energy storage, and updates on autonomy/robotaxi and the Optimus program.
events.whyItMatters: Tesla trades as much on narrative as numbers: automotive gross margin (ex-credits), the pace of the robotaxi rollout, and energy-storage growth are the swing factors. Reporting the same evening as Alphabet, it doubles Wednesday's after-hours volatility for the Nasdaq and for retail-heavy sentiment. Guidance on 2026 delivery trajectory and any concrete autonomy timeline will drive the stock's double-digit post-earnings moves that ripple into the broad index.
events.ifHigher: Auto margins beat and robotaxi timeline firms: bull case reanimated. TSLA gaps up, lifts retail risk appetite and the Nasdaq.
events.ifLower: Margin compression or delivery guidance cut: growth-story doubts return. Sharp drop pressures megacap-growth and high-beta sentiment.

events.event: ECB Rate Decision (July 2026) + Lagarde Press Conference (12:30 UTC)
events.previous: Deposit rate 2.25% (hiked 25bps on June 11 -- first hike since 2023)
events.whatItIs: The European Central Bank Governing Council's monetary policy decision, announced at 11:45 UTC, followed by President Christine Lagarde's press conference at 12:30 UTC. July is a non-projection meeting, so no updated staff forecasts accompany the decision.
events.whyItMatters: The ECB broke from the global pack in June with a surprise hike tied to Middle East energy-driven inflation. With a hold near-certain (markets price ~88%), all the signal is in the tone: roughly 70% of economists expect another hike in 2026, likely September. Because there are no new projections, Lagarde's characterisation of inflation risks and any explicit conditioning of a September move is what drives the euro. A hawkish hold widens the EUR-USD rate story; a dovish 'one-and-done' framing unwinds it.
events.ifHigher: Hawkish hold signalling September hike live: EUR firms, bunds sell off, European banks bid, adds to broad USD-EUR two-sidedness.
events.ifLower: Dovish hold framing June as one-and-done: EUR softens, bunds rally, European equities catch a relief bid.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of new unemployment-insurance claims for the week ended July 18, released every Thursday at 12:30 UTC -- the most frequent real-time gauge of US labor-market conditions.
events.whyItMatters: With the Fed in blackout and no jobs report this week, claims are the only fresh US labor read before the July 28-29 FOMC. Now past the July 4 holiday distortion, the print is cleaner: a sustained drift toward 250K would start to shift the narrative toward labor softening and revive 2026 cut expectations that markets have largely priced out under Chair Warsh's higher-for-longer stance.
events.ifHigher: Above 250K: labor market cooling into the FOMC. Gold and bonds bid, USD softens, cut expectations edge back.
events.ifLower: Below 200K: labor market still tight. Reinforces higher-for-longer; USD firms, gold softens.

events.whatItIs: Intel's second-quarter 2026 results, released after the US close -- watched for what could be the company's first GAAP-profitable quarter after six consecutive quarters of GAAP losses, plus foundry progress and AI-accelerator traction.
events.whyItMatters: Intel is the turnaround bellwether of the semiconductor space. A first GAAP profit in seven quarters would validate the restructuring and foundry strategy; continued losses would sharpen doubts about its ability to compete for AI silicon. Coming a day after Alphabet and Tesla, and amid a jittery chip tape, Intel's foundry and data-center commentary colours sentiment across the semiconductor complex into Friday.
events.ifHigher: GAAP profit with foundry milestones: turnaround credibility improves. Supports chips and the broad semi sentiment.
events.ifLower: Another GAAP loss or weak guidance: restructuring doubts deepen. Adds to semiconductor-sector pressure.

events.event: Eurozone Flash PMIs (July 2026 -- Manufacturing, Services, Composite)
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary July purchasing-managers indices for the euro area, the first read on eurozone business activity for the month -- a reading above 50.0 signals expansion.
events.whyItMatters: Released the morning after the ECB, the flash PMIs are the first hard activity data to test the ECB's growth assumptions under a newly restrictive stance. The services and prices sub-indices matter most: sticky input prices would validate the June hike, while a slide back below 50 would stoke stagflation worries just as the ECB signals more tightening.
events.ifHigher: Composite above 52 with firm prices: economy absorbing higher rates. EUR firms, ECB September-hike bets build.
events.ifLower: Composite below 49: activity rolling over under restrictive policy. EUR softens, European equities pressured on stagflation fears.

events.event: UK Flash PMIs (July 2026 -- Manufacturing, Services, Composite)
events.whatItIs: S&P Global/CIPS preliminary July PMIs for the UK, the earliest gauge of British private-sector activity for the month across manufacturing and services.
events.whyItMatters: The flash PMIs feed directly into Bank of England expectations. Services activity and input-price pressure are the swing factors for whether the BoE can keep easing or must stay on hold, and they drive sterling and gilts ahead of the next MPC meeting.
events.ifHigher: Composite above 52 with hot services prices: sticky UK inflation. GBP firms, BoE cut bets pared.
events.ifLower: Composite below 49: UK activity contracting. GBP softens, BoE easing expectations firm.

events.event: US Flash PMIs (July 2026 -- S&P Global Manufacturing, Services, Composite)
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary July purchasing-managers indices for the US, the first monthly read on private-sector activity -- released at 13:45 UTC, ahead of the official ISM surveys.
events.whyItMatters: As the last major US data before the July 28-29 FOMC (with the Fed in blackout), the flash PMIs are the market's freshest look at growth and pricing momentum. The prices-charged sub-index is a real-time services-inflation proxy the Fed watches; the output and new-orders components gauge whether the economy is holding above stall speed. A hot composite with firm prices cements the no-cuts stance; a sharp cooling reopens the cut debate the moment the Fed can speak again.
events.ifHigher: Composite above 54 with rising prices: growth and inflation both firm. USD bid, gold softens, yields tick up into the FOMC.
events.ifLower: Composite below 50: activity contracting. Growth scare bids gold and bonds, USD softens, cut expectations rebuild.

events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's report on newly built single-family homes sold in June 2026, reported as a seasonally adjusted annual rate at 14:00 UTC -- a timely read on housing demand and the rate-sensitivity of the consumer.
events.whyItMatters: Housing is the most interest-rate-sensitive corner of the economy, so new home sales are a clean gauge of how restrictive policy is biting. With mortgage rates elevated under the Fed's higher-for-longer stance, a soft print would evidence the lagged drag of tight policy; a resilient number would argue the consumer and housing are absorbing high rates better than feared.
events.ifHigher: Above 700K: housing demand resilient despite high mortgage rates. Supports the soft-landing narrative; homebuilders bid.
events.ifLower: Below 620K: rate drag intensifying on housing. Adds to slowdown evidence; homebuilders and cyclicals soften.

2026-07-27.summary: July FOMC, Microsoft/Meta/Apple/Amazon earnings, Q2 GDP and core PCE in one week.

events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's advance report on new orders for manufactured goods designed to last three years or more -- aircraft, machinery, computers, vehicles -- released at 12:30 UTC as an early read on business investment.
events.whyItMatters: Headline durable goods is dominated by lumpy aircraft orders, so the signal sits in core capital goods (nondefense ex-aircraft), the cleanest monthly proxy for corporate capex. Coming into FOMC week, a firm capex trend argues the economy is absorbing a 3.50-3.75% funds rate without breaking, which supports the hawkish case Warsh has been building.
events.ifHigher: Above +2%: business investment accelerating, higher-for-longer looks affordable. USD firms, cyclicals bid.
events.ifLower: Below flat: capex hesitancy spreading, growth-scare tone. Gold bid, cut expectations creep back in.

events.whatItIs: The Conference Board's monthly survey of roughly 3,000 US households, split into a Present Situation Index on current conditions and an Expectations Index on the six-month outlook, released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The labour-market internals matter more than the headline right now. The share of consumers saying jobs are 'hard to get' climbed to 22.5% in June, the highest since January 2021, even as the Expectations Index rose. That divergence -- households feeling worse about jobs today but better about tomorrow -- is exactly the tension the Fed has to resolve on Wednesday, and it lands the day before the decision.
events.ifHigher: Above 96 with 'jobs hard to get' falling: labour softening was a blip. Supports the hawkish hold, USD firms.
events.ifLower: Below 87 with 'jobs hard to get' above 23%: labour cracks widening. Gold bid, 2026 hike odds trimmed.

events.event: FOMC Meeting Day 1 (July 28-29) -- no statement until Wednesday
events.whatItIs: The first of two days of Federal Open Market Committee deliberations. No communication is released on day one; the statement and press conference follow on Wednesday afternoon.
events.whyItMatters: The Fed remains in its communications blackout through Wednesday's decision, so there is no Fed-speak to trade and positioning tends to compress ahead of the announcement. Volume thins and ranges narrow into the event.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- no release.
events.ifLower: N/A -- no release.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending July 24)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly report on US commercial crude, gasoline, and distillate stockpiles, plus refinery utilisation, released at 14:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Energy is the swing factor in this inflation cycle. The oil rally tied to Middle East supply risk is what pushed CPI to 4.2% year-over-year and what turned the Fed hawkish in the first place. A sustained draw that pushes crude higher directly feeds the inflation-expectations channel the FOMC is worried about, hours before the decision.
events.ifHigher: Large draw: crude rallies, inflation-expectation channel reopens, adds hawkish pressure to the statement.
events.ifLower: Large build: crude softens, headline-inflation pressure eases, mildly dovish read-through.

events.event: FOMC Rate Decision (July 2026) + Warsh Press Conference (18:30 UTC)
events.whatItIs: The Federal Open Market Committee's policy decision at 18:00 UTC, followed by Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 18:30 UTC. This is a non-projection meeting: no dot plot and no updated Summary of Economic Projections accompany the statement.
events.whyItMatters: A hold would be the fifth consecutive one, but the tail has fattened considerably: market-implied hike odds tripled from roughly 11% to 35% in the week to July 22 as oil prices, heavy Treasury supply, and 4.2% headline CPI reset the inflation debate. Nine officials in the June dot plot see at least one hike this year. With no dot plot to anchor expectations and a chair who has signalled he will give minimal colour and no forward guidance, the entire market reaction hinges on statement wording and the vote split. Any dissent in favour of a hike would be read as a September move being live.
events.ifHigher: Surprise hike or a hold with explicit hawkish dissents: USD spikes, gold sells off hard, front-end yields jump, equities and crypto de-risk.
events.ifLower: Hold with softened inflation language or no dissent: relief rally in equities and gold, USD gives back, September hike odds unwind.

events.forecast: Azure growth guided 39-40% constant currency; buy-side bogey ~36%
events.whatItIs: Microsoft's fiscal fourth-quarter results, released after the US close, covering Azure and the Intelligent Cloud segment, Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption, and full-year capital expenditure on AI datacentre capacity.
events.whyItMatters: Azure's constant-currency growth rate is the single most-watched number in the AI trade. Management guided 39-40% and the buy-side bar sits near 36%, so the print has room to beat the whisper and still disappoint the guide. Alphabet cleared its revenue bar last week and still fell 7% because capex guidance overwhelmed it, which tells you the market is now punishing spend without a visible return. Microsoft's FY27 capex commentary will set the tone for the entire semiconductor complex.
events.ifHigher: Azure above 38% with disciplined capex: AI monetisation validated. Nasdaq and chips rally, risk appetite broadens to crypto.
events.ifLower: Azure below 36% or capex guided sharply higher: the Alphabet reaction repeats. Megacap tech and semis sell off, dragging the index.

events.whatItIs: Meta's second-quarter results covering Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Threads advertising revenue, Reality Labs losses, and the AI infrastructure spending programme, reported after the close alongside Microsoft.
events.whyItMatters: Meta is the purest read on digital ad demand, which is a real-time proxy for consumer-facing corporate confidence, and simultaneously one of the largest AI capex spenders outside the hyperscalers. Revenue consensus near $60.2B implies roughly 27% growth. The swing factor is the same as everywhere else this season: whether the AI spend line is framed as an investment with visible returns or an open-ended commitment.
events.ifHigher: Revenue beat with capex held in check: ad market healthy and AI spend disciplined. Lifts the Nasdaq alongside Microsoft.
events.ifLower: Ad revenue softens or capex guidance jumps again: the 'spend without return' trade resumes. High-multiple tech de-rates.

events.event: Bank of England Rate Decision + Minutes (July 2026)
events.whatItIs: The Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee's Bank Rate decision at 11:00 UTC, published with the minutes and the vote split, plus the updated Monetary Policy Report forecasts.
events.whyItMatters: A hold is close to fully priced, so the trade is entirely in the vote split and the new inflation profile. ING expects a prolonged pause through 2026 with the forecasts showing inflation peaking near 3% later this year, but a Reuters poll found nearly 40% of economists expect at least one hike, and Chief Economist Huw Pill has said rates will need to rise. Sterling's reaction depends on how many members break ranks and whether the MPC treats the energy-price spike as a hike trigger or a pass-through it can look past.
events.ifHigher: Multiple hike dissents or an above-3% inflation peak in the forecasts: GBP rallies, gilts sell off, September hike gets priced.
events.ifLower: Unanimous hold with the energy spike framed as transitory: GBP softens, gilts rally, the pause extends into 2027 pricing.

events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's first of three estimates of second-quarter real GDP growth, expressed as a seasonally adjusted annual rate, released at 12:30 UTC the morning after the FOMC decision.
events.whyItMatters: This is the first hard verdict on whether the economy is absorbing a restrictive funds rate. Because it lands the morning after the Fed, it either validates or immediately undercuts whatever Warsh said the night before. Consumer spending is the component to watch given June personal spending arrives in the same release window. A print below 1.5% would revive the dovish case that the hawkish tail is being priced into a slowing economy.
events.ifHigher: Above 2.5%: growth resilient under tight policy, the hawkish case strengthens. USD firms, gold pressured.
events.ifLower: Below 1.5%: the slowdown is real, policy is biting. Gold rallies, cut expectations return, cyclicals sold.

events.event: Core PCE Price Index (June 2026) + Personal Income and Spending
events.previous: Core 3.4% YoY, headline 4.1% YoY (May 2026); income +0.7%, spending +0.7% MoM
events.forecast: Core ~+0.2% MoM; income and spending near +0.5-0.7%
events.whatItIs: The BEA's Personal Income and Outlays report containing the PCE price index, the inflation measure the Fed formally targets, alongside monthly household income and consumption. Released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Core PCE at 3.4% year-over-year is 140 basis points above target and the direct justification for Warsh's hawkish framing. A core reading at or below +0.2% month-over-month starts bending the annual rate lower and validates the decision to hold rather than hike; anything at +0.4% or above makes the September meeting genuinely live. It is also the last major inflation datapoint before the August recess, so it sets the summer narrative.
events.ifHigher: Core above +0.3% MoM: disinflation stalled at a high level. USD spikes, gold sells off, September hike odds jump.
events.ifLower: Core at or below +0.2% MoM: the annual rate starts rolling over. Gold and equities rally, the hawkish tail deflates.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of new unemployment insurance filings, the highest-frequency read available on the labour market, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Claims at 187K describe a labour market that is still historically tight, which sits awkwardly against consumer surveys showing 'jobs hard to get' at a five-year high. Claims are the tiebreaker between those two stories. Staying below 200K removes any labour-market argument against a hawkish Fed; a break above 230K would be the first genuine crack.
events.ifHigher: Above 230K: labour market loosening, the dovish case gets its evidence. Gold bid, yields fall.
events.ifLower: Below 190K: no cracks at all, hawkish hold fully justified. USD firms.

events.whatItIs: Apple's fiscal third-quarter results covering iPhone, Services, and Greater China revenue, with gross margin guidance for the September quarter, released after the US close.
events.whyItMatters: Apple goes into the print near its 52-week high, which sets a demanding bar. The specific pressure point this quarter is memory costs: DRAM and NAND pricing has risen sharply on AI datacentre demand, and Apple is a price-taker on both. That squeezes hardware gross margin at the same time investors want evidence that Apple Intelligence is driving an upgrade cycle rather than just a marketing line.
events.ifHigher: iPhone beat with margins defended and China stabilising: the safest megacap holds the tape up into month-end.
events.ifLower: Margin guidance cut on memory costs or China weakness: a large index weight rolls over, dragging the S&P.

events.whatItIs: Amazon's second-quarter results covering AWS growth and margin, North America and International retail segments, advertising revenue, and capital expenditure guidance, released after the close alongside Apple.
events.whyItMatters: AWS is the third leg of the hyperscaler stool after Google Cloud and Azure, and by Thursday evening the market will have all three. If AWS growth confirms the pattern set by the other two, the AI-infrastructure thesis is intact for another quarter; if it diverges, the read is that cloud demand is being concentrated rather than expanding. Retail margin also matters as a consumer-health datapoint two days after GDP.
events.ifHigher: AWS accelerates with retail margin expansion: completes a clean megacap sweep, risk assets close the month strong.
events.ifLower: AWS decelerates or capex guidance jumps: caps a week where every hyperscaler was punished for spending. Nasdaq sells off.

events.event: China Official Manufacturing and Non-Manufacturing PMI (July 2026)
events.whatItIs: The National Bureau of Statistics' monthly survey of purchasing managers at large, mostly state-owned Chinese enterprises, published at 01:30 UTC. Readings above 50 signal expansion.
events.whyItMatters: China's factory sector is the demand side of the global commodity complex. With the PBoC holding the Loan Prime Rate steady and limited room to ease without pressuring the yuan, the PMI is the clearest monthly evidence on whether existing stimulus is working. It also lands ahead of the Asian session's reaction to the BoJ, making Friday morning in Asia unusually busy.
events.ifHigher: Above 51: Chinese demand recovering. Copper, iron ore, AUD and China-exposed equities bid.
events.ifLower: Below 49: contraction deepening. Commodity demand fears, risk-off tone into the European open.

events.event: Bank of Japan Rate Decision + Quarterly Outlook Report (July 2026)
events.forecast: 1.00% hold; Outlook Report expected to lift FY2026 GDP to ~0.8%
events.whatItIs: The Bank of Japan's policy decision concluding the July 30-31 meeting, released around 03:00 UTC with the quarterly Outlook for Economic Activity and Prices, followed by Governor Ueda's press conference at 06:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The BoJ hiked to 1.00% in June, its highest policy rate since 1995, and is expected to pause here while the yen sits near a 40-year low. That combination is the tension: a weak yen imports inflation and argues for moving faster, but the bank has signalled a deliberately slow path. Reuters-polled analysts see 1.25% by December with October live. Barclays and Bank of America both read July as a tactical pause rather than a cycle end, and Barclays expects Ueda to sound hawkish. For global markets the yen carry trade is the transmission channel -- a hawkish surprise tightens financial conditions well beyond Japan.
events.ifHigher: Surprise hike or an explicitly hawkish Ueda flagging October: yen surges, carry trades unwind, global risk assets wobble.
events.ifLower: Hold with cautious guidance: yen stays weak near multi-decade lows, Nikkei bid, carry trade extends.

events.event: Eurozone Flash CPI (July 2026) + Q2 GDP Flash Estimate
events.forecast: Near 2.8%; core the key swing factor
events.whatItIs: Eurostat's first estimate of July consumer price inflation across the 20-member euro area, published alongside the flash estimate of second-quarter GDP growth.
events.whyItMatters: The ECB hiked in June for the first time since 2023 on energy-driven inflation, then held in July with roughly 70% of economists expecting another move by September. June's drop to 2.8% from 3.2% took some urgency off, so July decides whether that was a genuine turn or a one-month energy base effect. Pairing it with Q2 GDP gives the cleanest available snapshot of whether the ECB is tightening into a slowing economy.
events.ifHigher: Above 3.1% with core firm: September hike becomes the base case. EUR rallies, bunds sell off.
events.ifLower: Below 2.6% with soft GDP: June's hike looks one-and-done. EUR softens, European equities catch a relief bid.

events.whatItIs: The BLS's quarterly measure of total labour compensation including wages, salaries and benefits, controlled for shifts in the mix of jobs and industries -- the cleanest available read on underlying wage pressure.
events.whyItMatters: ECI is the Fed's preferred wage gauge precisely because it is not distorted by composition effects the way average hourly earnings is. In an inflation episode driven by an energy shock, the whole question is whether it leaks into wages. A print above +1.0% would be direct evidence of second-round effects and would materially raise September hike odds, closing out the week on the same theme the FOMC opened it with.
events.ifHigher: Above +1.0%: wage-price spiral risk is live. USD firms, gold sells off, hike odds jump.
events.ifLower: At or below +0.8%: wage pressure contained despite the energy shock. Risk assets rally into month-end.

events.event: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (July 2026, final)
events.whatItIs: The final July reading of the University of Michigan's household survey, covering current conditions, expectations, and one-year and five-to-ten-year inflation expectations, released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Sentiment rebounded sharply from 49.5 in June to a 54.4 preliminary July reading, but the level remains deeply depressed by historical standards. The market-relevant component is long-run inflation expectations: the Fed has repeatedly cited de-anchoring risk as its reason for staying hawkish, so a further rise there matters more than the headline. It is the last datapoint of a heavy month and lands into month-end rebalancing flows.
events.ifHigher: Confirmed above 55 with stable inflation expectations: consumer recovering, month-end closes constructive.
events.ifLower: Revised below 52 or long-run inflation expectations rising: de-anchoring worry, gold bid.

2026-08-03.summary: July NFP, ISM Services, and AMD/Disney/Palantir earnings drive a busy post-FOMC week.

events.whatItIs: China's National Bureau of Statistics monthly survey of purchasing managers at large state-owned manufacturers; above 50 signals expansion, below 50 contraction.
events.whyItMatters: China's factory sector is the demand engine behind global commodity flows. With Beijing's stimulus constrained by the PBoC's reluctance to widen the US-China rate gap, the PMI is the best monthly read on whether the industrial economy is stabilising. A print decisively above 50 would lift copper, oil, and AUD going into a week where the US labour market already commands attention.
events.ifHigher: Above 51: Chinese factory demand recovering, commodity complex gets a lift. Copper, crude, and AUD bid.
events.ifLower: Below 48: contraction deepening. Risk-off tone on global demand fears; commodity proxies soften.

events.whatItIs: Destatis's monthly report on the volume of goods sold by German retailers -- the euro area's largest consumer market -- covering food, clothing, electronics, and online sales.
events.whyItMatters: German consumers have been squeezed by elevated energy costs and rising ECB rates, leaving retail sales persistently weak. A second consecutive negative month would add to the stagflation picture in the bloc and reinforce the case that the ECB's June hike is slowing an already-weak economy -- EUR-negative on growth fears but potentially EUR-supportive once it forces the ECB to signal a pause.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.8%: German consumer rebounding. EUR firms, European equities get a relief bid, ECB pause bets ease.
events.ifLower: Below -0.5%: spending deteriorating. EUR softens, stagflation fears firm, European equities under pressure.

events.event: S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI Final (July 2026)
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's final July read on US manufacturing activity, revising the preliminary flash PMI with complete survey data -- released at 13:45 UTC, 15 minutes ahead of the ISM version.
events.whyItMatters: The flash-to-final revision is rarely large, but the output, new orders, and prices-charged sub-indices are the components traders use to cross-check the ISM Manufacturing print arriving shortly after. A divergence between the two surveys sets up a tiebreaker narrative for the session.
events.ifHigher: Final revised above flash with rising prices: factory inflation re-emerging. Modest USD bid ahead of ISM.
events.ifLower: Revised down from flash: demand weaker than the preliminary signalled. Slight USD softness heading into ISM.

events.whatItIs: The Institute for Supply Management's monthly composite index of conditions across US manufacturing, surveying purchasing managers on new orders, production, employment, supplier deliveries, and inventories -- a reading above 50 signals expansion.
events.whyItMatters: Manufacturing has been in contraction territory for most of 2026, and at 49.0 in June it stayed in its rut even as the broader services economy held firm. The new orders sub-index is the forward demand signal and prices paid is the inflation gauge that speaks directly to the Fed's debate. A sustained break back above 50 would be a genuine growth-positive surprise; a slip below 47 would revive factory-recession concerns.
events.ifHigher: Above 51: factory orders accelerating, cycle is turning. USD firms, cyclicals and industrials bid.
events.ifLower: Below 47: manufacturing contraction deepening. Growth scare; gold bid, cyclicals sold.

events.whatItIs: Palantir's second-quarter results covering its US commercial and government AI software revenue, international operations, and AI Platform (AIP) adoption, released after the US close with a webcast at 21:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Palantir has become one of the primary proxies for AI monetisation in government and enterprise settings. US government revenue is structurally protected by long-term contracts -- making this a cleaner read on commercial AIP uptake than any hyperscaler. With Iran-war defence spending elevated and Washington's appetite for AI-enabled intelligence tools at a cycle high, the government segment bar is high. The stock carries a premium multiple, so the reaction is asymmetric: a guide above $1.1B for Q3 could add 10%+, while a miss or soft commercial commentary would be punished sharply.
events.ifHigher: Revenue above $1.1B with commercial AIP acceleration: AI monetisation narrative strengthened. PLTR surges, pulls defence-tech and AI software peers.
events.ifLower: Revenue miss or weak commercial bookings: high-multiple AI stocks re-rate lower. Drags speculative risk assets including crypto.

events.event: New Zealand Unemployment Rate + Employment Change (Q2 2026)
events.whatItIs: Statistics New Zealand's quarterly Labour Market Statistics, covering the official unemployment rate, employment change, and labour force participation -- released at 22:45 UTC (Tuesday NZ time).
events.whyItMatters: The RBNZ surprised markets with a 25bps hike to 2.50% at its July meeting, and the next decision hinges on whether the labour market is tight enough to validate further tightening. A rising unemployment rate above 5.3% would push back against the hiking cycle; a steady or tightening labour market keeps October live. NZD is the cleanest expression.
events.ifHigher: Unemployment above 5.4%: labour market deteriorating. NZD softens, RBNZ October hike odds trimmed.
events.ifLower: Unemployment at or below 5.0%: tighter than expected. NZD firms, October RBNZ hike bets rise.

events.whatItIs: Caterpillar's second-quarter results covering construction, mining, and energy equipment sales across North America, EMEA, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America -- the most widely watched industrial-sector bellwether.
events.whyItMatters: Caterpillar is the premier read on global capital expenditure in construction and mining, and its dealer inventory data and order backlog are real-time gauges of infrastructure and commodity-sector demand. With the US infrastructure bill still driving multiyear spending and Middle East energy disruption lifting mining capex globally, consensus expects a strong quarter. The swing factor is management commentary on the H2 order pipeline -- any softening in North American construction given elevated financing costs would pressure the entire industrial complex.
events.ifHigher: Beat with raised full-year guidance: industrial capex holding despite high rates. Industrials rally, cyclicals bid, supports the no-landing narrative.
events.ifLower: Revenue miss or H2 guide cut: infrastructure demand cracking under high rates. CAT drags the industrial and materials sectors.

events.whatItIs: Pfizer's second-quarter results covering its oncology, internal medicine, vaccines, and antiviral franchises -- the first major pharma company to report Q2 this week, ahead of Eli Lilly on Wednesday.
events.whyItMatters: Pfizer's pipeline progress in oncology and weight-management is the primary lens this quarter, with the stock having lagged Eli Lilly substantially on GLP-1 competitive positioning. Any positive signal on Pfizer's own obesity candidate or its cancer pipeline would be disproportionately well-received given the sector discount. Commentary on US drug-pricing legislation is also live given the ongoing Congressional debate.
events.ifHigher: Surprise pipeline beat or raised guidance: healthcare sector gets a bid, narrows the gap with LLY.
events.ifLower: Revenue miss or pipeline setback: pharma stays under pressure; LLY and Novo remain the dominant GLP-1 plays.

events.event: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) Q2 2026 Earnings (after close)
events.whatItIs: AMD's second-quarter results covering its Data Center (MI300 AI accelerator), Client (Ryzen CPUs), Gaming, and Embedded segments, with the analyst call at 21:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: AMD is the primary challenger to Nvidia in the AI accelerator market, and its MI300 GPU ramp is the single data point that tells you whether AI silicon demand is broad enough to support two winners. Hyperscalers Google, Meta, and Microsoft have all publicly committed to AMD as a second-source supplier -- so a strong Data Center beat validates that commitment and extends the AI hardware cycle. A soft MI300 guide would raise questions about whether customers are consolidating spend on Nvidia and pulling back from AMD.
events.ifHigher: Data Center above $4.5B with strong MI300 guide: two-winner AI thesis intact. AMD surges, pulls semis and AI hardware peers, risk sentiment improves into Thursday.
events.ifLower: Data Center miss or weak Q3 guide: AI silicon concentration risk raised. Semi sector sells off, drags Nasdaq.

events.whatItIs: Eli Lilly's second-quarter results led by Mounjaro (tirzepatide for diabetes) and Zepbound (for obesity) -- the fastest-growing pharmaceutical products in the world by revenue -- with the analyst call at 13:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: LLY is the most important single-stock read on whether the GLP-1 obesity-drug market is living up to its multi-trillion-dollar valuation premise. The supply constraint that limited prescriptions in 2024-2025 has largely unwound, so growth must now come from genuine demand expansion. Manufacturing capacity guidance for H2 2026 and any update on the oral GLP-1 pipeline will drive a stock that trades at a steep premium to the broader pharma sector.
events.ifHigher: GLP-1 revenue above $7B with raised full-year guidance: obesity market demand confirmed durable. LLY rallies, lifts healthcare sector and biotech broadly.
events.ifLower: GLP-1 revenue miss or market saturation signals: the market-size assumption is challenged. LLY and Novo Nordisk both sell off sharply.

events.whatItIs: Disney's fiscal third-quarter results covering Disney+, Hulu, ESPN+, Parks and Experiences, and its Entertainment studios segment, reported before the US open with management commentary at 12:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The Iran war and elevated fuel costs have created a bifurcated consumer -- premium domestic park attendance may be soft as households watch spending, while streaming engagement could be a beneficiary of at-home substitution. The critical metric is streaming profitability: after years of losses, Disney+ turned profitable in 2025 and the market's patience for the parks drag depends on streaming delivering durable margins. Any sign of subscriber churn would undercut the 'streaming is the growth engine' thesis.
events.ifHigher: Streaming profitability beats and parks guidance holds: consumer resilience confirmed. DIS rallies, lifts consumer discretionary.
events.ifLower: Streaming margins compress or parks attendance guides soft: consumer-discretionary demand eroding. DIS drags the sector.

events.whatItIs: Uber's second-quarter results covering its Mobility (rides) and Delivery (Uber Eats) segments globally, with the analyst call at 12:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Uber gross bookings are a real-time read on consumer spending on discretionary services -- a category under pressure from elevated fuel costs and cautious household budgets. Autonomous vehicle commentary is increasingly relevant as Waymo expands, so any update on Uber's AV partnership strategy will drive the stock beyond the headline numbers. Solid bookings growth would read as a green light for the consumer-services segment heading into Friday's NFP.
events.ifHigher: Gross Bookings beat with margin improvement: consumer discretionary spend holding up. UBER rallies, lifts gig-economy and consumer tech peers.
events.ifLower: Bookings miss or margin guidance cut: consumers pulling back on discretionary services. Signals caution for Friday's NFP consumer-spending context.

events.whatItIs: Shopify's second-quarter results covering gross merchandise volume, merchant solutions, and subscription services -- the broadest available read on small-to-mid-size e-commerce merchant health.
events.whyItMatters: Shopify's GMV growth tracks the health of the independent e-commerce ecosystem, which has been buffeted by tariff uncertainty affecting merchant inventory planning and consumer price sensitivity. Management commentary on checkout conversion rates and merchant take rates will determine whether the platform is capturing e-commerce share gains or facing headwinds from large-platform substitution.
events.ifHigher: GMV above $77B with margin expansion: SMB e-commerce resilient. SHOP rallies, lifts fintech and e-commerce infrastructure plays.
events.ifLower: GMV miss or guidance cut: SMB merchants under pressure from tariffs and cautious consumers. E-commerce complex softer.

events.whatItIs: ADP Research Institute's monthly estimate of private-sector payroll growth derived from its payroll-processing data covering roughly 25 million US workers, released at 12:15 UTC -- two days ahead of the official BLS jobs report.
events.whyItMatters: June's ADP came in at +98K, soft but less alarming than the BLS's +57K official count, and the gap between the two series underscores that the labour-market picture is genuinely murky. With the FOMC having just held in July partly on the strength of a tight labour market, a second consecutive ADP reading below 100K would make Friday's NFP a potentially market-moving shock regardless of the headline. The breakdown by firm size matters: small-business hiring is the first to crack, and any acceleration in small-firm layoffs would flag genuine labour-market fragility.
events.ifHigher: Above +150K: private payrolls rebounding strongly. NFP bar set high for Friday. USD firms, gold softens, hike bets tick up.
events.ifLower: Below +75K: second month of soft private hiring. NFP miss risk elevated. Gold bid, USD softens, cut expectations re-emerge.

events.whatItIs: The Institute for Supply Management's monthly composite index of business conditions across the US services sector, surveying purchasing managers on activity, new orders, employment, and prices -- a reading above 50.0 signals expansion.
events.whyItMatters: Services account for roughly 80% of US GDP, and ISM Services at 54.0 in June was one of the pillars supporting the Fed's 'economy is absorbing high rates' argument. A meaningful slip toward 52 or below would challenge that narrative in the same week that ADP may already be soft. The prices-paid sub-index is the most market-sensitive component: it is a real-time read on services inflation, which is the stickiest component of core PCE and the Fed's primary inflation battleground.
events.ifHigher: Above 55 with firm prices-paid: services economy accelerating, inflation sticky. USD firms, hike bets tick up, gold softens.
events.ifLower: Below 52: services growth decelerating materially. Growth concern hits before Friday's NFP; gold bid, USD softer, cut bets re-emerge.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending August 1)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly report on US commercial crude oil, gasoline, and distillate stockpiles plus refinery utilisation, released at 14:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Oil prices are the inflation cycle's primary transmission channel -- the Middle East conflict pushed crude higher and triggered the Fed's hawkish pivot in 2026. Sustained draws signal tight supply and support crude prices, which feed directly into headline CPI and PCE, keeping the hawkish case alive. A large build would ease energy-price pressure and mildly support the view that headline inflation is about to roll over -- a relief signal on the same day ISM Services prints.
events.ifHigher: Large draw (5M+ barrels): crude rallies, energy-inflation channel reopens. Adds to inflationary pressure heading into Friday's NFP.
events.ifLower: Large build (5M+ barrels): crude softens, headline inflation eases. Mild dovish read-through ahead of the jobs report.

events.whatItIs: The Australian Bureau of Statistics' monthly report on the difference between goods exported and imported, a key gauge of Australian commodity export demand -- primarily iron ore, coal, and LNG -- and domestic import appetite.
events.whyItMatters: Australia's trade surplus is a direct read on Chinese and global demand for raw materials. A narrowing surplus driven by weaker iron ore export volumes would confirm that China's factory PMI weakness is flowing through to physical commodity purchases. Strong export values driven by higher energy prices (LNG) would paint a different and more bullish picture for AUD.
events.ifHigher: Surplus above A$7B: strong commodity export demand. AUD bid, iron ore and copper-linked assets firmer.
events.ifLower: Surplus below A$3B: commodity demand softening. AUD weakens, materials sector under mild pressure.

events.whatItIs: Eurostat's flash estimate of euro-area retail sales volume for June 2026, measuring the monthly change in consumer spending across the 20-member currency bloc.
events.whyItMatters: Euro-area consumers have been squeezed between elevated ECB rates and imported energy inflation. The June data lands the week after the ECB held at 2.25% and gives the first consumption read for Q3, setting the stage for whether the bloc's GDP trajectory is improving or deteriorating. A rebound would ease recession fears; a dip would add to the 'tightening into weakness' narrative ahead of the September ECB meeting.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.5%: consumers adapting, ECB over-tightening fears ease. EUR firms, European equities get a lift.
events.ifLower: Below -0.3%: spending contracting. EUR softer, adds to case for ECB pause in September.

events.whatItIs: Airbnb's second-quarter results covering nights and experiences booked, average daily rates, and full-year revenue guidance -- the peak-travel quarter and the most important period of the fiscal year.
events.whyItMatters: Airbnb is a real-time read on whether the global travel and tourism sector is shrugging off geopolitical uncertainty from the Iran war or adjusting its booking behaviour. The company has noted the conflict has weighed on some regional markets while boosting domestic and alternative-destination travel. Q2 is the most critical quarter for the travel economy, and whether average daily rates are holding is the clearest signal on consumer willingness to pay for discretionary experiences.
events.ifHigher: Nights booked and ADRs both beat with raised full-year guidance: travel demand resilient. ABNB rallies, lifts travel and hospitality sector.
events.ifLower: Bookings miss or ADR compression: geopolitical friction dampening travel. ABNB and the travel complex soften.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of new unemployment insurance filings, the highest-frequency real-time gauge of US labour-market conditions, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Thursday claims are the market's last labour-market data point before Friday's NFP, functioning as an unofficial handicap for the jobs number. After June's shocking +57K NFP print, claims are being watched for any sign of genuine deterioration versus statistical anomaly. Claims above 220K would add to the case that labour is cracking; below 190K would argue the June miss was noise and set NFP expectations higher.
events.ifHigher: Above 230K: labour market cracks visible before NFP. Gold bid, USD softens, markets position defensively.
events.ifLower: Below 185K: no deterioration evident. NFP expectations firm, USD bid, gold softer into Friday.

events.whatItIs: China's General Administration of Customs monthly report on exports, imports, and the resulting trade surplus, released in early Asian trading and reported in US dollar terms.
events.whyItMatters: China's export growth is a real-time read on global demand for manufactured goods -- particularly relevant given the ongoing US-China tariff regime and the impact of Middle East disruptions on shipping routes. Imports reveal the state of domestic Chinese demand, a critical signal for commodity markets. A weak imports number arriving on the same morning as US NFP would compound any risk-off mood.
events.ifHigher: Exports beating and imports firm: global demand resilient, Chinese domestic economy recovering. Commodity complex and AUD get a lift.
events.ifLower: Export miss with weak imports: global trade slowing and China domestic demand soft. Risk-off tone, commodity proxies soften.

events.whatItIs: Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey for July 2026, measuring net employment change, the unemployment rate, and full-time vs. part-time job creation -- Canada's equivalent of the US nonfarm payrolls report, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The Bank of Canada held rates steady at its July 29 meeting -- the same day as the Fed -- and the labour market is the primary input into whether the BoC stays on hold or resumes easing in September. Canada's export-heavy economy is also sensitive to US demand trends, so a weak Canadian jobs print arriving alongside US NFP would be a double-negative for CAD and would reinforce any dovish read on North American labour markets broadly.
events.ifHigher: Above +50K with unemployment steady: BoC on hold narrative reinforced. CAD firms, oil-correlated assets get a mild lift.
events.ifLower: Below 0 or unemployment above 6.9%: labour market deteriorating. CAD weakens, BoC September cut bets firm, oil softens.

events.event: Nonfarm Payrolls (July 2026) + Unemployment Rate + Avg Hourly Earnings
events.previous: +57K jobs (June 2026); Unemployment 4.2%; Avg Hourly Earnings +0.3% MoM
events.forecast: ~+130K jobs; Unemployment 4.2%; Avg Hourly Earnings ~+0.3% MoM
events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' Employment Situation report, covering July's net payroll change across all non-farm sectors, the unemployment rate, labour force participation, and average hourly earnings growth -- the single most market-moving monthly data release in the US.
events.whyItMatters: June's +57K print was one of the softest readings since the 2020 pandemic shock, arriving well below the +115K consensus and immediately cutting Fed hike odds -- a key input into the July 29 FOMC hold. The July number decides whether June was a one-month weather or seasonal anomaly or the start of sustained labour-market cooling that would shift the September 15-16 FOMC from a hawkish hold toward a possible cut. Average hourly earnings are the secondary focus: if wages stay at +0.3% MoM even as hiring slows, the wage-price channel is narrowing in the Fed's favour; a drop to +0.1-0.2% would make a September cut explicitly live.
events.ifHigher: Above +175K with unemployment at 4.1%: June was noise, labour market re-accelerating. USD spikes, gold sells off, September hike bets re-emerge, stocks whipsaw on hawkish repricing.
events.ifLower: Below +75K or unemployment above 4.4%: labour deterioration confirmed. Gold rallies strongly, USD drops, September cut fully priced, equities catch a relief bid on rate-cut hopes.

2026-08-10.summary: July CPI and PPI both cooled; retail sales and UMich sentiment close the week.

events.whatItIs: A composite of eight labour-market indicators that the Conference Board aggregates into a single leading gauge of hiring momentum.
events.whyItMatters: A quiet Monday with no tier-one data, but after the -23K July payrolls shock this index is one of the few forward reads available before the inflation block starts on Wednesday. It smooths the month-to-month noise that made the NFP print so jarring.
events.ifHigher: A rise back above 107 argues the payrolls drop was a one-month distortion; mildly USD-supportive.
events.ifLower: A slide below 105 confirms hiring momentum is genuinely rolling over; gold bid, hike odds fade.

events.whatItIs: The National Federation of Independent Business survey of small-firm owners across hiring plans, capital spending, pricing intentions, and general outlook.
events.whyItMatters: Small businesses employ roughly half the private workforce, so this is the cleanest counterweight to a weak payrolls print. It beat hard: 99.8 against a ~96.8 estimate, the highest since August 2025 and above the 52-year average of 98.0, with eight of ten components rising and hiring plans the single biggest contributor. That directly contradicted the -23K NFP read and kept the hawkish Fed dissenters in the argument going into CPI.
events.ifHigher: Above 99 with firm hiring plans: the labour market is not breaking. USD firms, hike odds hold.
events.ifLower: Below 95: small-business demand cracking alongside payrolls. Gold bid, cyclicals sold.

events.event: CPI (July 2026) -- headline and core, MoM and YoY
events.forecast: +0.1% MoM headline, +0.2% MoM core; 3.4% and 2.5% YoY
events.actual: +0.1% MoM headline (3.4% YoY); +0.2% MoM core (2.5% YoY) -- in line
events.whatItIs: The BLS Consumer Price Index: the monthly change in what urban consumers pay for a fixed basket of goods and services, reported both including and excluding volatile food and energy.
events.whyItMatters: This was the week's centrepiece and the direct test of the three hawkish FOMC dissents from July 29. It came in precisely on the Dow Jones consensus across all four measures, which was the quietly bullish outcome: no hawkish re-pricing, no dovish catalyst, just confirmation that disinflation is grinding on. Shelter rose only 0.1% and contributed about two-thirds of the monthly increase, while energy fell 1.5% MoM despite still sitting 14.7% above year-ago levels. Markets moved to roughly a 62-67% probability of a September hold, with only about a third pricing a 25bp hike.
events.ifHigher: Core above +0.4% MoM would have handed the dissenters their case: USD spikes, gold and BTC sold, September hike repriced above 50%.
events.ifLower: Core at +0.1% or below would have killed the hike debate outright: USD sold, gold and risk assets rally hard.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending August 7)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly count of commercial crude oil held in US storage, plus gasoline and distillate stocks.
events.whyItMatters: Landing two hours after CPI, this print carried more than usual weight because gasoline was the story on both sides of the inflation data -- prices fell 12% in June and another 5.7% at the wholesale level in July. Builds in crude and gasoline stocks reinforce the disinflation that CPI and PPI just delivered; a sharp draw would start rebuilding the energy contribution the Fed has been counting on to fade.
events.ifHigher: A large build signals soft demand or strong supply: crude sells off, the energy drag on CPI extends.
events.ifLower: A large draw signals tight supply: crude rallies, and the disinflation tailwind from energy starts to reverse.

events.event: PPI (July 2026) -- final demand, MoM and YoY
events.whatItIs: The BLS Producer Price Index for final demand: what domestic producers receive for their output, measured before those costs reach the consumer.
events.whyItMatters: PPI is the upstream cross-check on CPI and several of its components feed directly into the PCE deflator the Fed actually targets. July came in flat against a +0.2% forecast, a second straight soft month after June's -0.3%, and the annual rate dropped from 5.5% to 4.7%. The composition matters: final demand goods fell 0.7% on a 3.1% drop in energy and a 5.7% plunge in gasoline, while services rose only 0.2% after +0.5% in June and construction jumped 2.2%. Back-to-back soft PPI months with services decelerating is the strongest evidence this week that the pipeline pressure behind the hawkish dissents is genuinely easing.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.4% MoM with services accelerating: pipeline inflation rebuilding, USD bid, September hike odds jump.
events.ifLower: Negative MoM again: producer margins compressing and disinflation broadening. Gold and risk assets bid, hike odds collapse.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of new filings for unemployment insurance -- the highest-frequency read on layoffs available.
events.whyItMatters: After the -23K payrolls print, weekly claims became the market's real-time check on whether that was a data artefact or the start of something. Claims rose 9K to 209K but the four-week average held at 199K, still historically low. That combination -- negative payrolls with sub-200K claims -- points to a hiring freeze rather than a layoff wave, which is exactly the ambiguity keeping the September FOMC decision live.
events.ifHigher: Above 240K sustained: layoffs are broadening, the hike debate ends. Gold rallies, USD sold.
events.ifLower: Back below 200K: no layoff cycle, just slower hiring. USD firms, hawkish dissenters retain leverage.

events.event: Deribit BTC + ETH Weekly Options Expiry
events.whatItIs: Deribit's weekly settlement of Bitcoin and Ether options contracts, the largest crypto options venue by open interest.
events.whyItMatters: The expiry lands four and a half hours before US retail sales, so dealer hedging into settlement can amplify whatever the data does. With BTC having reclaimed $64K on the back of the CPI relief bid, the max-pain level determines whether market makers are selling into strength or buying dips through the European session.
events.ifHigher: BTC settling well above max pain: call holders paid, dealers buy to hedge, momentum extends into the US session.
events.ifLower: BTC settling below max pain: puts in the money, hedging flows add downside pressure ahead of retail sales.

events.event: Retail Sales (July 2026) -- headline and ex-autos, MoM
events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's monthly estimate of receipts at US retail and food service establishments, reported in nominal dollars and not adjusted for inflation.
events.whyItMatters: The week's last real question. Payrolls fell, small-business optimism surged, and inflation cooled -- the consumer is the tiebreaker. Because retail sales are nominal, a soft CPI month mechanically flatters the real volume read, so a +0.3% headline against +0.1% CPI means genuine volume growth. The control group excluding autos, gas, building materials, and food services is the piece that feeds GDP and the one to watch.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.5% with a firm control group: the consumer is intact despite the payrolls drop. USD bid, cyclicals rally, September hike odds rebuild.
events.ifLower: Negative headline with a soft control group: weak jobs are already hitting spending. Gold rallies, growth scare tone, hike talk ends.

events.event: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (August 2026, preliminary)
events.whatItIs: The University of Michigan's monthly survey of household attitudes toward personal finances, business conditions, and buying intentions, plus its closely watched inflation expectations series.
events.whyItMatters: July's final reading was revised up to 55.2 from a 54.0 preliminary, but sentiment is still about 11% below year-ago levels. The number that matters to the FOMC is not the headline: it is the one-year inflation expectation at 4.2%, which is running far above actual CPI at 3.4%. Anchored expectations are the entire justification for holding rates rather than hiking, so a move higher here does more damage to the dovish case than any single price print this week.
events.ifHigher: Sentiment above 57 with 1-year expectations easing below 4.0%: the best combination for risk assets. Gold steady, equities and BTC bid.
events.ifLower: Sentiment below 52 with expectations above 4.5%: stagflationary read, the worst outcome. Gold rallies on the growth scare while hike odds rise on expectations.

2026-08-17.summary: FOMC minutes, UK CPI, and Friday flash PMIs headline a retail-earnings week.

events.event: Japan Q2 GDP (preliminary) -- QoQ and annualized
events.whatItIs: The Cabinet Office's first estimate of second-quarter real GDP, covering private consumption, business investment, and net exports, released at 23:50 UTC Sunday.
events.whyItMatters: Sources have the BoJ preparing to hike as soon as September, with money markets pricing around a 62% chance after last week's hawkish Summary of Opinions. A solid Q2 print with consumption at or above +0.5% strengthens that case into Friday's national CPI; a miss gives the doves a growth argument and takes September off the table.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.7% QoQ with firm consumption: BoJ September hike odds jump. JPY bids, USD/JPY sold, global carry unwinds at the margin.
events.ifLower: Below +0.2% or consumption negative: hike case delayed. JPY sold, USD/JPY extends, risk assets catch a mild carry bid.

events.event: China Activity Data (July 2026) -- industrial production, retail sales, fixed-asset investment
events.previous: IP +5.3% YoY; retail +1.0% YoY; FAI -5.7% YTD YoY (June 2026)
events.forecast: IP ~5.0% YoY; retail ~1.5% YoY; FAI ~-6.0% YTD YoY
events.whatItIs: The National Bureau of Statistics monthly snapshot of factory output, household spending, and year-to-date capital formation -- the three numbers that define China's growth pulse.
events.whyItMatters: The split is the story: industry has held up while retail is barely growing and fixed investment is contracting. Thursday's PBoC LPR decision is expected to hold at 3.00%/3.50%, so a soft Monday print would raise the odds of targeted easing later and hit copper, oil, and the Aussie before Australian jobs on Thursday.
events.ifHigher: IP above 5.5% with retail above 2.0%: China demand stabilizing. Commodities and AUD bid, risk tone firms into the US open.
events.ifLower: IP below 4.5% or retail negative: growth scare. Oil and copper sold, AUD and CNH weaken, risk-off tone into Canada CPI.

events.event: Canada CPI (July 2026) -- headline and core, MoM and YoY
events.previous: -0.4% MoM / +2.8% YoY headline; +0.1% MoM / +2.1% YoY core (June 2026)
events.forecast: +0.5% MoM headline; ~2.9% YoY; core ~2.2% YoY; Common/Median/Trim watched near 2.1%
events.whatItIs: Statistics Canada's monthly Consumer Price Index, including the Bank of Canada's preferred Common, Median, and Trimmed-mean core measures, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The BoC is on hold inside a 1-3% control range with money markets pricing about a 52% chance of a 25bp hike by year-end. June's drop to 2.8% headline and 2.1% core was the dovish print; July has to show whether energy and the Middle East risk premium are pushing Canada back toward the top of the band. A hot core average would re-open a September hike; another soft month would lock the hold.
events.ifHigher: Headline above 3.1% or the three-measure average above 2.4%: BoC hike odds jump. CAD firms, oil-linked FX bid, USD/CAD sold.
events.ifLower: Headline at or below 2.6% with the average under 2.0%: hike case dies. CAD sold, gold catches a mild bid on easier North American policy.

events.whatItIs: The New York Fed's monthly survey of manufacturers in New York State, reported as a diffusion index where any reading above zero signals expanding activity.
events.whyItMatters: July's 15.6 was a strong print; August is expected to cool toward 10. The prices-paid and employment sub-indices are the pieces that matter this week: they are the first regional tell on whether factory inflation is still fading after last week's soft PPI, ahead of Friday's national flash PMI.
events.ifHigher: Above 15 with hot prices paid: factory inflation re-accelerating. Modest USD bid, Friday PMI bar rises.
events.ifLower: Below 5 or negative: regional factory demand rolling over. USD softens, cyclicals sold into housing starts Tuesday.

events.event: UK Labour Market (June/July 2026) -- unemployment, wages, claimant count
events.previous: Unemployment 4.9%; AWE incl. bonus +4.3%; AWE ex-bonus +3.4%; claimant count +6.7K
events.forecast: Unemployment 4.8%; AWE incl. bonus +4.0%; AWE ex-bonus +3.3%; claimant count +5.2K
events.whatItIs: The ONS labour-market package: the ILO unemployment rate for the April-June quarter, regular and total average weekly earnings, and July's claimant-count change.
events.whyItMatters: Wage growth is the BoE's live second-round-effects test after the Middle East energy shock. Headline CPI is expected to bounce to 2.9% on Wednesday purely from the Ofgem cap; if pay is still cooling toward 4%, the Bank can look through that bounce. A re-acceleration in regular pay would hand the three hawkish dissenters their case into the next MPC.
events.ifHigher: Regular pay above 3.6% or unemployment down to 4.6%: labour still tight. GBP bids, gilt yields up, Wednesday CPI bar rises.
events.ifLower: Regular pay at or below 3.1% or unemployment at 5.1%+: slack building. GBP sold, BoE hold locked, risk-on in UK equities.

events.whatItIs: The ZEW Institute's monthly survey of analysts and institutional investors on six-month economic expectations for Germany and the euro area, plus Germany's current-conditions index.
events.whyItMatters: ZEW is a sentiment read, not hard data, but it is the first euro-area mood check of the week ahead of Friday's flash PMIs. Consensus looks for a further rise toward 30 in Germany after July's 26.3. Current conditions are still deeply negative near -78, so a hop in expectations without any repair in current conditions is a 'hope, not activity' signal.
events.ifHigher: Germany above 35: analysts turning constructively bullish. EUR firms, European cyclicals bid into Friday PMIs.
events.ifLower: Germany below 20: the summer bounce fading. EUR softens, Friday PMI bar is lowered.

events.forecast: EPS ~$4.71-$4.73; revenue ~$47B; US comps the swing line
events.whatItIs: The world's largest home-improvement retailer's fiscal second-quarter results, covering the peak spring-and-summer selling season, with the call at 13:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the first of four consumer-bellwether prints after Friday's 0.6% retail-sales drop. Home Depot's comparable-sales line is the cleanest read on whether households are still spending on big-ticket housing projects or have pulled back as mortgage rates stay restrictive. A comps miss would confirm the retail-sales warning; a beat would argue Friday was a World Cup hangover rather than a consumer break.
events.ifHigher: Comps beat with guidance held: the consumer is intact. HD and the discretionary complex rally, Friday's sales miss is faded.
events.ifLower: Comps miss or full-year guide cut: big-ticket demand is cracking. HD, LOW, and housing-linked names sold; growth-scare tone into Walmart Thursday.

events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau and HUD monthly count of new residential construction starts and building permits, expressed as a seasonally adjusted annual rate.
events.whyItMatters: June starts jumped 19% to 1.427 million, far above the 1.31 million consensus. July is expected to give most of that back toward 1.34 million. Combined with Home Depot's print the same morning, this is the housing-demand double-header that tells you whether June was a weather-and-catch-up spike or a genuine turning point.
events.ifHigher: Starts holding above 1.40M: June was real. Homebuilders bid, rates-sensitive cyclicals firm, USD modestly supported.
events.ifLower: Starts below 1.25M: June was a one-month spike. Homebuilders sold, growth-scare tone, gold bid at the margin.

events.whatItIs: The Federal Reserve's monthly G.17 report on output across factories, mines, and utilities, plus the share of installed capacity in use.
