events.whyItMatters: A quiet but useful cross-check on Monday's Empire State print and Friday's manufacturing PMI. Capacity utilization near 76% is well below the zone that usually generates goods inflation, which is why a soft IP number would reinforce last week's disinflation narrative rather than scare anyone on growth.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.6% with utilization over 77%: factory momentum rebuilding. Modest USD and cyclicals bid.
events.ifLower: Negative MoM: factory output stalling. Soft-landing-to-slowdown tone; Friday PMI expectations trimmed.

events.event: UK CPI (July 2026) -- headline and core, YoY
events.whatItIs: The ONS Consumer Prices Index for July, the Bank of England's primary inflation target series, covering the official basket of goods and services.
events.whyItMatters: Headline is expected to bounce from 2.6% to 2.9% solely because of the latest Ofgem energy-price-cap adjustment, not because underlying inflation re-accelerated. Core is actually expected to ease a tenth to 2.5%. The split is the trade: a headline bounce with a cooler core is the hold-and-look-through outcome; a core upside surprise on top of the known utility jump is the hawkish one, especially if Tuesday's wages also firmed.
events.ifHigher: Headline at 3.1%+ or core at 2.7%+: second-round effects arriving. GBP spikes, gilt yields jump, BoE hike talk returns.
events.ifLower: Headline at or below 2.7% with core at 2.4% or under: the Ofgem bounce failed to land. GBP sold, BoE hold cemented, UK duration bid.

events.previous: Flash 2.9% YoY headline / 2.5% YoY core (July 2026); June final 2.8%
events.whatItIs: Eurostat's final Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices for July, confirming or revising the 31 July flash estimate.
events.whyItMatters: The flash already printed 2.9% headline and 2.5% core, both a tenth above June, driven by energy at +10% YoY. Finals rarely move markets unless they revise, but a core revision higher would sit poorly next to UK CPI the same morning and Friday's PMI price gauges.
events.ifHigher: Revised to 3.0%+ or core to 2.7%+: euro-area disinflation stalling. EUR bids, Friday PMI inflation components get a higher bar.
events.ifLower: Revised down to 2.8% or core to 2.4%: flash overstated the bounce. EUR softens slightly, ECB hold even more locked.

events.forecast: EPS ~$2.24-$2.32; discretionary vs. consumables mix is the tell
events.whatItIs: Target's fiscal second-quarter results, the mid-tier discretionary-retail read that sits between Home Depot's housing consumer and Walmart's value consumer.
events.whyItMatters: Target is the most cyclical of this week's four retailers. When households trade down, Target feels it first in apparel, home, and beauty. After Friday's control-group sales drop of 0.4%, a comps miss here would confirm the consumer is pulling back on anything that is not a staple, and would put extra weight on Walmart's print Thursday.
events.ifHigher: Comps beat with mix holding: the consumer is trading down, not dropping out. TGT rallies, discretionary complex stabilizes.
events.ifLower: Comps miss or guide cut: discretionary demand is breaking. TGT and the consumer-discretionary sector sold; Walmart becomes the last line of defence.

events.whatItIs: Lowe's fiscal second-quarter results and 13:00 UTC conference call, the number-two US home-improvement retailer reporting one day after Home Depot.
events.whyItMatters: Lowe's confirms or contradicts whatever Home Depot said Tuesday. A split -- HD beat, LOW miss, or the reverse -- would say the housing consumer is uneven rather than broken. A double miss would be the clean growth-scare signal into the FOMC minutes that afternoon.
events.ifHigher: Beat with guidance held: home-improvement demand is broad, not HD-specific. Housing-linked names bid.
events.ifLower: Miss or guide cut: the HD print was the exception. Homebuilders and housing retail sold into the minutes.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending August 14)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly count of commercial crude oil held in US storage, plus gasoline and distillate stocks.
events.whyItMatters: Last week's +17.4 million-barrel build was the largest since January 2023 and landed against a -1.7 million forecast, a massive miss that should have crushed crude and instead got looked through as WTI held near $82. Another outsized build would be harder to ignore, especially with gasoline already doing the disinflation work in last week's CPI and PPI.
events.ifHigher: Another multi-million-barrel build: demand is soft or supply is overflowing. Crude sold, energy drag on inflation extends, USD mixed.
events.ifLower: A draw of 3M+ barrels: last week was the outlier. Crude rallies, the energy disinflation tailwind starts to reverse.

events.event: FOMC Minutes (July 28-29 meeting) -- the three hawkish dissents in detail
events.whatItIs: The Federal Reserve's detailed record of the July 28-29 FOMC meeting, released three weeks after the decision at 18:00 UTC, covering the internal debate behind the 9-3 hold at 3.50-3.75%.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's fulcrum. Hammack, Kashkari, and Logan voted for an immediate 25bp hike -- the first three-way hawkish dissent since 2016 -- and Warsh gave no forward guidance. The minutes will show whether those three had broader sympathy or were isolated. The catch is staleness: July CPI, PPI, payrolls, and retail sales have all printed since the meeting, and all of them lean against a September hike. Markets may look through a hawkish recap toward Jackson Hole next week.
events.ifHigher: Minutes show the hike case had wide sympathy beyond the three dissenters: September hike odds reprice above 50%. USD spikes, gold and BTC sold, front-end yields jump.
events.ifLower: Minutes show the dissenters were isolated and the center wanted patience: hike odds collapse further. Gold and risk assets bid, USD sold, Jackson Hole bar for a hawkish Warsh speech rises.

events.whatItIs: The People's Bank of China's monthly setting of the one-year and five-year Loan Prime Rates, the benchmark references for most new bank lending and mortgages.
events.whyItMatters: A 15th consecutive hold is fully priced. Monday's activity data is the live input: if industrial production, retail, and FAI all missed, a surprise 10bp cut would be the easing signal markets have been waiting for. A hold after weak data would confirm Beijing prefers targeted liquidity over another broad cut that would squeeze bank margins.
events.ifHigher: Surprise hike (extremely unlikely): CNY spikes, commodities sold, global tightening impulse.
events.ifLower: 10bp cut in either tenor: CNY softens, copper and iron ore bid, AUD catches a China-stimulus bounce.

events.whatItIs: The Australian Bureau of Statistics monthly Labour Force Survey, covering employment change, the unemployment rate, and the participation rate.
events.whyItMatters: The RBA held at 4.35% last week in a unanimous decision and said it did not even discuss a cut -- only hold versus hike. June's +76.3K was a blowout; July is expected to cool toward +20K with unemployment steady at 4.4%. A second strong month would put an October hike in play. A rise in unemployment to 4.6%+ would be the first real crack in the RBA's hawkish stance.
events.ifHigher: Jobs above +40K with unemployment at 4.3% or below: labour still too tight. AUD bids, RBA October hike odds firm.
events.ifLower: Jobs negative or unemployment at 4.6%+: slack arriving. AUD sold, RBA hike talk fades, gold mildly bid via the rates channel.

events.event: KAITO Token Unlock (~$13M / ~13.5% of market cap)
events.whatItIs: A scheduled cliff unlock of Kaito (KAITO) tokens equal to roughly 13.5% of circulating market cap, one of the week's largest single-name supply events.
events.whyItMatters: A double-digit-percent-of-float unlock is large enough to pressure the name on its own and, if it hits a thin-liquidity session, can leak into broader altcoin risk appetite. It lands the same morning as Walmart and jobless claims, so any crypto-wide de-risking will be hard to separate from the macro tape.
events.ifHigher: Unlock absorbed with KAITO holding: supply was already priced. Mild constructive signal for mid-cap alts.
events.ifLower: KAITO breaks on the unlock and pulls beta: supply overhang hits a weak tape. Altcoin risk-off, BTC relatively resilient.

events.forecast: EPS ~$0.74; same-store sales and grocery traffic are the tells
events.whatItIs: Walmart's fiscal second-quarter results, released at 06:00 Central with the call at 07:00 Central -- the last and most important consumer-bellwether print of the week.
events.whyItMatters: Walmart is where households go when they trade down. After Friday's 0.6% retail-sales drop and whatever Home Depot and Target just reported, Walmart's traffic and grocery-share comments are the cleanest read on whether the US consumer is bending or breaking. Guidance is the market-mover: a cut would confirm the growth scare into Friday's PMIs; a raise would fade the retail-sales miss.
events.ifHigher: Beat with guidance raised: the value consumer is healthy. WMT rallies, staples and discretionary both bid, Friday's sales miss is treated as noise.
events.ifLower: Miss or guidance cut: even the trade-down destination is weakening. Consumer complex sold, growth-scare tone into flash PMIs, gold bid.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of new filings for unemployment insurance -- the highest-frequency read on layoffs available.
events.whyItMatters: Claims have stayed historically low even after July payrolls printed -23K, which is the combination that says hiring freeze, not layoff wave. A break above 230K would start to look like the payrolls drop was the start of something; another sub-210K print keeps the September FOMC decision live and the hawkish dissenters in the argument.
events.ifHigher: Above 240K: layoffs broadening, the hike debate ends. Gold rallies, USD sold, Friday PMIs become a growth read.
events.ifLower: Back below 200K: no layoff cycle. USD firms, hawkish minutes language gets more traction.

events.whatItIs: The Statistics Bureau's national Consumer Price Index for July, covering headline, the BoJ's preferred ex-fresh-food core, and the ex-fresh-food-and-energy core-core series.
events.whyItMatters: This is the last hard inflation print before a possible September BoJ hike. Newsquawk's preview has core accelerating to 1.8% on energy and Tokyo's recent firmness. Combined with Monday's GDP, a hotter core would all but lock a September move; a miss would give Governor Ueda cover to wait for the October Outlook Report.
events.ifHigher: Core at 2.0%+ or headline above 2.0%: September hike fully priced. JPY spikes, USD/JPY sold, global carry tightens.
events.ifLower: Core stuck at 1.6% or below: hike delayed to October or later. JPY sold, USD/JPY extends, risk appetite firms at the margin.

events.whatItIs: The ONS monthly estimate of the volume of goods sold by Great Britain retailers, including and excluding auto fuel.
events.whyItMatters: The BRC monitor already cooled more than expected in July, blaming the heatwave even as the World Cup tail faded. Official sales are unlikely to repeat June's strength. For the BoE this is an activity input, not an inflation one: a soft print after Wednesday's expected CPI bounce is the hold-friendly mix; a hot print with hot CPI is the squeeze.
events.ifHigher: Firm MoM rebound: UK consumer still spending into a CPI bounce. GBP bids, UK equities mixed (growth good, rates bad).
events.ifLower: Negative MoM: heatwave plus squeezed real incomes. GBP softens, BoE hold even more locked.

events.event: S&P Global Flash PMIs (August 2026) -- Germany and eurozone
events.previous: Germany mfg 52.2 / services 49.8 / composite 51.3; eurozone mfg 51.9 / services 51.6 / composite 51.9 (July 2026)
events.forecast: Eurozone manufacturing ~52.0; services and composite near 52
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary August purchasing-managers surveys for Germany (07:30 UTC) and the euro area (08:00 UTC), covering manufacturing, services, and the composite.
events.whyItMatters: These are the first hard-activity reads of Q3 for the bloc and the last before Jackson Hole. Manufacturing is expected to edge up to 52.0. The market-sensitive pieces are the price gauges and the German services line, which is still below 50. A services reclaim of 50 with cooler prices is the goldilocks euro print; a drop back below 50 with hotter prices is the stagflation one.
events.ifHigher: Composites above 53 with cooler prices: euro-area recovery broadening. EUR and European cyclicals bid.
events.ifLower: Composites back below 50 or prices re-accelerating: recovery stalling or inflation returning. EUR mixed-to-soft, defensive rotation in European equities.

events.event: Deribit BTC + ETH Weekly Options Expiry
events.whatItIs: Deribit's weekly settlement of Bitcoin and Ether options contracts, the largest crypto options venue by open interest.
events.whyItMatters: Expiry lands five and a half hours before the US flash PMIs, so dealer hedging into settlement can amplify whatever the European PMI complex just did. With BTC having reclaimed the mid-$60Ks on last week's inflation relief, the max-pain level decides whether market makers are selling into strength or buying dips through the London-to-New-York handoff.
events.ifHigher: BTC settling well above max pain: call holders paid, dealers buy to hedge, momentum extends into the US PMI print.
events.ifLower: BTC settling below max pain: puts in the money, hedging flows add downside pressure into the US session.

events.forecast: Composite near 52; watch the prices-charged component
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary August survey of UK manufacturers and services firms, released 30 minutes after the eurozone flash.
events.whyItMatters: July's rebound was welcome but still sluggish, and the heatwave may have weighed on August services. For the BoE the price components matter more than the headline after Wednesday's CPI: another cooling in charges would support the hold; a reversal would keep the hawkish dissenters live.
events.ifHigher: Composite above 53 with cooler prices: activity and disinflation together. GBP and UK equities both bid.
events.ifLower: Composite below 50 or prices re-accelerating: stagflationary mix. GBP mixed, UK duration sold if prices are the miss.

events.event: S&P Global US Flash PMIs (August 2026) -- manufacturing, services, composite
events.forecast: Composite near 54; services the swing factor
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary August read on US private-sector activity, covering factories and services, released at 13:45 UTC -- the last major US data point before Jackson Hole.
events.whyItMatters: July's 54.5 composite was an eight-month high and the services side is what has let Warsh argue the economy can absorb current rates. A slip toward 52 after last week's -23K payrolls and -0.6% retail sales would be the third growth scare in eight days and would all but kill a September hike before the minutes even finish being digested. A hold above 54 with hotter prices would hand the dissenters their activity-plus-inflation case going into Warsh's Friday-week speech.
events.ifHigher: Composite above 55 with rising prices: demand and inflation both firm. USD bids, gold sold, September hike odds rebuild into Jackson Hole.
events.ifLower: Composite at 52 or below: the consumer and the factory floor are both cooling. Gold and duration bid, USD sold, Warsh's Jackson Hole bar for sounding hawkish gets much higher.

2026-08-24.summary: Core PCE, Nvidia earnings, and Warsh's first Jackson Hole speech headline the week.

events.whatItIs: Remarks from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, the administration's lead voice on sanctions, buybacks, and the dollar, scheduled for 18:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Bessent's shop just doubled long-end liquidity-support buybacks, crushing more than $1 billion of crypto shorts last week and knocking the 30-year yield off a 19-year high. Any colour on Iran sanctions, the $40 trillion debt, or further buybacks lands into a quiet Monday and sets the rates tone before Tuesday's consumer-confidence print.
events.ifHigher: Hawkish on sanctions or more aggressive buyback talk: USD and duration both move; gold and BTC catch the liquidity bid.
events.ifLower: A nothing-burger or a retreat from last week's buyback stance: the squeeze fades, yields back up, risk tone cools into Tuesday.

events.whatItIs: The Reserve Bank of Australia's published minutes of the August policy meeting, released at 01:30 UTC, two weeks after the Board left the cash rate at 4.35%.
events.whyItMatters: June monthly CPI cooled to 3.8% and took an August hike off the table; Wednesday's July CPI is the next live print. The minutes will show how close the Board was to tightening on the energy-driven inflation spike, and whether the hold is a pause or a peak, into a week when US core PCE and Warsh's Jackson Hole speech will drag the entire dollar bloc.
events.ifHigher: Minutes show a live hike bias into September: AUD bids, front-end Aussie yields up, Wednesday CPI bar rises.
events.ifLower: Minutes show a comfortable hold with easing discussed: AUD sold, rate-sensitive Aussie equities bid into the CPI.

events.event: Germany Q2 GDP (final) -- QoQ and YoY
events.whatItIs: Destatis's final estimate of second-quarter German real GDP, including the expenditure breakdown of consumption, investment, and net exports, released at 06:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The flash already printed +0.2%, so revisions and the composition are the story. Germany is the euro area's growth engine and a miss on consumption or a deeper investment drop would undercut Friday's Spanish and French inflation flashes and the ECB accounts on Thursday. Ifo follows two hours later as the sentiment cross-check.
events.ifHigher: Revised to +0.4% or better with firm consumption: EUR bids, European cyclicals supported into Ifo.
events.ifLower: Revised to flat or negative: German growth scare. EUR sold, Bunds bid, Ifo bar is lowered.

events.whatItIs: The ifo Institute's monthly survey of roughly 9,000 German firms, combining current conditions and six-month expectations into a single climate index.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's first real-time read on German activity after Friday's euro-area flash PMIs and two hours after the GDP final. Consensus looks for a modest hop toward 87.3. Current conditions have been the weak leg; a rise in expectations without any repair in current conditions is hope, not activity, into Thursday's ECB accounts.
events.ifHigher: Above 88: German mood turning. EUR firms, European cyclicals bid into Jackson Hole.
events.ifLower: Below 86: the summer bounce fading. EUR softens, Bunds bid, ECB-accounts bar for any hawkish residual falls.

events.event: S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller Home Price Index (June 2026)
events.whatItIs: The S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller 20-city home-price index plus the FHFA House Price Index, both measuring US residential prices for June, released at 13:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Housing is the rates-sensitive sector that last week's starts miss (1.2M vs 1.3M) already flagged. A further slowdown in year-on-year prices would confirm that 4.70% 10-year yields are biting, and it sets up 14:00 UTC new-home sales. A re-acceleration would argue last week's starts drop was noise.
events.ifHigher: YoY above 2.2% or a firm MoM gain: housing not rolling over. Homebuilders bid, USD modestly supported.
events.ifLower: YoY below 1.3% or a MoM decline: prices catching down to rates. Homebuilders sold, gold catches a mild growth-scare bid.

events.whatItIs: The Conference Board's monthly survey of 5,000 US households on current conditions and six-month expectations, released at 14:00 UTC alongside new-home sales.
events.whyItMatters: This is the first national consumer-mood print after last week's 0.6% retail-sales drop and a Walmart guide that disappointed. Confidence has been stuck in the low 90s, well below the 100-plus zone that usually accompanies a healthy consumer. The labour-differential (jobs plentiful minus jobs hard to get) is the line that feeds Wednesday's personal-spending print and Friday's Warsh speech: a break lower would confirm the consumer is cracking; a hold would argue Friday's sales miss was a World Cup hangover.
events.ifHigher: Above 93 with a firmer labour differential: the consumer is intact. Discretionary stocks and USD bid, Wednesday spending bar rises.
events.ifLower: Below 87 or a sharp drop in the labour differential: households retrenching. Defensives bid, USD sold, gold catches the growth-scare bid into PCE.

events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's monthly count of newly built single-family homes sold, expressed as a seasonally adjusted annual rate, released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Last week's starts miss already showed builders pulling back. New-home sales are the demand side of that picture and the cleanest read on whether 6.8% mortgage rates are freezing the entry-level buyer. Combined with Case-Shiller an hour earlier and consumer confidence at the same stamp, this is Tuesday's housing-and-household triple.
events.ifHigher: Above 650K: demand absorbing high mortgage rates. Homebuilders bid, rates-sensitive cyclicals firm.
events.ifLower: Below 580K: the buyer has left. Homebuilders sold, growth-scare tone into Wednesday PCE.

events.whatItIs: The tax-and-accounting software company's fiscal fourth-quarter results, covering the tail of tax season and TurboTax Live, with the call after the close.
events.whyItMatters: Intuit is Tuesday's only large-cap software print and a read on whether households and small businesses are still paying up for software after last week's retail-sales miss. Guidance for fiscal 2027, not the beat, is the mover: a cut would confirm the consumer is trading down; a raise would argue the software wallet is intact into Wednesday's Nvidia and Salesforce double-header.
events.ifHigher: EPS beat with FY2027 guide raised: software demand intact. INTU and the application-software complex rally.
events.ifLower: Miss or guide cut: small-business and household software spending is cracking. INTU sold; Wednesday's Salesforce bar rises.

events.event: Australia CPI (July 2026) -- monthly headline and trimmed mean
events.previous: -0.1% MoM / +3.8% YoY headline; trimmed mean +3.6% YoY (June 2026)
events.forecast: ~+0.7% MoM / +3.2% YoY headline; trimmed mean ~3.5% YoY
events.whatItIs: The Australian Bureau of Statistics monthly Consumer Price Index, including the RBA's preferred trimmed-mean core, released at 01:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The RBA is on hold at 4.35% after June CPI cooled to 3.8% from 4.0% and took an August hike off the table. Consensus looks for a further slide to about 3.2% year-on-year, which would lock the hold into September. A hot trimmed mean would reopen the hike debate just as US core PCE prints 11 hours later and would drag the Aussie and the entire commodity bloc into Jackson Hole.
events.ifHigher: Headline above 3.5% or trimmed mean holding at 3.6%+: RBA hike odds rebuild. AUD bids, gold sold at the margin, US PCE bar for a hawkish reaction rises.
events.ifLower: Headline at or below 3.0% with trimmed mean under 3.4%: hold locked, easing talk returns. AUD sold, rate-sensitive Aussie equities bid.

events.event: Core PCE Price Index (July 2026) + Personal Income and Spending
events.previous: Core +0.1% MoM / +3.3% YoY; headline -0.1% MoM / +3.7% YoY (June 2026); income +0.2%, spending +0.3% MoM
events.forecast: Core +0.2% MoM / +3.3% YoY; headline +0.1% MoM / +3.6% YoY; income +0.2%; spending +0.1%
events.whatItIs: The BEA's Personal Income and Outlays report containing the PCE price index, the inflation measure the Fed formally targets, alongside monthly household income and consumption. Released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the last official US inflation print before Warsh's Friday keynote and the September 15-16 FOMC. Core is expected to hold at 3.3% year-on-year, still 130 basis points above target, with the monthly rate firming from +0.1% to +0.2%. The July minutes already showed 'many' participants ready to hike if inflation does not decline. A 0.3% or hotter core print hands them their case two days before Jackson Hole; a 0.1% or softer print lets Warsh sound patient. Personal spending, seen slowing to +0.1% after last week's 0.6% retail-sales drop, is the growth half of the same release.
events.ifHigher: Core above +0.3% MoM or the annual rate ticking up: disinflation stalled. USD spikes, gold sold, September hike odds jump into Jackson Hole.
events.ifLower: Core at or below +0.1% MoM: the annual rate starts rolling over. Gold and equities bid, USD sold, Warsh's bar for sounding hawkish on Friday gets much higher.

events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's second estimate of second-quarter real GDP, incorporating more complete source data than last month's advance, released at 12:30 UTC in the same window as PCE.
events.whyItMatters: The advance already showed the economy slowing to 1.5% from 2.1% in Q1. Second estimates rarely rewrite the headline, so the composition -- consumer spending, inventories, net exports, and the GDP price index at a very hot 6.2% -- is the story. A downward revision combined with soft personal spending in the same release would confirm the slowdown into Jackson Hole; an upward revision with a still-hot deflator would hand the July dissenters their growth-plus-inflation case.
events.ifHigher: Revised to 2.0%+ with a firm consumer: growth resilient under 3.50-3.75% policy. USD bids, cyclicals supported, hike odds firm.
events.ifLower: Revised to 1.0% or below: the slowdown is real. Gold and duration bid, USD sold, Warsh's bar for a hawkish keynote rises.

events.event: Durable Goods Orders (July 2026) -- headline and core
events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's monthly advance report on manufacturers' orders for goods expected to last at least three years, including the core capital-goods series that proxies business equipment investment.
events.whyItMatters: A quiet third print in the morning release, but core capital goods are the capex tell that Nvidia's data-center customers will be asked about after the close. A miss would argue businesses are pausing equipment orders into tighter financial conditions; a beat would support the AI-capex narrative the chip complex needs.
events.ifHigher: Core above +1.0%: capex still expanding. Cyclicals and semis bid into the Nvidia print.
events.ifLower: Core negative: businesses pulling back. Industrials sold, a mild growth-scare overlay on the PCE reaction.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending August 21)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly count of commercial crude-oil stocks held at US refineries, tank farms, and pipelines, released at 14:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Crude built 4.4 million barrels last week after a 17.4 million-barrel blowout the week before, yet WTI held near $85.70 because distillates drew 1.5 million and Hormuz risk never left the tape. A third straight large build would argue the physical market is loosening just as core PCE lands; a surprise draw would re-tighten the energy impulse Warsh has to look through on Friday.
events.ifHigher: Build above 5M: physical market loosening. WTI sold, a mild disinflation assist into Jackson Hole.
events.ifLower: Draw, or a build under 1M with another distillate drop: tightness persists. WTI bids, headline PCE path stays elevated.

events.whatItIs: The AI chip designer's fiscal second-quarter results, covering May-July, with the conference call at 21:00 UTC. Data-center revenue, gross margin, and Q3 guidance are the three lines that move the entire semiconductor complex.
events.whyItMatters: Nvidia is the single largest index-level earnings of the week and the AI-capex tell after a summer in which megacap cloud spend has been the only growth story that has held. Wall Street is looking for about $91.8 billion of revenue, nearly double the year-ago quarter, and 75% gross margins. Guidance is the mover: a raise would rescue a stalled-out tape into Jackson Hole; a China-or-margin warning would hit the entire AI complex two sessions before Warsh speaks.
events.ifHigher: Revenue beat with Q3 guide above $95B and margins holding ~75%: AI capex intact. NVDA, semis, and the Nasdaq squeeze; BTC catches the risk bid.
events.ifLower: Guide cut, China commentary, or gross margin under 73%: AI-spend pause. NVDA and the mega-cap complex sold; Friday's Warsh speech inherits a risk-off tape.

events.whatItIs: The enterprise-software company's fiscal second-quarter results, with current remaining performance obligation (cRPO) growth and Agentforce AI attach the lines that set the software complex.
events.whyItMatters: Salesforce is the largest non-chip software print of the week and reports in the same after-close window as Nvidia and CrowdStrike. The question is whether generative-AI agents are converting into paid seats or just demo-ware. A cRPO acceleration would support the software multiple into Jackson Hole; a deceleration would extend the multiple compression that has already hit the group this year.
events.ifHigher: cRPO beat with AI-attach commentary and guide raised: software complex rallies with NVDA.
events.ifLower: cRPO miss or FY guide cut: software sold, a second risk-off leg after any NVDA disappointment.

events.whatItIs: GfK's monthly survey of German household income, spending, and economic expectations, released at 06:00 UTC as a leading read on the next month.
events.whyItMatters: German households have been stuck near -30 for months, a deeply pessimistic reading that matches the ifo current-conditions slump. A further drop would stack a consumer-scare on top of Tuesday's GDP/ifo pair into Thursday's ECB accounts; a hop toward -27 would be the first real repair.
events.ifHigher: Above -27: German consumer thawing. EUR and European retail bid.
events.ifLower: Below -32: households digging in. EUR sold, ECB-accounts bar for any hawkish residual falls.

events.whatItIs: The European Central Bank's published accounts of the July Governing Council meeting, the euro-area equivalent of FOMC minutes, released at 11:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The ECB is on hold at 2.40% and has been the more patient of the two Atlantic central banks. The accounts will show whether the energy shock and Spanish inflation (flash CPI Friday, seen jumping to 4.2%) have created a hawkish minority, and they land on day one of Jackson Hole, so any surprise hawkish colour would travel into Warsh's speech. A comfortable hold would leave the euro as the funding currency into Friday.
events.ifHigher: Accounts show a live hike discussion: EUR bids, Bunds sold, a hawkish overlay on Jackson Hole day one.
events.ifLower: Accounts show a unified hold with easing optionality: EUR sold, European duration bid.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of new unemployment insurance filings, the highest-frequency read available on the labour market, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Claims have been stuck in the mid-200Ks even as July payrolls printed -23K, a split that the Friday CES benchmark revision is supposed to resolve. A break above 230K on Jackson Hole day one would be the first real labour crack Warsh has to address; another 206K print would let him treat July's payroll drop as a one-month artefact.
events.ifHigher: Above 230K: labour market loosening. Gold and duration bid, USD sold, Friday's benchmark revision becomes the confirmation print.
events.ifLower: Below 200K: no cracks. USD firms, the -23K payrolls print looks like noise into Warsh.

events.event: Jackson Hole Economic Symposium opens (runs August 27-29)
events.whatItIs: The Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's annual symposium in Moran, Wyoming, this year themed 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy,' gathering central bankers, academics, and markets officials through Saturday.
events.whyItMatters: Jackson Hole is where Fed chairs historically reset the policy narrative. Warsh's keynote is Friday, but Thursday's panels, corridor chatter, and any other-governor remarks start moving rates from the open. The July minutes already showed 'many' participants ready to hike if inflation does not fall; two days after core PCE, the symposium is the venue where that split either hardens or gets talked down.
events.ifHigher: Hawkish corridor colour or a hot PCE hangover: USD bids, gold sold, September hike odds rebuild into the keynote.
events.ifLower: Dovish panels or a 'look through energy' framing: gold and duration bid, USD sold, Friday's bar for a hawkish Warsh speech rises.

events.event: Marvell Technology (MRVL) Q2 FY2027 Earnings (after close)
events.whatItIs: The custom-silicon and networking-chip company's fiscal second-quarter results, with data-center custom ASICs for hyperscalers the line that maps onto Wednesday's Nvidia print.
events.whyItMatters: Marvell is the first major confirmation (or contradiction) of Nvidia's AI-capex message. Custom ASICs are the second-source story: if hyperscalers are still paying Marvell to design accelerators alongside Nvidia, the AI build-out is broad. A miss the night after an Nvidia disappointment would be a double-down selloff into Warsh; a beat after an Nvidia raise would extend the squeeze.
events.ifHigher: Revenue beat with a raised data-center guide: custom-AI demand confirmed. MRVL, AVGO, and the semiconductor complex bid.
events.ifLower: Data-center miss or guide cut: customers consolidating spend. MRVL sold, a second leg down in semis into Friday.

events.event: Tokyo Core CPI (August 2026) + Japan Unemployment Rate (July)
events.whatItIs: The Statistics Bureau's Tokyo-area core CPI (excluding fresh food), the leading read on the national print, plus the July unemployment rate, both released at 23:30 UTC Thursday.
events.whyItMatters: Tokyo core has been drifting toward 1.8-1.9%, under the BoJ's 2% comfort zone, even as money markets still price a decent chance of a September hike after last week's Q2 GDP. A further slide would take September off the table; a rebound combined with unemployment holding at 2.5% would keep the hike live into Warsh's speech a few hours later.
events.ifHigher: Tokyo core at 2.0%+ or unemployment at 2.3%: BoJ September hike odds jump. JPY bids, USD/JPY sold.
events.ifLower: Tokyo core at 1.6% or below: hike delayed. JPY sold, USD/JPY extends.

events.whatItIs: Spain's preliminary August Consumer Price Index, the first euro-area national flash of the month, released at 07:00 UTC, with France's prelim CPI in the same early window.
events.whyItMatters: Consensus is a sharp jump to 4.2% from 3.6%, which would be the hottest Spanish reading in months and a live input for the ECB after Thursday's accounts. Energy and the VAT/tax base are the usual culprits; the core line is the one that would force the Council to revisit its hold. It lands three hours before Warsh, so a hot print would be on every Jackson Hole briefing note.
events.ifHigher: Above 4.5% or a hot core: euro-area inflation re-accelerating. EUR mixed (rates up, growth scare), Bunds sold.
events.ifLower: At or below 3.6%: the jump was over-forecast. EUR softer, Bunds bid, Warsh inherits a cooler global inflation tape.

events.forecast: +0.2% MoM; Q2 details watched vs the advance
events.whatItIs: Statistics Canada's monthly GDP by industry for June plus the second-quarter national accounts, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Canada is the other North American growth print on Jackson Hole morning, and the BoC is on hold with markets still pricing a modest chance of a hike by year-end after this month's CPI bounce. A soft June would stack a Canadian growth scare on top of last week's US retail miss; a firm print would keep the oil-linked CAD bid into Warsh.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.4% MoM: Canadian growth holding. CAD bids, oil-linked FX supported.
events.ifLower: Flat or negative: growth scare. CAD sold, a mild risk-off overlay on the Warsh tape.

events.whatItIs: The ISM-Chicago Business Barometer, a diffusion index of Chicago-area manufacturing and services activity, released at 13:45 UTC, 15 minutes before Warsh speaks.
events.whyItMatters: Chicago PMI has been running hot in the high 50s, well above the national flash manufacturing PMI of 53.2. It is not a national print, but it is the last activity number before the keynote. A drop toward 52 would put a growth-scare number on the screen as Warsh walks on stage; a hold above 57 would let him point to resilient activity.
events.ifHigher: Above 60: Midwest activity booming. Modest USD and cyclicals bid into the speech.
events.ifLower: Below 54: regional activity rolling over. Soft-landing-to-slowdown tone as Warsh starts talking.

events.event: Fed Chair Warsh Jackson Hole keynote -- first symposium speech as Chair
events.whatItIs: Chair Kevin Warsh's keynote remarks at the 2026 Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium in Moran, Wyoming, at 14:00 UTC, streamed by the Kansas City Fed. The symposium theme is financial innovation, payments, and policy.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's fulcrum and Warsh's first Jackson Hole as Chair, 18 days before the September 15-16 FOMC. He left the funds rate at 3.50-3.75% on a 9-3 vote in July, offered no forward guidance, and told reporters the speech was still a blank page pending his five policy task forces. The July minutes showed 'many' participants ready to hike if inflation does not decline. Wednesday's core PCE is the last number that can still change what he says. A hawkish reset would reprice September; a 'look through energy, watch the labour market' frame would lock the hold.
events.ifHigher: Hawkish: inflation still too high, hike live in September, or a higher-for-longer frame. USD spikes, gold and BTC sold, yields up, stocks wobble.
events.ifLower: Patient: look through energy, labour cooling, no rush to hike. Gold and duration rally, USD sold, risk assets bid into the weekend.

events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' preliminary estimate of the annual benchmark revision to the level of nonfarm payrolls as of March 2026, released at 14:00 UTC. It measures how much the monthly CES survey has over- or under-counted jobs over the prior year.
events.whyItMatters: Last year's prelim was -911K, a historically large downward revision that rewrote the labour-market narrative more than any monthly print. This year's number lands at the same stamp as Warsh's keynote, after July payrolls already printed -23K. A second large negative revision would confirm the monthly survey has been too optimistic and would collapse September hike odds in real time as Warsh is speaking; a small or positive revision would argue July was a one-month drop in a still-solid labour market.
events.ifHigher: Small revision (under 200K in either direction) or a positive one: monthly payrolls were broadly right. Hawkish case intact, USD supported as Warsh speaks.
events.ifLower: Downward revision of 500K+: the labour market is much weaker than the monthly prints showed. Gold and duration spike, USD sold, hike odds collapse.

events.event: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (August 2026 final)
events.whatItIs: The final August reading of the University of Michigan Survey of Consumers, including the 1-year and 5-year inflation-expectations series, released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The preliminary already slumped to 51.0 from July's 55.2, a weak print that matched last week's retail-sales miss. Final revisions are usually a point or two, so the market-sensitive line is inflation expectations: 1-year stuck at 4.3% would keep the second-round-effects worry alive as Warsh speaks; a drop toward 4.0% would be the disinflation confirmation the minutes said 'many' participants need.
events.ifHigher: Sentiment back above 54 or 1-year expectations down to 4.0%: mood stabilizing, inflation psychology cooling. Mild risk-on overlay on the Warsh reaction.
events.ifLower: Sentiment under 49 or 1-year expectations at 4.5%+: households gloomier and unanchored. Gold bid, a hawkish constraint on whatever Warsh just said.

2026-08-31.summary: August NFP, euro-area CPI, and Broadcom headline the last week before Fed blackout.

events.event: Japan Industrial Production (July prelim) + Retail Sales (July)
events.whatItIs: METI's preliminary July industrial production plus the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry retail-sales print, released at 23:50 UTC Sunday.
events.whyItMatters: BoJ hike odds for the September 17-18 meeting have been climbing after Deputy Governor Himino's hawkish tone and board member Takata's failed 1.25% proposal in July. A production relapse with firm retail would keep the hike case alive on mixed activity; a double miss would give the doves a growth argument into Takata's Wednesday speech.
events.ifHigher: IP above flat with retail beating 3.5%: activity holding. JPY bids, USD/JPY sold, September hike odds firm.
events.ifLower: IP below -1.5% or retail under 2%: factory slump. JPY sold, carry bid returns, BoJ September bar rises.

events.whatItIs: The National Bureau of Statistics official purchasing-managers survey of large Chinese manufacturers, where 50 separates expansion from contraction, released at 01:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: July slipped back below 50 and a second contraction month is the base case after heavy summer rains. Global AI-related export demand is the offset; weak domestic orders would hit copper, iron ore, and the Aussie hours before Australia's Q2 GDP on Wednesday and keep the PBoC on a targeted-easing path rather than a broad cut.
events.ifHigher: Above 50.5: factories back in expansion. Commodities and AUD bid, CNH firms, risk tone lifts into the US open.
events.ifLower: Below 49.0: contraction deepening. Oil and copper sold, AUD and CNH weaken, China-demand scare into Tuesday's RatingDog print.

events.whatItIs: The NBS official survey of Chinese services and construction firms, released in the same 01:30 UTC window as the manufacturing PMI.
events.whyItMatters: Services and construction are the domestic-demand half of China's story. July's 49.0 was a contraction print; consensus looks for a hop back through 50. A miss would confirm that the property slump is still capping household spending and would weigh on metals and the Aussie alongside the manufacturing number.
events.ifHigher: Above 51: domestic services healing. CNH and AUD bid, industrial metals supported.
events.ifLower: Below 49: services still shrinking. China-demand scare, commodities sold, PBoC easing chatter returns.

events.event: UK Summer Bank Holiday -- London cash and sterling products closed
events.whatItIs: The late-August public holiday. UK equity, gilt, and sterling cash markets are shut; futures and FX still trade with thinner London liquidity.
events.whyItMatters: Monday's tape is an Asia-and-Europe session without a London cash close. German CPI still prints, and any sterling move on the German inflation surprise will have to wait for Tuesday's reopen to find real UK flows. Spreads in FTSE names and gilts typically gap on the Tuesday open.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- UK cash closed.
events.ifLower: N/A -- UK cash closed.

events.event: Germany CPI (August 2026 preliminary) -- MoM and YoY
events.whatItIs: Destatis's flash estimate of German consumer prices, including the harmonised HICP that feeds the euro-area flash on Tuesday, released around midday UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Germany is the first large euro-area inflation print of the week and the energy-price tell after the Middle East premium kept fuel elevated. Consensus is a 3.0% year-on-year rebound from 2.8%. A hotter number would lift Tuesday's euro-area bar and keep the ECB on a hike-watch footing into the September 10 decision; a miss would argue the July spike was energy noise.
events.ifHigher: YoY above 3.2% or MoM above 0.5%: energy leaking into German prices. EUR bids, Bunds sold, Tuesday euro-area CPI bar rises.
events.ifLower: YoY at or below 2.7%: disinflation still in train. EUR sold, Bunds bid, ECB September hold looks more comfortable.

events.whatItIs: The private S&P Global / RatingDog survey of smaller Chinese manufacturers and exporters, released at 01:45 UTC, a day after the official NBS PMI.
events.whyItMatters: This sample has been running above 50 on AI-related export demand even as the official index contracted. A drop toward 50 would say the export offset is fading; a hold above 51 would confirm the official miss (if Monday was weak) was large-SOE and weather, not the coastal engine that actually moves copper and the Aussie.
events.ifHigher: Above 52: exporters still expanding. AUD and industrial metals bid, CNH supported.
events.ifLower: Below 50: private factories joining the contraction. Commodities sold, China-demand scare confirmed.

events.whatItIs: A scheduled vesting release of Ethena (ENA) tokens worth about $22 million at recent prices, one of Tuesday's larger named unlocks.
events.whyItMatters: ENA unlocks have been a recurring supply event through 2026. This one lands into a crypto tape that just squeezed Bitcoin toward $77,000 on Treasury-buyback liquidity, so any alt-specific selling will be hard to separate from the macro bid. A clean absorb would be a constructive mid-cap tell; a break would be the first supply test of that squeeze.
events.ifHigher: Unlock absorbed with ENA holding: supply was priced. Mild constructive signal for mid-cap alts.
events.ifLower: ENA breaks and pulls beta: supply hits a thin tape. Altcoin risk-off, BTC relatively resilient.

events.event: Eurozone CPI Flash (August 2026) -- headline and core
events.whatItIs: Eurostat's flash estimate of euro-area HICP, including the core measure that excludes energy, food, alcohol, and tobacco, released at 09:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the ECB's last inflation print before the September 10 decision. Headline is expected to re-accelerate to about 3.1% on fuel; RBC has a 3.6% risk case. The signal is services and core: if core holds near 2.5-2.6% the ECB can look through energy, but a jump would reopen second-round-effects talk nine days before Lagarde speaks.
events.ifHigher: Headline above 3.3% or core at 2.8%+: energy leaking into core. EUR spikes, Bunds sold, September ECB hike chatter returns.
events.ifLower: Headline at or below 2.8% with core under 2.4%: disinflation intact. EUR sold, Bunds bid, September hold locked.

events.event: S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI (August 2026 final)
events.whatItIs: The final August reading of S&P Global's survey of US manufacturers, released 15 minutes before ISM, covering output, new orders, employment, and prices.
events.whyItMatters: The flash already printed 53.9, so revisions and the prices-paid line are the story. It is the first national factory print after Friday's Chicago PMI crash to 47.1 from 57.6. A downward revision toward 52 would confirm that regional miss; an unrevised 53.9 would argue Chicago was local noise ahead of ISM.
events.ifHigher: Revised above 55: factories still humming. Modest USD and cyclicals bid into ISM.
events.ifLower: Revised below 52: national factory demand rolling over. Cyclicals sold, ISM bar falls.

events.whatItIs: The Institute for Supply Management's monthly survey of US factory purchasing managers. A reading above 50 signals expansion. Prices paid and employment are the two sub-indices that move rates.
events.whyItMatters: ISM manufacturing has been running in the mid-50s, well above the 50 line, even as July payrolls fell 23,000. Consensus is a modest cooling to about 55. Friday's Chicago PMI collapse to 47.1 is the live risk: if ISM follows Chicago lower, the growth-scare camp gets its evidence two days before ADP and four days before NFP. Prices paid at 71.1 in July is the inflation tell Warsh flagged at Jackson Hole.
events.ifHigher: Above 56 with prices paid holding 70+: activity and factory inflation both hot. USD bids, hike odds for September firm, cyclicals mixed.
events.ifLower: Below 53 or a drop in prices paid toward 60: factories cooling and disinflating. Gold and duration bid, September hike odds fade into ADP.

events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, measuring unfilled vacancies, hires, and quits for July, released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Openings have been drifting around 7.3-7.4 million after the post-pandemic bulge. July JOLTS is the vacancies read that pairs with Friday's August payrolls. A drop below 7.0 million would confirm labour demand is cooling in line with the -23,000 July payrolls print; a rebound above 7.6 million would argue firms are still hunting for workers and would keep September hike odds alive.
events.ifHigher: Above 7.6M with quits firm: labour demand still tight. USD bids, wage-inflation channel stays open into NFP.
events.ifLower: Below 7.0M or a sharp drop in quits: firms pulling back. Gold bid, September hike odds fade, Friday's NFP bar falls.

events.event: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) FY2026 Q4 Earnings (after close)
events.whatItIs: The cybersecurity company's fiscal fourth-quarter results, covering the May-July quarter, with the call after the US close.
events.whyItMatters: PANW is Tuesday's large-cap software print and a read on whether enterprise security spend is still holding after last week's Intuit guide-down. Billings growth and FY2027 guidance are the movers, not the EPS beat. A cut would confirm IT budgets are tightening into Friday's payrolls; a raise would keep the software complex bid into Wednesday's Broadcom.
events.ifHigher: EPS beat with FY2027 billings guide raised: security spend intact. PANW and software rally.
events.ifLower: Miss or guide cut: enterprise IT pausing. PANW sold; Wednesday's Broadcom bar for a clean AI print rises.

events.event: Dell Technologies (DELL) Q2 FY2027 Earnings (after close)
events.whatItIs: Dell's fiscal second-quarter results, covering May-July, with AI-server revenue, PC demand, and current-quarter margin guidance as the three lines that move the stock.
events.whyItMatters: Dell is the hardware follow-through one week after Nvidia's beat-and-raise-and-fade. Wall Street is looking for about $45 billion of revenue and a doubling of year-ago EPS. AI-server mix and margin guidance are the tell: a fat AI print with thin margins would rhyme with last year's pattern and would hit the whole server chain into Broadcom Wednesday.
events.ifHigher: Revenue beat with AI-server guide raised and margins holding: hardware capex intact. DELL, server names, and the Nasdaq bid.
events.ifLower: AI-server miss or margin warning: the Nvidia fade was the tell. DELL and the AI-hardware complex sold into Broadcom.

events.whatItIs: The Australian Bureau of Statistics quarterly national accounts, covering consumption, business investment, and net exports, released at 01:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The RBA is on hold at 4.35% with senior officials warning that further tightening is 'quite possible.' Consensus is a stall: 0.0% quarter-on-quarter after last week's monthly CPI cooled. An upside surprise would reopen a September/November hike; a contraction would be the first real crack in the RBA's hawkish stance and would drag the Aussie into a US ADP-and-BoC afternoon.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.4% QoQ: demand still too strong. AUD bids, RBA hike odds rebuild.
events.ifLower: Negative QoQ: growth scare. AUD sold, RBA hike talk fades, gold mildly bid via the rates channel.

events.whatItIs: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand's Monetary Policy Statement, OCR decision, and Governor Adrian Orr press conference. A hike to 2.75% would be the second consecutive increase after July's first tightening in more than three years.
events.whyItMatters: Twenty-seven of 31 economists in the Reuters poll expect +25bp, and OIS prices it above 90%. The decision itself is not the event; the OCR track is. Markets want to know whether the Bank still sees 3.0% by year-end or whether weaker labour data and lower energy prices pull the peak forward. A pause would be a genuine shock given July's 'some further reduction in monetary stimulus is likely' line.
events.ifHigher: Hike to 2.75% with a year-end track at 3.25%+ or an October hike flagged: NZD spikes, front-end NZ yields jump.
events.ifLower: Hold at 2.50%, or a hike with a dovish 2.75% peak: NZD sold, the whole dollar-bloc easing bid firms into the BoC.

events.whatItIs: ADP's monthly estimate of US private-sector employment, released two days before the BLS payrolls report at 12:15 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: July ADP printed +44K and then BLS private payrolls printed +30K against a -23K headline. Consensus is a modest bounce to about +59K. A second sub-50K print would confirm the low-hire, low-fire story ING is telling and would collapse September hike odds heading into Friday; a rebound above +100K would argue July was the anomaly and would keep Warsh's Jackson Hole hike threat live.
events.ifHigher: Above +100K: private hiring re-accelerating. USD bids, Friday NFP bar rises, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Below +20K or negative: labour demand stalling. Gold and duration rally, September hike odds fade into claims Thursday.

events.whatItIs: The Bank of Canada's policy-rate announcement at 13:45 UTC, followed by Governor Tiff Macklem's press conference. No change from 2.25% is the consensus.
events.whyItMatters: The hold is fully priced. The live issue is trade: Canada has announced retaliatory tariffs after President Trump raised duties on Canadian goods, and Macklem will have to say whether that shock changes the outlook. A hawkish hold that plays down the tariff hit would support CAD; any signal that the BoC is preparing to ease into a trade war would sell the loonie into Friday's Canadian jobs print.
events.ifHigher: Surprise hike, or a hold with a clearly hawkish statement: CAD bids, USD/CAD sold.
events.ifLower: Cut, or a hold that flags trade-war easing: CAD sold, oil-linked FX weakens, mild gold bid via easier North American policy.

events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's monthly report on manufacturers' new orders, including the factory-orders follow-through on last week's durable-goods print, released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: A quiet third print on a crowded Wednesday. Core capital goods are the capex tell that Dell and Broadcom will be asked about after the close. A miss would argue businesses are pausing equipment orders into tighter financial conditions; a beat would support the AI-hardware narrative Wednesday night needs.
events.ifHigher: Headline above +1.0% with firm core capex: business investment holding. Cyclicals and semis bid into Broadcom.
events.ifLower: Headline negative with core capex rolling over: capex pause. Industrials sold, a mild growth-scare overlay on ADP.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending August 28)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly count of commercial crude-oil stocks held at US refineries, tank farms, and pipelines, released at 14:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Crude barely built 0.1 million barrels last week after two outsized builds, and gasoline and distillate remain below seasonal norms. WTI has been chopping in the low $80s as Hormuz risk faded from the August spike. A surprise draw would re-tighten the energy impulse that pushed euro-area and German CPI higher this week; another build would be the disinflation assist Warsh would want before NFP.
events.ifHigher: Build above 3M: physical market loosening. WTI sold, a mild disinflation assist into Friday payrolls.
events.ifLower: Draw of 2M+ with another gasoline drop: tightness persists. WTI bids, headline-inflation path stays elevated.

events.whatItIs: The Federal Reserve's qualitative survey of economic conditions across the 12 districts, released at 18:00 UTC, two weeks before the September 15-16 FOMC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the last official Fed colour before the communications blackout starts Saturday. Anecdotes on hiring, wages, and prices paid will be read against July's -23,000 payrolls and Warsh's Jackson Hole hike threat. 'Labour cooling, prices still sticky' is the configuration that keeps September live; 'activity rolling over' would undercut the hike camp heading into Friday's NFP.
events.ifHigher: Districts report firm hiring and sticky prices: hawkish Beige Book. USD bids, September hike odds firm.
events.ifLower: Districts report weaker labour demand and cooling prices: dovish Beige Book. Gold bid, hike odds fade into NFP.

events.forecast: EPS ~$3.22; revenue ~$29.24B; AI semiconductor revenue watched vs ~$16B guide
events.whatItIs: Broadcom's fiscal third-quarter results, covering May-July, with AI semiconductor revenue, custom-XPU backlog, and Q4 guidance as the three lines that move the $2 trillion stock.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's largest remaining earnings print and the AI-capex follow-through after Nvidia beat, guided $108 billion, and still faded. Street looks for about $29.2 billion of revenue, up 83% year-on-year, and $16 billion of AI semiconductor sales. Guidance is the mover: a raise would rescue the AI complex two sessions before NFP; a China-or-margin warning would hit the whole semiconductor tape into Friday.
events.ifHigher: AI revenue beat with Q4 guide raised: custom-silicon demand intact. AVGO, semis, and the Nasdaq squeeze; BTC catches the risk bid.
events.ifLower: AI miss, guide cut, or gross-margin warning: the Nvidia fade was the tell. AVGO and the mega-cap complex sold; Friday NFP inherits a risk-off tape.

events.whatItIs: The data-cloud company's fiscal second-quarter results, covering May-July, with product revenue growth and remaining performance obligations as the two lines that move the stock.
events.whyItMatters: Snowflake is Wednesday's software companion to Broadcom and a read on whether data-platform spend is still compounding after last week's Salesforce and CrowdStrike prints. A guide cut would confirm enterprise software is tightening; a beat with RPO acceleration would keep the software bid alive into NFP.
events.ifHigher: Revenue beat with RPO and cRPO accelerating: data-platform demand intact. SNOW and software rally.
events.ifLower: Miss or guide cut: cloud-data spend slowing. SNOW sold; risk-off overlay on the Broadcom reaction.

events.whatItIs: The private S&P Global / RatingDog survey of Chinese services firms, released at 01:45 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the last China activity print of the week and the domestic-demand tell after Monday's official PMIs and Tuesday's manufacturing RatingDog. A drop back through 50 would confirm that household spending is still the weak link; a hold above 51 would be a modest offset if the official non-manufacturing index missed.
events.ifHigher: Above 52: private services expanding. AUD and CNH supported, industrial metals catch a bid.
events.ifLower: Below 50: services contraction. China-demand scare into the US claims-and-ISM morning.

events.whatItIs: The Swiss Federal Statistical Office monthly Consumer Price Index, the SNB's primary inflation input.
events.whyItMatters: Swiss inflation is still undershooting the SNB's 0-2% range, which is why policy sits at 0%. A return toward 1% year-on-year would be the first sign that imported energy is leaking into the Swiss basket; another near-zero print keeps the SNB on hold into the September 24 decision and keeps CHF in its safe-haven role rather than a rates story.
events.ifHigher: YoY above 0.8%: inflation returning. CHF bids on hike-odds rebuild.
events.ifLower: YoY at or below 0.2% or another MoM decline: undershoot persists. CHF sold on the margin, gold mildly bid via easier Swiss policy.

events.whatItIs: Scheduled Thursday vesting releases: about $41 million of Bittensor (TAO) and $17 million of Sui (SUI) at recent prices, the week's largest named Layer-1 unlocks.
events.whyItMatters: TAO is large enough relative to its float to move the name on its own. Combined with SUI it is a supply test of last week's Bitcoin squeeze toward $77,000, landing the same morning as US claims and ISM services. A clean absorb would be constructive; a break that pulls beta would be the first real supply shock of that squeeze.
events.ifHigher: Unlocks absorbed with TAO and SUI holding: supply was priced. Mild constructive signal for L1 alts.
events.ifLower: TAO or SUI breaks and pulls beta: supply hits a thin tape. Altcoin risk-off into Friday NFP.

events.event: BoE Monetary Policy Report Hearings (Treasury Committee)
events.whatItIs: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey and MPC members testify before Parliament's Treasury Committee on the latest Monetary Policy Report and the inflation outlook.
events.whyItMatters: UK cash reopened Tuesday after the bank holiday; this is the first BoE-speak of the week and the last before the September 17 decision. Sterling will trade Bailey's tone on services inflation and the labour market. A hawkish panel that refuses to rule out a hike would lift GBP into a US claims-and-ISM morning; a dovish 'data-dependent pause' would sell the pound.
events.ifHigher: Hawkish: inflation still too high, further tightening live. GBP bids, gilts sold.
events.ifLower: Dovish: labour cooling, hold locked for September. GBP sold, gilts bid.

events.whatItIs: The Labor Department's weekly count of first-time unemployment-insurance filings, plus continuing claims, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Claims have been stuck in the low 200s even as July payrolls fell 23,000 -- the low-hire, low-fire signature. A print above 230K on the last reading before NFP would confirm labour demand is cracking; another 200-210K hold would argue Friday's bounce-or-not is a hiring story, not a firing story. Governor Waller is also listed to speak in the same window.
events.ifHigher: Above 230K: layoffs arriving. Gold and duration rally, Friday NFP bar falls, September hike odds fade.
events.ifLower: Below 190K: labour still tight. USD bids, Friday NFP bar rises, gold sold.

events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau / BEA monthly goods-and-services trade balance, covering July exports and imports, released at 12:30 UTC with claims.
events.whyItMatters: Consensus is a sharp widening to about -$91 billion from -$73 billion as imports rebound. A blowout deficit would be a GDP drag heading into the Q3 tracking estimates the FOMC will have on September 16; a narrower gap would be a modest growth assist. The dollar reaction is usually second-order to claims on this stamp.
events.ifHigher: Deficit narrower than -$80B: net exports less of a drag. Modest USD support.
events.ifLower: Deficit wider than -$100B: import surge, GDP drag. USD mixed, a mild growth-scare overlay on claims.

events.whatItIs: The Institute for Supply Management's monthly survey of US services-firm purchasing managers. Services are about 80% of US GDP. A reading above 50 signals expansion.
events.whyItMatters: Services have been the resilient half of the US economy -- flash S&P services jumped to 56.8 two weeks ago -- and this is the last activity survey before Friday's payrolls. Consensus is a modest cooling to 53.8. A drop toward 50 would confirm Friday's Chicago crash was the tell and would collapse September hike odds; a hold above 55 with hot prices paid would keep Warsh's Jackson Hole threat intact into NFP.
events.ifHigher: Above 55 with prices paid firm: services still booming. USD bids, Friday NFP bar rises, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Below 51: services joining the factory slowdown. Gold and duration rally, September hike odds fade into NFP.

events.event: Fed Hammack and Goolsbee remarks -- Connecting Communities
events.whatItIs: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee deliver remarks at the Cleveland Fed's 'Connecting Communities' online event at 19:00 UTC. Hammack dissented for a hike in July.
events.whyItMatters: This is the last named Fed-speak before the communications blackout starts Saturday. Hammack is one of the three July hike dissenters; any repeat of that call 13 days before the September 15-16 FOMC would reprice hike odds into Friday's NFP. Goolsbee has been the more patient voice. A split on stage would be the live signal.
events.ifHigher: Hammack repeats the hike call and Goolsbee joins her: hawkish last word. USD bids, gold sold into NFP.
events.ifLower: Both stress labour cooling and patience: dovish last word. Gold bid, September hike odds fade.

events.whatItIs: The athletic-apparel retailer's fiscal second-quarter results, covering May-July, with comparable-sales growth, China commentary, and full-year guidance as the three lines that move the stock.
events.whyItMatters: Lululemon is Thursday's consumer-discretionary print and a read on whether the higher-income shopper is still paying up after last week's Walmart miss and the 0.6% retail-sales drop. A guide cut would confirm the consumer is trading down heading into Friday's payrolls; a beat with comps intact would be a relief bid for discretionary retail.
events.ifHigher: Comps beat with FY guide raised: the premium consumer is intact. LULU and discretionary retail rally.
events.ifLower: Miss or guide cut: the consumer is cracking. LULU sold; a growth-scare overlay on Friday NFP.

events.whatItIs: Eurostat's monthly volume of retail trade, the main hard-data read on euro-area household spending, released at 09:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: A quiet companion to US and Canadian payrolls. July sales follow a -0.3% June print. A further drop would stack a European consumer miss on top of whatever NFP does; a rebound would be a modest EUR-supportive offset if US payrolls disappoint.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.4% MoM: euro-area consumer holding. EUR mildly bid, European cyclicals supported.
events.ifLower: Another negative month: consumer retrenching. EUR sold, a mild risk-off overlay on the NFP tape.

events.whatItIs: Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey for August, covering net employment change, the unemployment rate, full-time versus part-time jobs, and participation, released at 12:30 UTC alongside US NFP.
events.whyItMatters: The BoC just decided Wednesday. A second strong jobs print would make that hold look behind the curve; a drop in employment with unemployment jumping toward 6.7% would reopen an October cut and sell CAD into whatever the US payrolls number is doing at the same stamp. Trade-war headlines are the overlay.
events.ifHigher: Jobs above +40K with unemployment steady: labour still tight. CAD bids, BoC cut talk fades.
events.ifLower: Jobs negative or unemployment at 6.7%+: labour cracking. CAD sold, BoC easing bets return, oil-linked FX weakens.

events.event: Nonfarm Payrolls (August 2026) + Unemployment Rate + Avg Hourly Earnings
events.previous: -23K jobs (July 2026); Unemployment 4.1%; Avg Hourly Earnings +0.1% MoM / +3.2% YoY
events.forecast: ~+45K jobs (range +12K to +65K); Unemployment 4.2%; AHE ~+0.2% MoM / ~+3.3% YoY
events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' Employment Situation report, covering August's net payroll change, the unemployment rate, labour-force participation, and average hourly earnings -- the single most market-moving monthly US data release.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's fulcrum and the last hard labour print before the September 15-16 FOMC. July's -23,000 print, the preliminary benchmark revision, and Warsh's Jackson Hole warning that inflation is still too high have markets assigning about a 57% chance of a September hike. A bounce toward +50K with unemployment at 4.1% lets the hike camp argue July was noise; a second negative month, or unemployment at 4.3%+, would collapse those odds 12 days before the decision. Average hourly earnings are the wage-inflation channel Warsh actually cares about.
events.ifHigher: Above +100K with unemployment at 4.0% and AHE at +0.3%+: July was noise, labour re-accelerating. USD spikes, gold and BTC sold, September hike odds jump above 70%, stocks whipsaw.
events.ifLower: Below 0 or unemployment at 4.3%+: labour deterioration confirmed. Gold and duration rally, USD drops, September hike odds collapse, equities catch a relief bid on the hold.

events.event: Fed communications blackout begins Saturday September 5 (through September 17)
events.whatItIs: The FOMC external-communications blackout starts at 04:00 UTC on Saturday September 5, the second Saturday before the September 15-16 meeting, and runs through Thursday September 17. No governor or voting president will discuss the outlook in public.
events.whyItMatters: Friday's NFP is the last number that can still be debated by named Fed speakers. From Saturday the tape trades the data, the Beige Book, and Warsh's Jackson Hole text with no live pushback. Positioning typically compresses into the September 16 18:00 UTC decision, the SEP, and the dot plot.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- no release.
events.ifLower: N/A -- no release.

2026-09-14.summary: Fed hike, BoJ to 1.25%, and BoE hold headline a three-central-bank week.

events.whatItIs: METI's final July reading of Japanese factory, mine, and utility output, revising the preliminary print released in late August.
events.whyItMatters: This is a quiet Japan print four days before the BoJ is widely expected to hike to 1.25%. An unrevised +0.1% keeps the 'domestic economy is solid' line that sources say is in the draft statement; a downward revision would be the first growth argument the doves can use into Friday.
events.ifHigher: Revised above +0.5%: factories firmer than the prelim. Mild JPY bid, hike-and-hawkish-guidance case intact.
events.ifLower: Revised below -0.5%: activity slipping. JPY sold at the margin, Ueda's 'solid economy' line gets a question at the press conference.

events.event: Canada CPI (August 2026) -- headline, trimmed-mean, and median
events.whatItIs: Statistics Canada's monthly Consumer Price Index plus the Bank of Canada's preferred core gauges (CPI-trim and CPI-median), released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Headline is expected to hold at 3.0% on still-elevated gasoline (up about 23% year-on-year) while the BoC's core measures stay around the 2% target. The Bank held at 2.25% this month and warned that significant energy spillover into broader prices could force a hike; Monday's cores are the test, and the summary of deliberations lands Wednesday afternoon.
events.ifHigher: Headline above 3.2% or trimmed-mean at 2.2%+: energy leaking into core. CAD bids, BoC hike chatter for December returns.
events.ifLower: Headline at or below 2.8% with cores under 1.8%: pass-through still contained. CAD sold, December hike odds fade.

events.event: China Industrial Production + Retail Sales + FAI (August 2026)
events.previous: IP +4.5% YoY; retail +0.6% YoY; FAI -6.7% YTD (July 2026)
events.forecast: IP ~+4.8% YoY; retail ~+0.8% YoY; FAI ~-7.0% YTD
events.whatItIs: The National Bureau of Statistics monthly activity dump: factory output, consumer-goods sales, and year-to-date fixed-asset investment, typically released at 02:00 UTC with an NBS press conference.
events.whyItMatters: China is still an export-led, domestic-demand-soft story. Consensus is another month of that split: industrial production firming on AI-related external demand, retail stuck under 1%, and fixed-asset investment deepening its contraction. The print lands into a global tape that is already pricing a Fed hike and a BoJ hike, so a domestic miss would hit copper, iron ore, and the Aussie just as RBA Governor Bullock speaks Thursday.
events.ifHigher: IP above 5.5% with retail at 1.5%+: domestic demand joining the export bid. AUD, CNH, and industrial metals rally.
events.ifLower: IP below 4% or retail negative: the domestic slump is spreading. Commodities sold, AUD and CNH weaken, China-demand scare into the Fed.

events.event: UK Labour Market (August 2026) -- unemployment, average earnings, claimant count
events.previous: Unemployment 4.9%; average earnings incl. bonus +4.1% 3m/y; claimant count -11.0K (July 2026)
events.whatItIs: The ONS labour-market package: the ILO unemployment rate, three-month average weekly earnings with and without bonuses, and the claimant-count change, released at 06:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the last labour print before Thursday's BoE decision. Markets expect a hold at 3.75% on slack and cooling pay; consensus is unemployment stuck at 4.9% with earnings slowing to 3.9% from 4.1%. A pay re-acceleration would fatten the 32% hike tail; a jump in unemployment would lock the hold and argue the next move is still a cut, not a hike.
events.ifHigher: Earnings at 4.3%+ or unemployment down to 4.7%: labour tighter than the MPC assumed. GBP bids, Thursday hike odds jump.
events.ifLower: Unemployment at 5.1%+ or earnings under 3.6%: slack building. GBP sold, hold locked, 2026 hike pricing unwinds.

events.whatItIs: A scheduled vesting cliff of about 93 million ARB, worth roughly $13 million at recent prices, the largest named dollar unlock of the week.
events.whyItMatters: ARB unlocks have been a monthly supply event through 2026. This one lands into a crypto tape that is already pricing an 85% Fed-hike probability, so any alt-specific selling will be hard to separate from the macro bid. A clean absorb is a constructive L2 tell into Wednesday's FOMC; a break is the first supply test of that hike-priced tape.
events.ifHigher: Unlock absorbed with ARB holding: supply was priced. Mild constructive signal for L2 beta.
events.ifLower: ARB breaks and pulls ETH beta: supply hits a thin tape. Altcoin risk-off, BTC relatively resilient.

events.whatItIs: The New York Fed's monthly survey of manufacturers in New York state, a diffusion index where zero separates expansion from contraction, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the first regional factory print of the FOMC week and a cooling from August's 20.6 is the base case. Prices-paid and employment sub-indices are the lines that feed the hike debate: a still-hot prices-paid print hours before the Committee sits would be one more input for the hawks; a collapse toward zero would argue the summer factory bounce is fading.
events.ifHigher: Above 20 with prices-paid firm: factories still running hot. Modest USD bid into the FOMC.
events.ifLower: Below 5: the regional bounce is reversing. Cyclicals sold, a soft-activity overlay on a hawkish Fed.

events.event: FOMC Meeting Day 1 (September 15-16) -- no statement until Wednesday
events.whatItIs: The first of two days of Federal Open Market Committee deliberations. No communication is released on day one; the statement, SEP, dot plot, and Warsh press conference follow Wednesday at 18:00 and 18:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The Fed remains in its communications blackout through Wednesday's decision, so there is no Fed-speak to trade and positioning typically compresses. Volume thins and ranges narrow into the 18:00 UTC announcement. Tuesday's Empire State print and Wednesday's retail sales are the last data the tape can trade before the statement.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- no release.
events.ifLower: N/A -- no release.

events.forecast: Headline ~+2.8% YoY (fuel boost); core ~+2.7% YoY; RPI ~+3.5% YoY
events.whatItIs: The ONS Consumer Price Index, including the core measure that excludes energy, food, alcohol, and tobacco, plus RPI, released at 06:00 UTC the day before the BoE decision.
events.whyItMatters: Investec's base case is a fuel-led headline bounce with steady core -- the configuration that lets the MPC hold at 3.75%. A core jump toward 3% would fatten Thursday's 32% hike tail and put the three hike-voters in the majority argument. This is also the UK analogue of Friday's hot US core CPI, so a miss here would split the two hiking cycles the tape is trading as one theme.
events.ifHigher: Headline above 3.0% or core at 2.9%+: fuel leaking into core. GBP spikes, gilts sold, Thursday hike odds jump through 50%.
events.ifLower: Headline at or below 2.5% with core under 2.5%: disinflation intact. GBP sold, hold locked, 2026 hike pricing fades.

events.event: US Retail Sales (August 2026) -- headline and ex-autos
events.actual: Headline +1.2% MoM (vs +0.8% expected); core retail sales +1.4%
events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's Advance Monthly Retail Trade report: the first look at August consumer spending, including the control group that feeds directly into GDP goods consumption.
events.whyItMatters: This is the last demand print the FOMC sees before the 18:00 UTC statement. July fell 0.6% and was part of the 'economy is cooling' case; consensus is a bounce to +0.3% as gasoline prices lifted the headline. The control group (ex-autos, gas, building materials, food services) is the real signal: a second negative month would sit awkwardly next to a hike, while a +0.9% rebound would let Warsh say demand is still too firm for a hold.
events.ifHigher: Headline above +0.6% with control group at +1%+: the consumer is not slowing. USD spikes into the FOMC, hike looks locked, equities mix.
events.ifLower: Headline negative again or control group under 0: demand rolling over. A hold argument into a Committee that is 85% priced to hike; gold bids, USD wobbles.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending September 11)
events.previous: -0.39M barrels (week ending September 4; consensus had been -1.3M)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly count of commercial crude oil held in US storage, plus gasoline and distillate stocks and refinery utilisation, released at 14:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Energy is the inflation overlay on this FOMC. Brent has been above $100 on Middle East supply risk, August CPI gasoline jumped 3.9%, and last week's EIA was a smaller-than-expected crude draw with gasoline and distillates building. A large crude and gasoline draw two hours before the Fed statement would re-open the energy-inflation channel Warsh has to address; a build would take some heat off the hike.
events.ifHigher: Large draw in crude and gasoline: WTI rallies, the energy-CPI channel stays live into the statement.
events.ifLower: Large build: crude sells off, the pump-price impulse starts to fade, mildly dovish read-through for the dots.

events.event: FOMC Rate Decision + SEP / Dot Plot + Warsh Press Conference (18:30 UTC)
events.forecast: 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% (~85% priced); first hike of 2026
events.actual: Hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00%; 12-0 vote; 12 of 18 SEP participants see one more 2026 hike
events.whatItIs: The Federal Open Market Committee's policy decision at 18:00 UTC, the quarterly Summary of Economic Projections and dot plot, and Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 18:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is a projection meeting, so the hike (if it comes) is only half the event: the 2026-2028 dots and the inflation forecasts are the other half. August payrolls at +162,000, core CPI at +0.3% MoM, and PPI at +5.4% YoY have taken hike odds from about 57% at Jackson Hole to about 85%. A hike with a 2026 median that shows another move would reprice the front end and gold; a hike framed as a one-and-done, or a hold against the strip, would be the surprise.
events.ifHigher: Hike plus a 2026 median that shows another hike, or a dissent for 50bp: USD spikes, gold and BTC sold, 10-year tests 5%, equities de-risk.
events.ifLower: Hold, or a hike with dots that show no further 2026 moves and dovish Warsh colour: relief rally in gold, duration, and risk; USD gives back the hike premium.

events.whatItIs: The second-largest US homebuilder's fiscal third-quarter results, covering orders, deliveries, margins, and incentive commentary, reported after the cash close.
