events.whyItMatters: Lennar is the cleanest housing-and-rates print of a week that also brings Thursday's housing starts and a Fed that is 85% priced to hike. Higher mortgage rates from a hike would hit the order book; any cut to full-year deliveries or a jump in incentives would be a growth-scare overlay on an already hawkish tape. A beat with margins intact would argue the buyer is still there at current rates.
events.ifHigher: Orders and margins beat with guide intact: the housing consumer is holding. LEN and homebuilder beta rally.
events.ifLower: Orders miss or incentives jump: rate-sensitive demand is cracking. LEN sold; a housing overlay on Thursday's starts.

events.event: Eurozone CPI Final (August 2026) -- headline and core
events.previous: Flash was +3.3% YoY headline; core +2.4% YoY
events.whatItIs: Eurostat's final August HICP, confirming or revising the flash estimate, released at 09:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The flash already printed a hot 3.3% headline after the ECB hiked to 2.50% last Thursday. Final prints rarely move the tape unless they revise, but a core revision higher would add to the 65% chance markets are assigning to another ECB hike in October. This lands two hours before the BoE and the morning after the FOMC, so it is a confirmation print in a three-bank week, not a catalyst of its own.
events.ifHigher: Core revised to 2.6%+: second-round effects in the euro area. EUR bids, Bunds sold, October ECB hike odds firm.
events.ifLower: Headline revised to 3.1% or below: the flash overstated the fuel impulse. EUR sold, October hike odds fade.

events.event: BoE Interest Rate Decision + MPC Votes + Monetary Policy Summary
events.forecast: Hold at 3.75%; votes ~3-0-6; ~32% chance of a 25bp hike
events.actual: Held at 3.75%; votes 6-3 (three for a hike to 4%); gilt sales paused six months
events.whatItIs: The Bank of England's Bank Rate decision at 11:00 UTC, the nine-member MPC vote split, the monetary-policy summary, and the minutes, released the morning after the FOMC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the hold in a week of hikes. Markets assign only about a 32% chance of a 25-basis-point move after a muted labour backdrop and scant second-round inflation effects, with three members already voting to hike. Tuesday's earnings and Wednesday's CPI are the live inputs: hot UK data plus a Fed hike overnight would put those three in a stronger position; soft data locks 3.75% and argues the next UK move is still not a hike.
events.ifHigher: Surprise hike, or a hold with 4+ hike votes: GBP spikes, gilts sold, 2026 UK hike path re-steepens.
events.ifLower: Hold with fewer than three hike votes, or a cut: GBP sold, gilts rally, the UK cycle decouples from the Fed and BoJ.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of first-time filings for unemployment insurance, the highest-frequency US labour-market print, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the first labour print after a Fed decision that will have been written on the back of +162,000 August payrolls. A spike toward 230K would be the first crack in that labour story and would start to fade 2026 hike-follow-through; a drop back through 200K would confirm the payrolls bounce was not a one-month blip.
events.ifHigher: Above 230K: labour softening after the hike. Gold and duration bid, USD gives back, 2026 dots questioned.
events.ifLower: Below 195K: labour still tight. USD bids, the hike looks validated, gold sold.

events.whatItIs: The Philadelphia Fed's monthly Business Outlook Survey of manufacturers in the Third District, a diffusion index released at 12:30 UTC alongside claims and housing starts.
events.whyItMatters: August's 47.4 was an unusually strong regional print; consensus is a sharp cooling toward 29. Prices-paid is the line that matters the morning after a Fed hike: a still-elevated prices-paid sub-index would argue the Committee is tightening into firm pipeline inflation, while a collapse would be the first activity-and-prices cooling the doves wanted before the hike.
events.ifHigher: Above 40 with prices-paid firm: the regional boom is not fading. Modest USD and cyclicals bid.
events.ifLower: Below 15: the August spike was noise. Cyclicals sold, a growth-scare overlay on the hike.

events.whatItIs: Census Bureau counts of new residential construction begun and permits issued, reported at an annualised rate at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Housing is the most rate-sensitive demand block, and this print lands the morning after a Fed that is 85% priced to hike plus Lennar's overnight numbers. Starts are expected to rebound to 1.32 million from 1.24 million; permits are expected to ease. A starts miss alongside a Lennar order-book warning would be the first evidence the rate impulse is hitting housing in real time.
events.ifHigher: Starts above 1.40M: housing holding at current mortgage rates. Homebuilder beta supported, USD mixed.
events.ifLower: Starts below 1.20M: rate-sensitive demand cracking. Homebuilders sold, a growth overlay on the hike.

events.whatItIs: The National Association of Realtors' index of housing contracts signed but not yet closed, a leading read on existing-home sales, released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Pending sales fell 2.3% in July and are expected to bounce 0.3%. Signed contracts today become closings in 30-60 days, so this is the first look at whether August's mortgage-rate backup already froze the buyer. It lands in the same housing block as starts, permits, and Lennar, the morning after the Fed.
events.ifHigher: Above +2%: buyers still engaging. Mild support for homebuilders and the consumer-durable complex.
events.ifLower: Another drop of 2%+: the rate backup is locking the existing-home market. Housing beta sold.

events.event: Japan CPI (August 2026) -- headline and core (ex-fresh food)
events.whatItIs: The Statistics Bureau's national CPI, including the BoJ's preferred core measure that excludes fresh food, released at 23:30 UTC Thursday morning, hours before the rate decision.
events.whyItMatters: The BoJ is hiking into this print. Underlying inflation is approaching the 2% target and sources say upside risks from oil, a weak yen, and AI demand are the reason for moving to 1.25%. A core hold at 1.8% is the base case and does not block the hike; a jump toward 2.1% would argue for hawkish Ueda guidance on the pace of further moves, which is what the yen actually trades.
events.ifHigher: Core at 2.0%+: the hike looks behind the curve. JPY spikes, USD/JPY sold, 50bp chatter (still not the base case) returns.
events.ifLower: Core at 1.6% or below: the inflation case for hiking now is thinner. JPY sold, Ueda's 'upside risks' line gets a harder question.

events.whatItIs: RBA Governor Michele Bullock's scheduled remarks, timed for Friday morning in Australia, ahead of the September 28-29 policy meeting.
events.whyItMatters: Officials have been hawkish enough that markets are leaning toward a fourth RBA hike this month. Bullock speaks into a tape that will already have a Fed hike (or a hold shock) and a Japan CPI print, with the BoJ decision still a few hours away. Any signal that September 28-29 is live would bid the Aussie; a patient tone would fade the fourth-hike pricing.
events.ifHigher: Bullock flags September as live or stresses upside inflation risks: AUD bids, front-end swaps reprice a hike.
events.ifLower: Patient tone, data-dependent, no September tell: AUD sold, November becomes the live meeting instead.

events.event: BoJ Interest Rate Decision + Ueda Press Conference
events.previous: 1.00% (hiked in June; 8-1 hold in July with Takata dissenting for 1.25%)
events.actual: Hiked 25bp to 1.25%; 7-2 vote (Asada and Sato dissented); yen through 157
events.whatItIs: The Bank of Japan's policy-rate decision, typically around 03:00 UTC, followed by Governor Kazuo Ueda's press conference. Sources say the Board will raise the policy rate to 1.25%, the highest in about 31 years.
events.whyItMatters: This hike is as close to a done deal as BoJ meetings get: Nikkei, Jiji, and 97% of a Reuters poll all look for 25bp, three months after the June move -- the shortest gap in this cycle. The event is therefore Ueda's guidance. A hawkish press conference that keeps October or December in play would extend the yen bid and pressure the carry trade; a hike framed as a pause-to-assess would be the yen-negative surprise, especially if the Fed hiked the night before.
events.ifHigher: Hike plus hawkish Ueda (another 2026 move live, or a 50bp discussion): JPY spikes, USD/JPY sold, global carry unwinds at the margin.
events.ifLower: Hold, or a hike with dovish 'pause' language and no further-hike signal: JPY sold, carry bid returns, Nikkei supported.

events.event: UK Retail Sales (August 2026) -- MoM and YoY
events.whatItIs: The ONS measure of the volume of retail spending, including and excluding auto fuel, released at 06:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the first UK demand print after Thursday's BoE hold. Investec expects another small drop as higher fuel prices weigh on volumes. A third consecutive monthly decline would confirm the consumer is the slack the MPC is looking at; a surprise bounce would sit awkwardly next to a hold and start to rebuild December hike odds.
events.ifHigher: MoM above +0.3%: the UK consumer is not rolling over. GBP bids, December hike odds firm.
events.ifLower: MoM below -0.8%: demand cracking. GBP sold, gilts bid, the hold looks well judged.

events.event: US Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (August 2026)
events.whatItIs: The Federal Reserve's monthly index of output at factories, mines, and utilities, plus the share of installed capacity in use, released at 13:15 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: A quiet Friday capstone after the three central-bank decisions. Capacity utilisation is a late-cycle inflation input: a rise alongside a Fed hike would argue the Committee is tightening into a still-tight industrial base; a drop would be the first activity cooling in the post-decision tape. Manufacturing production is the line that maps onto Thursday's Philly Fed.
events.ifHigher: IP above +0.5% with utilisation rising: factories still tight. Modest USD bid, cyclicals supported.
events.ifLower: IP below -0.3%: industrial demand rolling over. Cyclicals sold, a growth-scare overlay on the new funds rate.

2026-09-21.summary: Flash PMIs, Trump-Xi, and Costco headline a post-hike digestion week.

events.event: Japan Silver Week -- markets closed Monday through Wednesday
events.whatItIs: A five-day Japanese holiday stretch: Respect for the Aged Day (Monday), a Citizens' Holiday bridge (Tuesday), and Autumnal Equinox Day (Wednesday). Tokyo cash, JGBs, and the yen session are shut until Thursday.
events.whyItMatters: The BoJ hiked to 1.25% on Friday and the yen slipped through 157 on two dovish dissents. Tokyo's first full session is Thursday, the same morning Australia jobs and the SNB print and the same day Trump hosts Xi. Thin Asia liquidity Mon-Wed means USD/JPY and Nikkei futures will gap into Thursday's reopen.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- market holiday.
events.ifLower: N/A -- market holiday.

events.event: PBoC Loan Prime Rate Decision -- 1-year and 5-year
events.whatItIs: China's benchmark lending rates: the 1-year LPR prices most corporate and household loans, the 5-year LPR prices mortgages. Published monthly by the National Interbank Funding Center under PBoC authorization.
events.whyItMatters: The hold was fully priced (21 of 21 in the Reuters poll) and landed into a stronger yuan and a Fed that just hiked. Pan Gongsheng has flagged weak credit demand from property and local government, so the constraint is bank net-interest margins, not a hawkish turn. The mapping this week is the Trump-Xi summit, not a China easing surprise.
events.ifHigher: A surprise hike (not the base case): CNH bids, property and EM risk sold.
events.ifLower: A 10bp cut: the first easing in 16 months. CNH sold, AUD and industrial metals bid, a stimulus overlay on Thursday's summit.

events.event: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee Speaks (OMFIF, London)
events.whatItIs: The first named FOMC speaker off last week's blackout, livestreamed from an OMFIF event in London at 10:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: October hike odds are a coin flip (~55-58%). Goolsbee is a 2026 voter and has been on the less-hawkish side of the room; any signal that last week's unanimous 25bp was one-and-done, or that another move is live, will reprice the front end before Williams and Jefferson speak Tuesday.
events.ifHigher: Goolsbee backs another 2026 hike or stresses broad inflation: USD bids, October odds jump, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Patient tone, data-dependent, oil-only inflation: October odds fade, gold and duration bid.

events.whatItIs: A weighted average of 85 monthly indicators of US growth, inflation, and the labor market. Zero is trend; positive is above-trend activity.
events.whyItMatters: A quiet Monday print after last week's +1.2% retail sales and +162K payrolls. A move back above zero would confirm the 'economy is expanding at a solid pace' line in Wednesday's FOMC statement; another negative month would be the first activity crack the doves can use into this week's Fed-speak.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.4: activity above trend. Modest USD bid into Goolsbee.
events.ifLower: Below -0.3: the July dip is extending. Cyclicals sold, a growth overlay on a hawkish Fed.

events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the ECB President, the first high-profile euro-area voice after last week's Fed hike and with euro-area flash PMIs due Wednesday.
events.whyItMatters: The ECB hiked to 2.50% the week before last; markets still assign a live chance of an October follow-up after the 3.3% August HICP flash. Lagarde's tone into Wednesday's PMIs is the EUR tell: hawkish and the dollar-euro spread compresses; patient and EUR sold against a Fed that just hiked.
events.ifHigher: Lagarde keeps October in play or flags second-round energy effects: EUR bids, Bunds sold.
events.ifLower: Hold-and-assess language: EUR sold, the US-euro policy gap widens.

events.event: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem Speaks
events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the BoC Governor, days after last Monday's Canada CPI and with Thursday's July retail-sales final on the docket.
events.whyItMatters: The BoC held at 2.25% this month and warned that energy spillover into core could force a hike. Last week's CPI was the test; Macklem's colour is the CAD tell into a Fed that just widened the US-Canada rate gap.
events.ifHigher: Macklem flags a December hike or core pass-through: CAD bids.
events.ifLower: Look-through-oil language: CAD sold, the policy gap vs the Fed stays wide.

events.whatItIs: The ONS monthly public-sector finance release: the gap between government spending and receipts, released at 06:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: A seasonal August hole is the base case. Sterling is still digesting Thursday's 6-3 BoE hold and Bailey's warning that a prolonged Middle East conflict may require tighter policy. A much larger deficit would be a gilt-supply story, not a Bank Rate story; a surprise shrink would take some heat off gilt issuance into Friday's Bailey remarks.
events.ifHigher: Borrowing worse than -20B: gilt cheapening, mild GBP drag.
events.ifLower: Better than -10B: issuance scare fades, modest GBP support.

events.whatItIs: The auto-parts retailer's fiscal fourth-quarter results, covering same-store sales, DIY vs commercial mix, and margin commentary, reported before the cash open.
events.whyItMatters: AutoZone is the first large consumer print of a week that ends with Costco. A miss on comps or a margin squeeze from higher freight and tariffs would be an early tell that the post-hike consumer is trading down; a beat with commercial mix intact would argue the repair-not-replace cycle is still funding the tape.
events.ifHigher: Comps and margins beat: consumer-discretionary beta supported.
events.ifLower: Comps miss or margins compress: a DIY-demand crack into Costco Thursday.

events.whatItIs: The Richmond Fed's Fifth District Survey of Manufacturing Activity, a diffusion index released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: A quiet regional print the day before national flash PMIs. Prices-paid is the line that matters in a post-hike week: a hot prices-paid sub-index would feed the 'inflation is broader than oil' case Schmid already made Friday; a drop toward contraction would be the first factory cooling into Wednesday's S&P Global flash.
events.ifHigher: Above 10 with prices-paid firm: regional factories still expanding. Modest USD bid.
events.ifLower: Below 0: Fifth District slipping into contraction. Cyclicals sold ahead of the flash PMIs.

events.whatItIs: The European Commission's flash monthly survey of euro-area household sentiment, released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: A hold near -16 is the base case into Wednesday's services PMI. Energy bills are the swing factor after Brent spent last week above $100. A drop toward -20 would argue the ECB's September hike is already hitting the consumer; a bounce would be the first confidence repair after the 3.3% HICP flash.
events.ifHigher: Above -12: households looking through energy. Mild EUR bid into Wednesday PMIs.
events.ifLower: Below -20: energy is hitting real incomes. EUR sold, a growth overlay on Lagarde.

events.event: New York Fed President John Williams Speaks -- Treasury Market Conference
events.whatItIs: Keynote remarks at the New York Fed's 2026 Treasury Market Conference. Vice Chair Philip Jefferson follows at 14:20 UTC on discount-window modernization. Williams is a permanent FOMC voter.
events.whyItMatters: Williams is the most important speaker of the week after the Chair. The 10-year is sitting on 5% and October odds are a coin flip. Any colour on the path of rates, the balance sheet, or whether last week's hike was the start of a sequence will reprice the front end more than Richmond Fed or AutoZone.
events.ifHigher: Williams backs another 2026 hike or flags 5% yields as consistent with the outlook: USD spikes, gold sold, October odds jump.
events.ifLower: Technical speech with no policy tell, or a data-dependent pause signal: October odds fade, duration bid.

events.whatItIs: The national homebuilder's quarterly results, covering orders, cancellations, incentives, and community-count guidance, reported after the cash close.
events.whyItMatters: This is the housing follow-through after Lennar missed last Wednesday (EPS $1.19 vs ~$1.30, orders -9%) into 7%+ mortgages and a Fed hike. A second order-book miss would confirm rate-sensitive demand is cracking; a beat with incentives contained would argue Lennar was company-specific. Thursday's new-home sales are the macro companion.
events.ifHigher: Orders and margins beat: homebuilder beta repairs after Lennar.
events.ifLower: Orders miss or incentives jump: housing beta sold into Thursday's sales print.

events.event: Australia Flash PMIs (September 2026) -- manufacturing and services
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary September read on Australian private-sector activity, released at 23:00 UTC Tuesday, the first flash of the global PMI batch.
events.whyItMatters: The RBA is ~90% priced to hike 25bp to 4.60% on September 29. A hot services print overnight Tuesday would lock that hike before Thursday's jobs report; a drop toward 50 would be the first activity argument the doves can use, and would fade the Aussie into the SNB and Trump-Xi Thursday.
events.ifHigher: Services above 54: activity still too firm for a hold. AUD bids, September 29 hike looks locked.
events.ifLower: Either index below 50: the domestic impulse is fading. AUD sold, November becomes the live meeting.

events.event: Germany Flash PMIs (September 2026) -- manufacturing, services, composite
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary September PMI for the euro area's largest economy, released at 07:30 UTC, 30 minutes before the euro-area aggregate.
events.whyItMatters: Germany is the factory engine of the euro-area flash. Manufacturing is expected to hold in the mid-54s on AI-related external demand; services are expected to crawl back to 50 after August's 49.7 contraction. A services miss would be the first post-ECB-hike demand crack; a manufacturing drop below 52 would hit the DAX into Thursday's ifo.
events.ifHigher: Composite above 53 with services back through 51: domestic demand joining the export bid. EUR and DAX bid.
events.ifLower: Composite below 50 or manufacturing under 52: the expansion is stalling. EUR sold, Bunds bid.

events.event: Eurozone Flash PMIs (September 2026) -- manufacturing, services, composite
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary September PMI for the euro area, the first bloc-wide activity read after the ECB's hike to 2.50%. Released at 08:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the European half of Wednesday's global flash. Consensus is a slight cooling that still stays in expansion -- the configuration that lets the ECB look through energy and keep October as a live-but-not-locked meeting. Prices-paid in services is the inflation tell Lagarde will have been asked about Monday.
events.ifHigher: Composite at 53+ with services prices-paid firm: the hike is not biting. EUR spikes, October ECB odds firm.
events.ifLower: Composite at or below 50: the expansion is stalling. EUR sold, Bunds rally, October hike odds fade.

events.event: UK Flash PMIs (September 2026) -- manufacturing, services, composite
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary September PMI for the UK, released at 08:30 UTC, the first activity read after Thursday's 6-3 BoE hold.
events.whyItMatters: Bailey warned that a prolonged Middle East conflict may require tighter policy. A services hold above 52 with prices charged still elevated would fatten the three hike-voters' case into Friday's Bailey speech; a drop toward 50 would lock the hold and argue the next UK move is still not a hike.
events.ifHigher: Composite above 53.5 with services prices charged firm: GBP bids, November hike odds jump.
events.ifLower: Composite below 51: demand cooling. GBP sold, gilts bid, the hold looks well judged.

events.event: General Mills (GIS) + Cintas (CTAS) + Paychex (PAYX) Earnings (before open)
events.whatItIs: A consumer-and-payroll cluster: General Mills on grocery pricing, Cintas on business-services demand, Paychex on small-business employment, all reporting before Wednesday's open.
events.whyItMatters: These three sit between AutoZone and Costco and give a read on whether the post-hike consumer and the small-business payroll complex are holding. Paychex is a high-frequency companion to Thursday's claims; GIS is the grocery-price tell into $100 oil.
events.ifHigher: All three beat with guides intact: the consumer-and-payroll complex is holding. Modest equity bid into Costco.
events.ifLower: GIS margin squeeze or Paychex employment miss: a demand crack the day of the flash PMIs.

events.event: S&P Global US Flash PMIs (September 2026) -- manufacturing, services, composite
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary September PMI for the US private sector, released at 13:45 UTC -- the first national activity read after Wednesday's FOMC hike.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's data pillar. August's 56.0 composite was a strong expansion print the Committee hiked into. Consensus is a slight cooling that still sits well above 50. A hold of 56 would keep October hike odds bid against a 5% 10-year; a drop through 53 with services prices charged rolling over would be the first argument that last week's hike is already doing work. Input prices are the inflation line Warsh has to own.
events.ifHigher: Composite at 56+ with services prices charged firm: the economy is not slowing. USD spikes, October odds jump through 70%, gold and BTC sold.
events.ifLower: Composite below 53 or services under 54: activity cooling after the hike. Gold and duration bid, October odds fade toward a hold.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending September 18)
events.previous: -0.6M barrels (week ending September 11; consensus had been -1.6M)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly count of commercial crude oil held in US storage, plus gasoline and distillate stocks and refinery utilisation, released at 14:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: WTI settled Friday at $100.30 after a $106.75 Tuesday high on Middle East supply risk. A large crude and gasoline draw the day before Trump-Xi would keep the energy-CPI channel live into Costco and Friday durables; a build would take some heat off the pump-price impulse the Fed just hiked into.
events.ifHigher: Large draw in crude and gasoline: WTI rallies, the energy-inflation overlay stays live into Thursday's summit.
events.ifLower: Large build: crude sells off, the $100 handle is tested, mildly dovish read-through for October odds.

events.event: Australia Labour Force (August 2026) -- employment change, unemployment, participation
events.whatItIs: The Australian Bureau of Statistics monthly Labour Force Survey, covering employment, unemployment, participation, and hours, released at 01:30 UTC -- the last labour print before the September 28-29 RBA meeting.
events.whyItMatters: Markets price about a 90% chance of a 25bp RBA hike to 4.60% next Tuesday. JP Morgan's base case is unemployment holding 4.5% with a +15K employment gain, which they say does not block the hike. A jump in unemployment toward 4.7% would be the first argument for waiting until the quarterly CPI the day after the meeting; a drop toward 4.3% with a +40K print would lock 4.60% and open the door to a second 2026 move.
events.ifHigher: Employment above +40K or unemployment down to 4.3%: labour too tight for a hold. AUD spikes, September 29 hike looks done.
events.ifLower: Unemployment at 4.7%+ or another employment drop: the RBA's labour case thins. AUD sold, November becomes live.

events.event: SNB Interest Rate Decision + Schlegel Press Conference (~08:00 UTC)
events.whatItIs: The Swiss National Bank's quarterly policy assessment at 07:30 UTC, the conditional inflation forecast, and Chairman Martin Schlegel's news conference at 08:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The SNB has been at 0% since cutting there in 2025 and the conditional forecast in June assumed it stays there through 2028. A hold is fully priced. The event is the franc and the inflation forecast: a higher 2026-28 path on energy would be the first hike-talk in a year; a cut back into negative territory (not the base case) would be the CHF-negative shock. Norges Bank (4.25%) and the Riksbank (hold at 1.75%) decide the same morning.
events.ifHigher: Surprise hike, or a hold with a higher inflation forecast and hike optionality: CHF spikes, EUR/CHF sold.
events.ifLower: Cut, or a hold with FX-intervention language and a lower forecast: CHF sold, the safe-haven bid fades into Trump-Xi.

events.whatItIs: The ifo Institute's monthly survey of 9,000 German firms covering current conditions and expectations, released at 08:00 UTC the morning after the German flash PMI.
events.whyItMatters: ifo is the slower, broader companion to Wednesday's flash. A hold near 89 with expectations ticking up would confirm the PMI expansion; a drop back through 88 with current conditions slipping would argue the flash overstated the factory bounce and would hit the DAX into the Trump-Xi session.
events.ifHigher: Above 90: German business mood repairing. Mild EUR and DAX bid.
events.ifLower: Below 87: the summer bounce is fading. DAX sold, Bunds bid.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of first-time filings for unemployment insurance, the highest-frequency US labour-market print, released at 12:30 UTC alongside the Q2 current account.
events.whyItMatters: Last week's 196K was the lowest since July and broke a five-week stretch above 200K -- a labour print the FOMC hiked into. A rebound toward 230K would be the first crack in that story and would start to fade October odds; a hold under 200K would confirm the payrolls bounce was not a one-week blip. Continuing claims (prior 1.730M) are the stock-of-unemployment companion.
events.ifHigher: Above 230K: labour softening after the hike. Gold and duration bid, USD gives back, October odds fade.
events.ifLower: Below 195K: labour still tight. USD bids, the hike looks validated, gold sold.

events.whatItIs: Statistics Canada's monthly retail trade report, confirming or revising the August 21 advance estimate of a 0.8% July drop, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The flash was the first monthly decline in seven months and the sharpest in ten. A confirmation would be a demand miss the morning of Trump-Xi and the day after US flash PMIs; an upward revision toward flat would argue Canadian households looked through $100 oil. CAD also trades as an oil currency into the EIA hangover.
events.ifHigher: Revised to 0% or better: the July hole was a flash miss. CAD bids.
events.ifLower: Revised below -1.2%: the consumer is rolling over. CAD sold, a growth overlay on Macklem.

events.whatItIs: Census Bureau / HUD count of new single-family houses sold, reported at a seasonally adjusted annual rate at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: July was a six-month low. Consensus is a bounce to about 620K after MBA's builder-application proxy pointed to ~664K. This lands the morning after KB Home, two days after Lennar's order-book miss, and the same session as Trump-Xi. Months' supply (9.6 in July) and the median price are the incentive tell into 7%+ mortgages.
events.ifHigher: Above 660K: the July hole was noise. Homebuilder beta repairs.
events.ifLower: Below 580K: rate-sensitive demand is cracking. Homebuilders sold, a housing overlay on Costco.

events.event: Trump-Xi White House Summit -- talks and state dinner
events.whatItIs: President Xi Jinping's first White House visit in a decade. He arrives Wednesday at Joint Base Andrews; Thursday is the bilateral meeting and a state dinner. The live policy question is whether the two extend the tariff truce that expires November 10.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's geopolitical fulcrum. White House officials have played down breakthroughs; Scott Bessent and He Lifeng held prep talks in New York on Sunday. A contained readout that extends the truce would bid the chip complex and CNH. A rare-earth, Taiwan, or Iran headline would reprice the same names first, and would hit Tokyo's first full session after Silver Week. October Fed odds are a second-order channel: a trade scare that lifts oil keeps the hike path bid.
events.ifHigher: Truce extended, or a constructive rare-earth / AI-export readout: chips, CNH, and risk bid; USD mixed.
events.ifLower: No truce language, or a Taiwan / rare-earth / Iran headline: chips and EM sold, USD and gold bid, oil bid if Iran is in the statement.

events.whatItIs: The warehouse retailer's fiscal fourth-quarter results, covering comparable sales, membership-fee income, and fuel, reported after the cash close with a call at 21:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Costco is the market-moving consumer print of the week and the first large membership-retail read after Warsh's hike, $100 oil, and 7%+ mortgages. Comps ex-fuel and membership-renewal commentary are the tells. Oppenheimer has flagged that the $6.55 EPS consensus may include tariff-refund noise; a clean beat with membership intact would argue the high-income consumer is holding, a miss with a traffic warning would be a growth-scare overlay on Friday durables.
events.ifHigher: Comps and membership beat with guide intact: COST and consumer staples bid; a quality-consumer bid into Friday.
events.ifLower: Comps miss or membership weakens: COST sold, a consumer-crack overlay on durables and Michigan.

events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the Bank of England Governor, the first after Thursday's 6-3 hold and Wednesday's UK flash PMIs.
events.whyItMatters: Bailey already said a prolonged Middle East conflict may require tighter policy. If Wednesday's services PMI held above 52, a repeat of that line would fatten November hike odds; a softer PMI plus patient colour would lock 3.75% and argue the three hike-voters stay in the minority.
events.ifHigher: Bailey leans toward a hike if energy persists: GBP bids, gilts sold.
events.ifLower: Data-dependent hold language: GBP sold, the UK cycle stays decoupled from the Fed.

events.previous: +1.1% MoM headline; +0.4% ex-transport; core capital goods +0.4% (July 2026)
events.forecast: Headline ~-0.3% to -0.5% MoM; core capital goods is the capex read
events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's Advance Report on Durable Goods: new orders for manufactured goods meant to last three years or more, including the core capital-goods line (nondefense ex-aircraft) that feeds business-investment estimates in GDP.
events.whyItMatters: July's +1.1% was part of the AI-capex boom the Committee hiked into. Consensus is a headline pullback; core capital goods is the tell. A second strong core print would argue hyperscaler demand is still running hot the morning after Costco; a miss would be the first capex crack in a post-hike tape and would map onto next Wednesday's Q2 GDP third estimate.
events.ifHigher: Headline above +0.5% with core capital goods at +0.8%+: AI capex still accelerating. USD and cyclicals bid, October odds firm.
events.ifLower: Headline below -1% or core capital goods negative: capex rolling over. Cyclicals sold, a growth overlay on Michigan.

events.event: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026 final)
events.previous: Prelim ~47.8; August final was the prior confirmed print
events.whatItIs: The University of Michigan's final monthly survey of consumer sentiment, including 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations, released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The final rarely rewrites the prelim unless inflation expectations jump. 1-year inflation expectations are the line that matters the week after a Fed hike and a week of $100 oil: a pop toward 5% would keep October odds bid; a fade would be the first household-inflation cooling Warsh can point to. This is also weekly options expiry, not monthly OpEx.
events.ifHigher: Sentiment above 50 or 1-year inflation expectations down: households looking through the hike. Modest equity bid.
events.ifLower: Sentiment below 45 or 1-year inflation expectations up: the hike and oil are hitting real incomes. Equities sold, a hawkish-and-growth-scare mix.

events.event: Plasma (XPL) Token Unlock (~$152M) + Deribit quarterly BTC/ETH options expiry
events.whatItIs: A scheduled Plasma vesting cliff of about $152 million, the largest named dollar unlock of the week, landing on the same Friday as Deribit's quarterly bitcoin and ether options expiry.
events.whyItMatters: Bitcoin reclaimed $80,000 last Friday for the first time since September 4. A large alt unlock plus quarterly options expiry is a supply-and-positioning event into a weekend after Trump-Xi. A clean absorb with BTC holding $80,000 is constructive; an unlock that pulls ETH beta into expiry is the first supply test of that reclaim.
events.ifHigher: Unlock absorbed and BTC holds $80,000 through expiry: supply was priced. Mild constructive signal into next week's PCE.
events.ifLower: XPL breaks and pulls ETH/BTC through $80,000: supply hits a thin post-summit tape. Altcoin risk-off, BTC still the relative winner.

2026-09-28.summary: RBA hike, August core PCE, and September payrolls set the October Fed path.

events.whatItIs: The National Bureau of Statistics' year-to-date profit growth for industrial firms above a designated size, the broadest monthly read on Chinese factory margins.
events.whyItMatters: Monday is a thin data open before Tuesday's RBA. Profits have been running hot on a year-to-date basis even as the official PMI sits under 50. A sharp slowdown would be the first China-demand crack into Wednesday's PMI and Thursday's National Day shutdown; a hold near the July pace keeps the post-summit tape about US data, not a China profit shock.
events.ifHigher: YTD growth holds near 17% or better: margins are absorbing $92 oil. Modest bid for industrial metals and AUD into the RBA.
events.ifLower: A drop toward single digits: factory margins are cracking. AUD and China proxies sold before Tuesday's hike.

events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the ECB President, the first high-profile euro voice of a week that ends with the September HICP flash.
events.whyItMatters: The ECB is at 2.50% and October is still a live meeting after August HICP printed 3.3%. Lagarde speaks before Spain's Tuesday flash and Friday's eurozone number. Hawkish colour would fatten October ECB odds and support the euro against a Fed that is itself a coin-flip for October 28; a patient line would sell the euro into the inflation prints.
events.ifHigher: Lagarde treats October as live or flags second-round energy effects: EUR bids, Bunds sold.
events.ifLower: Data-dependent, one-hike-and-done language: EUR sold, Bunds bid into Tuesday's Spanish CPI.

events.event: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin Speaks
events.whatItIs: A fireside chat from the Richmond Fed president, the first named FOMC voice of a week that runs through PCE, ISM, and payrolls into the October 28 decision.
events.whyItMatters: October hike odds are about 64-66% after Friday. Barkin speaks before any of this week's tier-one prints. A line that the September hike was enough would fade those odds into Tuesday's JOLTS; a line that the labour market is still too tight would firm them before Wednesday's PCE. Bowman and Cook are also on Monday's card. Barkin is the one with a clean afternoon slot.
events.ifHigher: Barkin backs another 2026 hike or stresses broad inflation: USD bids, October odds jump, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Patient, data-dependent, oil-only inflation: October odds fade, gold and duration bid.

events.event: RBA Interest Rate Decision -- cash rate, statement, Bullock press conference 05:30 UTC
events.previous: 4.35% (held June 17 and August 12; last hike May 6)
events.whatItIs: The Reserve Bank of Australia's cash-rate decision, published at 04:30 UTC, with Governor Michele Bullock's press conference an hour later.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's first policy decision and it is almost fully priced. All four major Australian banks expect 4.60%, which would be the fourth hike of 2026 and the highest cash rate since 2011. With the move priced, AUD trades the statement and Bullock: a one-and-done line fades November (markets already put a follow-up near a coin-flip by November 3), and an explicit second-hike warning bids AUD into Wednesday's August CPI, which the Board will not have seen.
events.ifHigher: A 25bp hike plus a November bias, or a surprise 50bp: AUD spikes, ASX sold, a global-hawkish overlay on Wednesday's PCE.
events.ifLower: A hold at 4.35%: the tail. AUD sold hard, rate-sensitive equities bid, a dovish shock the morning before US confidence and JOLTS.

events.whatItIs: Spain's preliminary consumer-price print, the first large euro-area national flash of the week and an early read on the energy impulse before Germany and Friday's eurozone aggregate.
events.whyItMatters: August already jumped to 4.3%, the highest since early 2023, and consensus looks for 4.7%. Spain is an energy-sensitive print. A beat would lift the bar for Friday's eurozone HICP (seen near 3.5% after 3.3%) and keep October ECB hike odds bid the same morning the RBA is expected to hike. A miss would be the first sign the fuel impulse is fading before Germany's Wednesday national figure.
events.ifHigher: Above 5.0%: energy is still accelerating in the periphery. EUR bids, Friday's eurozone bar rises.
events.ifLower: At or below 4.3%: the August jump is not extending. EUR sold into Wednesday's German CPI.

events.whatItIs: The Conference Board's monthly survey of US household confidence, including the present-situation and expectations indexes and the jobs-plentiful minus jobs-hard-to-get labour differential. Released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Confidence has been stuck just under 90 with the 10-year near 5.16% and gasoline still the household story even after WTI faded from $100 to $92.41. The labour differential inside this survey is a same-morning cross-check on JOLTS and a lead into Friday's payrolls. A drop through the mid-80s would be the growth-scare half of a week the Fed is trying to read as still-solid; a pop through 92 would say households looked through the September hike.
events.ifHigher: Above 93, with the labour differential improving: households are fine. Modest USD and equity bid into Wednesday's PCE.
events.ifLower: Below 86: confidence is cracking under the 5% 10-year. Equities sold, a growth overlay on Friday's payrolls.

events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey: vacancies, hires, and quits, released at 14:00 UTC with a one-month lag.
events.whyItMatters: August payrolls surprised at +162K and the unemployment rate is 4.1%, the rate the FOMC now pencils in for the end of 2026. JOLTS is the demand side of that story, two sessions before ADP and three before the September employment report. A drop toward 7.0 million would say the payrolls bounce is not being matched by new vacancies and would fade October hike odds. A hold above 7.3 million would tell the Committee the labour market they hiked into is still tight.
events.ifHigher: Above 7.4 million: labour demand still firm. USD bids, October odds firm, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Below 7.0 million: vacancies are rolling over. Duration and gold bid, a softer setup for Friday's NFP.

events.event: Fed's Austan Goolsbee and John Williams Speak
events.whatItIs: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee in a moderated discussion at 17:00 UTC, then New York Fed President John Williams with keynote remarks at 18:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Williams runs the desk that implements policy and Goolsbee has been on the less-hawkish side of a Committee that just hiked unanimously. They speak after JOLTS and the day before PCE. Any pushback on the 64-66% October odds, or a fresh insistence that another hike is the base case, will reprice the front end before Wednesday's inflation print. The rest of the week's speaker list is crowded. These two are the ones that can move it.
events.ifHigher: Williams or Goolsbee leans into another hike: USD bids, the October meeting stays live.
events.ifLower: Both sound patient and data-dependent: October odds fade into PCE.

events.forecast: Fuel-led firming; no single consensus pinned
events.whatItIs: The Australian Bureau of Statistics' monthly CPI indicator, covering about three quarters of the quarterly basket, released at 01:30 UTC the morning after the RBA decision.
events.whyItMatters: The Board is expected to hike on Tuesday without this print. Wednesday's number is the first test of whether November is live. July's easing to 3.5%, with trimmed mean stuck at 3.6%, is what made a September move a debate rather than a formality. A re-acceleration, especially in trimmed mean, would validate the hike and bid AUD into the November 3 meeting. A further slide would make Tuesday's hike look like the last one even if the statement sounded open.
events.ifHigher: Headline back toward 3.8% or trimmed mean above 3.6%: the hike is validated and November stays live. AUD bids.
events.ifLower: Headline under 3.3% with trimmed mean easing: Tuesday's hike is the cycle top. AUD sold.

events.event: China NBS Manufacturing and Non-Manufacturing PMI (September 2026)
events.whatItIs: The official purchasing managers' indexes from the National Bureau of Statistics, released at 01:30 UTC. The private RatingDog (Caixin) manufacturing PMI follows at 01:45 UTC, prior 51.5.
events.whyItMatters: Official manufacturing has been in contraction. Consensus looks for a return to just above 50, while the private survey has been the firmer one. This is the last China activity print before onshore markets shut for National Day on Thursday, and it lands hours after an expected RBA hike. A miss back toward 49 would sell AUD, copper, and China proxies into a holiday-thinned Asia tape. A clean 50-plus on both official and private surveys would say the post-summit demand picture is stabilising.
events.ifHigher: Manufacturing above 50.5 and RatingDog holding above 51.5: the contraction is over. AUD, metals, and China equity futures bid.
events.ifLower: Manufacturing back under 49.5: the official sector is still shrinking into a holiday week. China proxies sold.

events.previous: August national print already fed the 3.3% eurozone HICP flash
events.forecast: Another energy-led rise, into Friday's eurozone flash
events.whatItIs: Destatis's flash estimate of German consumer prices, including the harmonised HICP that is the largest input to Friday's eurozone aggregate. State figures drip out through the morning. The national number is around midday UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Germany is the swing factor in Friday's eurozone print, which consensus puts near 3.5% after 3.3%. A hot national figure the morning of US PCE would be a two-inflation-region shock: Bunds and Treasuries sold together, the euro bid, and October hike odds firmer on both sides of the Atlantic. A soft German number would take the pressure off Friday and leave Wednesday's tape to the Fed's preferred gauge.
events.ifHigher: A clear upside surprise versus the state-level run-rate: EUR bids, Bunds sold, Friday's 3.5% eurozone bar rises.
events.ifLower: A soft national print: the energy impulse is fading in the core. EUR sold into Friday, October ECB odds fade.

events.forecast: About +70K (surveys run from the high 50s to the mid 80s)
events.whatItIs: ADP's private-sector payroll estimate, released at 12:15 UTC, 15 minutes before the PCE and GDP bundle and two days before the Bureau of Labor Statistics report.
events.whyItMatters: August ADP was a soft +38K next to a strong +162K official payrolls print, so the gap itself is the story. Consensus for September is a bounce, but the range across desks is wide. A negative ADP would spook Friday's NFP positioning before traders have even seen core PCE. A print near +100K would say the official consensus of +100K is the right neighbourhood. Treat it as a positioning tell, not a substitute for Friday.
events.ifHigher: Above +100K: private hiring rebounded. USD bids, Friday's +100K bar looks light.
events.ifLower: Below +20K or negative: the soft August ADP was the trend. Friday NFP risk turns down, gold bid.

events.event: PCE Price Index, Personal Income and Spending (August 2026)
events.previous: Headline +0.2% MoM / +3.7% YoY; core +0.2% MoM / +3.3% YoY (July 2026)
events.forecast: Headline +0.4% MoM / 3.7% YoY; core +0.3% MoM / 3.3% YoY; income about +0.5%; spending about +0.8%
events.actual: Headline +0.3% MoM / +3.4% YoY; core +0.2% MoM / +3.0% YoY; income +0.2%; spending +0.9%
events.whatItIs: The BEA Personal Income and Outlays report, including the PCE price index the Fed targets, released at 12:30 UTC in the same window as the Q2 GDP third estimate.
events.whyItMatters: This is the inflation print that matters for October 28. Core is expected to accelerate to +0.3% on the month while the annual rate holds at 3.3%, still well above 2%, and headline is expected at +0.4% as the earlier oil spike shows up in the August basket. Spending is seen rebounding to about +0.8%. A 0.4% core print would push October hike odds through 70% with payrolls still to come. A 0.2% core print would tell the Committee the September hike is still working and would fade those odds before Friday.
events.ifHigher: Core at +0.4% MoM or the annual rate above 3.3%: disinflation stalled. USD bids, gold sold, October odds jump.
events.ifLower: Core at +0.2% or below, annual rate slipping: the hike is getting traction. Gold and duration bid, October odds fade.

events.whatItIs: The BEA's third estimate of second-quarter GDP growth, released at 12:30 UTC in the same tick as August PCE.
events.whyItMatters: This is a backward-looking confirmation. The live number in the morning bundle is PCE. A surprise revision of Q2 growth well away from 1.5% would still move the dollar for a few minutes, because it changes the starting point for the second-half pace the Committee just hiked into. Absent that, traders will look through it to core PCE and Friday's payrolls.
events.ifHigher: Revised to 2.0% or above: the first half was stronger than thought. Modest USD bid, a growth overlay on a hot PCE.
events.ifLower: Revised below 1.0%: the pre-hike economy was softer. A growth-scare bid for duration if PCE is also cool.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending September 25)
events.previous: +3.0 million barrels (week ending September 18; stocks 426.4 million, about 2% above the five-year average)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly change in commercial crude stocks, excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, released at 14:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: WTI settled Friday at $92.41 after a fade from the prior Friday's $100.30 October settlement. Last week's report was a surprise build of 3.0 million barrels against a draw that analysts had looked for, with refineries slowing to 94% of capacity. Another build would lean on a crude market that has already given back the spike. A large draw would put $95 back in play the same afternoon Micron reports, and would feed the inflation story Thursday's ISM prices-paid index is about to update.
events.ifHigher: A build of 3 million barrels or more: the surplus is growing. WTI sold, a small relief bid for duration.
events.ifLower: A draw of 2 million barrels or more: the fade from $100 stalls. WTI bids, inflation-sensitive equities soften.

events.whatItIs: Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter results, the AI-memory read of the week, reported after the US cash close. Consensus is about $50.8 billion of revenue and about $31.50 of EPS after a fiscal third quarter that did $41.5 billion of revenue.
events.whyItMatters: Micron is the cleanest large-cap read on whether AI memory pricing is still tightening. The stock has been a major 2026 winner and options were pricing a move of about 8% either way into the print. Guidance on high-bandwidth memory, data-center revenue, and gross margin will move the Nasdaq the same evening core PCE has reset October Fed odds. A beat with a raise extends the AI bid into Thursday's ISM. A guide-down is the first fundamental crack in that bid since the Nasdaq's Tuesday record.
events.ifHigher: Revenue and margin above the bar with HBM guidance raised: chips bid, a risk-on overnight into ISM.
events.ifLower: A miss or a margin guide-down: the AI-memory trade de-rates. SOX sold, a growth overlay on Thursday.

events.whatItIs: The Bank of Japan's quarterly business survey, released at 23:50 UTC on October 1. Large manufacturers' index and the outlook index are the lines markets trade.
events.whyItMatters: The BoJ hiked to 1.25% on September 18, the highest policy rate since 1995, and the yen's reaction was soft. Tankan is the first broad corporate read since that hike and it lands after US PCE and Micron, before Thursday's cash open in Tokyo. A strong capex and price-plans reading would revive talk of another BoJ move and bid the yen. A slump in the outlook index would say firms are already feeling 1.25% plus a still-firm oil bill, and would sell the yen into Friday's Tokyo CPI.
events.ifHigher: Large manufacturers above 26 with firm capex plans: the hike is being absorbed. JPY bids, Nikkei supported.
events.ifLower: Index back under 20, or outlook well below the current index: the hike is biting. JPY sold, Nikkei softer.

events.event: China National Day -- onshore markets closed through at least October 5
events.whatItIs: The start of China's National Day holiday. Onshore equities, bonds, and the RMB cash session are shut from Thursday October 1 through at least Monday October 5.
events.whyItMatters: Wednesday's PMI is the last China print desks will be able to trade onshore. Thursday and Friday's US data, ISM and payrolls, will hit a market without a China cash response until the following week. CNH and China ADRs will do the work in the meantime. Thin Asia liquidity also means the yen and AUD will carry more of the regional reaction to Tankan, Tokyo CPI, and Friday's NFP.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- market holiday.
events.ifLower: N/A -- market holiday.

events.whatItIs: Accenture's fiscal fourth-quarter results, released before the US cash open, the enterprise-IT and consulting read on AI project spending.
events.whyItMatters: Accenture is the demand side of the AI trade Micron just reported from the supply side. Bookings, generative-AI revenue, and the fiscal 2027 guide land the morning of ISM manufacturing. A strong bookings number would say companies are still writing cheques for AI implementation. A soft guide would say the enterprise buyer is slowing even if memory pricing is tight, which is a different and more worrying crack.
events.ifHigher: Bookings and AI revenue beat with a firm guide: IT services and the broader AI complex bid into ISM.
events.ifLower: A guide-down or weak bookings: the buyer is slowing. Software and services sold, a demand overlay on ISM new orders.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of first-time unemployment filings, released at 12:30 UTC, the last labour print before Friday's employment report.
events.whyItMatters: Claims have been sitting under 200K, which is the tight-labour half of the story that let the Fed hike in September. A jump toward 230K the day before payrolls would tell traders the +100K consensus is too high and would bid bonds into ISM. Another sub-200K print would confirm the labour market the Committee called solid and would keep Friday's risk on the wage and unemployment lines rather than the headline job count.
events.ifHigher: Above 230K: the first real crack. Gold and duration bid, Friday's NFP bar drops, October odds fade.
events.ifLower: Below 190K: still tight. USD bids, the hike looks validated heading into payrolls.

events.whatItIs: The Institute for Supply Management's factory survey, released at 14:00 UTC. Above 50 is expansion. Prices paid, new orders, and employment are the sub-indexes that move markets. S&P Global's final manufacturing PMI is at 13:45 UTC. The flash was 57.0.
events.whyItMatters: Factories are already expanding, and the flash survey jumped to a multi-year high at 57.0. Consensus for ISM is a smaller step up, to 55.0 from 54.6. The line that matters for October 28 is prices paid, which was 71.1 in August: a fresh rise says the oil shock is still in the goods pipeline the day before payrolls, and a drop toward the mid-60s says it is cooling. Employment inside ISM is the other tell, because Friday's consensus is a slowdown from +162K to about +100K.
events.ifHigher: Headline above 56 with prices paid still above 70: activity and inflation together. USD bids, October odds firm, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Headline under 53, or prices paid down sharply: the factory boom is cooling. Cyclicals sold, a softer setup for NFP.

events.whatItIs: Nike's fiscal first-quarter results, reported after the US cash close the night before nonfarm payrolls. Consensus is about $0.44 of EPS and about $11.3 billion of revenue.
events.whyItMatters: Nike is the global consumer print of the week, and the stock has been in a long drawdown, trading near $38 after leaving the S&P 100 on September 21. Greater China, gross margin, and the wholesale-versus-DTC mix are the lines. A China miss the week Xi sat with Trump, and the week China starts a holiday, would say the truce has not fixed demand. A margin beat would say the turnaround is showing up in the numbers the same night traders are setting NFP risk.
events.ifHigher: Revenue and margin beat with a steadier China line: NKE and global consumer discretionary bid overnight.
events.ifLower: A China or margin miss: NKE sold, a consumer-crack overlay on Friday morning's payrolls.

events.whatItIs: The Tokyo-area consumer price index, released at 23:30 UTC on Friday October 2. It leads the national CPI by about three weeks. Ex-fresh food is the BoJ's core.
events.whyItMatters: Tokyo CPI lands after Tankan and hours before US payrolls, so it is the yen's own inflation print on NFP day. A jump from 1.8% toward 2.4% on the ex-fresh-food measure would say the BoJ's hike to 1.25% has not cooled prices and would bid the yen into the US number. A stick at 1.8% would say September's hike is already enough and would sell the yen if payrolls are hot.
events.ifHigher: Ex-fresh food above 2.5%: Tokyo prices re-accelerated. JPY bids, another BoJ move stays in the conversation.
events.ifLower: Ex-fresh food at or below 1.8%: the hike is working. JPY sold into a hot NFP.

events.forecast: Headline about +3.5% YoY; core about +2.6% YoY
events.actual: Headline +3.8% YoY; core +2.5% YoY; energy +18.8% YoY
events.whatItIs: Eurostat's flash estimate of euro-area inflation, released at 09:00 UTC, including core HICP which excludes energy, food, alcohol, and tobacco.
events.whyItMatters: August's 3.3% flash is why October is still a live ECB meeting after the hike to 2.50%. Consensus looks for a further rise toward 3.5%, with core edging to about 2.6% from 2.4%. The print lands three and a half hours before US payrolls, so a hot eurozone number and a hot NFP would be a same-morning global inflation shock. A 3.3% or softer headline would take October ECB odds down before New York opens and would leave Friday's tape to the US labour market.
events.ifHigher: Headline above 3.7% or core at 2.8% or higher: energy is leaking into core. EUR bids, Bunds sold, October ECB odds jump.
events.ifLower: Headline at 3.3% or below and core unmoved at 2.4%: the August pop is not extending. EUR sold, October ECB odds fade.
events.learnMore:
Eurostat's flash HICP arrives at the end of the reference month, about two weeks before the final. Headline is the full basket and the ECB's target measure. Core strips energy, food, alcohol, and tobacco so the Council can see whether pressure is spreading beyond fuel. Services inflation is the line inside core that has kept the hawks in the conversation all year.

September's setup is another energy month. Spain's Tuesday flash and Germany's Wednesday national print will already have told traders most of the headline surprise. What the aggregate still adds is the core and services mix across the bloc. A headline rise to 3.5% that is entirely energy, with core stuck at 2.4%, is a different ECB meeting from a 3.5% headline with core at 2.7%. The first can be waited out. The second is the second-round effect the Council has said would justify another hike. Because US payrolls follow at 12:30 UTC, euro rates may only get a few hours to trade the number on their own before the dollar takes over the afternoon.

events.event: Nonfarm Payrolls, Unemployment Rate, Average Hourly Earnings (September 2026)
events.previous: +162K payrolls; unemployment 4.1%; average hourly earnings +0.3% MoM (August 2026)
events.forecast: +100K payrolls; private payrolls about +100K; unemployment 4.1%; average hourly earnings +0.3% MoM
events.actual: +29K payrolls; private +46K; unemployment 4.2%; average hourly earnings +0.1% MoM / +3.0% YoY; July -10K; August +133K
events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' Employment Situation report, released at 12:30 UTC: nonfarm payrolls, the unemployment rate, average hourly earnings, and the workweek.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's fulcrum for the October 28 FOMC. Consensus is a slowdown to about +100K from August's +162K, with unemployment steady at 4.1%, the rate officials just wrote into the end-2026 forecast, and wages at +0.3% again. The Chicago Fed's real-time unemployment estimate for September was about 4.13%. A repeat of August, something near +160K with wages at +0.4%, would push October hike odds well through the 64-66% Friday left them at. A print near the recent three-month average, closer to +70K, or a 4.3% unemployment rate, would tell the Committee the September hike is landing on a cooling labour market and would fade those odds into a China-holiday Friday.
events.ifHigher: Payrolls above +150K, or wages at +0.4% with unemployment at 4.0% or lower: the labour market is not cooling. USD bids, gold sold, October odds jump.
events.ifLower: Payrolls below +50K, or unemployment at 4.3% or higher: the August bounce was noise. Gold and duration bid, October odds fade hard.

2026-10-05.summary: FOMC minutes, ISM services, and PepsiCo plus Delta headline a post-payrolls week.

events.event: OPEC+ Ministerial Meeting -- November output quotas
events.previous: October output held at September levels (Sep 6 meeting)
events.whatItIs: A virtual meeting of the seven core OPEC+ producers (Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, Oman) to set November required production.
events.whyItMatters: The group held October output flat on September 6 after six monthly increases. Delegates have been pointing to another hold for November while the Iran war keeps millions of barrels shut in through Hormuz. WTI faded from last week's $100 handle toward the high $80s into payrolls. A hold leaves the oil tape to inventories and geopolitics. A surprise raise would be the first extra barrels into a still-disrupted Strait.
events.ifHigher: A production increase: more barrels on paper. WTI sold, a small relief bid for duration and risk.
events.ifLower: A cut, or language that November supply stays tight: WTI bids, the inflation overlay on Wednesday's minutes stays live.

events.event: China Golden Week -- onshore markets closed through October 7
events.whatItIs: The remainder of China's National Day holiday. Onshore equities, bonds, and the RMB cash session stay shut Monday through Wednesday, with trading set to resume Thursday October 8.
events.whyItMatters: Monday's ISM services, Tuesday's trade data, and Wednesday's FOMC minutes all print without a China cash response. CNH and China ADRs will do the work until Thursday. Thin Asia liquidity also means the yen and AUD will carry more of the regional reaction to Ueda, German orders, and the HYPE unlock.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- market holiday.
events.ifLower: N/A -- market holiday.

events.whatItIs: S&P Global's final euro-area services purchasing managers' index, combining the national finals from Germany, France, Italy, and Spain. Above 50 is expansion.
events.whyItMatters: The flash already said services are expanding at 53.0 after a 25bp ECB hike to 2.50% in September. Final revisions are usually small. A downward revision toward 52 would be the first activity crack after Friday's 3.8% eurozone HICP flash. An upward revision would keep the ECB's second-hike case alive into Thursday's accounts.
events.ifHigher: Final above 53.5: services stronger than the flash. EUR bids, Bunds sold.
events.ifLower: Final at 52.0 or below: the flash overstated the expansion. EUR sold into Tuesday's retail sales.

events.whatItIs: Eurostat's producer price index for the euro area, the factory-gate inflation print that leads consumer prices by one to two months.
events.whyItMatters: Friday's HICP flash jumped to 3.8% year over year on an 18.8% energy spike. A 1.9% monthly PPI rise would say that impulse is still in the pipeline the ECB hiked into, and would keep October as a live meeting. A miss back toward 1.0% would be the first sign factory prices are cooling after the fuel shock.
events.ifHigher: Above 2.2% MoM: pipeline inflation is still accelerating. EUR bids, Bunds sold, October ECB odds firm.
events.ifLower: At 1.0% or below: the energy impulse is fading at the factory gate. EUR sold, October ECB odds fade.

events.event: S&P Global US Services PMI Final (September 2026)
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's final US services PMI, the private-survey counterpart to ISM, covering a broader small-firm sample. The flash was 58.7, a five-year high.
events.whyItMatters: The flash said services were expanding at the fastest pace in over five years even as Friday's payrolls slowed to 29,000. Final revisions are usually tenths. A drop toward 57 would narrow the gap with ISM before the 14:00 print. A hold at 58.7 would leave ISM as the one that has to explain why the two surveys disagree.
events.ifHigher: Final above 59: the flash was not a one-month spike. Modest USD bid into ISM.
events.ifLower: Final at 57 or below: the flash overstated September. A softer setup for ISM 15 minutes later.

events.whatItIs: The Institute for Supply Management's services composite, released at 14:00 UTC. Above 50 is expansion. Prices paid, new orders, and employment are the sub-indexes that move markets.
events.whyItMatters: This is Monday's fulcrum and the first activity check after Friday's 29,000 payrolls print. Services are about 80% of GDP. August's 55.4 was firm, but employment inside the survey was already contracting at 47.8 and prices paid was 72.6, the hottest since 2022. Consensus is a small step down to about 55.0. A hold above 55 with prices still near 70 would say the labour miss has not hit the dominant sector and would keep October 28 in play. A drop toward 53 with employment still under 50 would confirm Friday's cooling and fade those odds before Wednesday's minutes.
events.ifHigher: Headline above 56 with prices paid still above 70: activity and inflation together. USD bids, October odds firm, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Headline under 53, or employment still under 48 with prices cooling: the services boom is rolling over. Gold and duration bid, a softer setup for the minutes.

events.whatItIs: Westpac and the Melbourne Institute's monthly survey of Australian household confidence, released at 23:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The RBA hiked 25bp to 4.60% last Tuesday, a 15-year high. This is the first household-confidence read after that move. September already dropped 5.2% to 84.4. Another slide would say households felt the hike immediately and would sell AUD into a China-holiday Asia tape. A bounce would say the hike was absorbed.
events.ifHigher: Index back above 86: households looked through 4.60%. AUD bids.
events.ifLower: Index under 82, or another 4%+ monthly drop: the hike is landing on weak morale. AUD sold.

events.whatItIs: A scheduled Hyperliquid (HYPE) vesting release estimated around $856 million, the largest named dollar unlock of October and of this week.
events.whyItMatters: This is an order of magnitude larger than a typical weekly unlock. Bitcoin has been holding the mid-$80,000s after Friday's payrolls miss. An $856 million cliff is a supply event the alt tape has to absorb on the same day Williams and Bowman speak. A clean hold in HYPE and BTC is constructive. A break that pulls ETH beta is the first supply test of the post-payrolls crypto bid.
events.ifHigher: HYPE absorbs the unlock and BTC holds the mid-$80,000s: demand matched the supply. Constructive for alts overnight.
events.ifLower: HYPE breaks and pulls ETH beta: the overhang hits a thin Tuesday tape. Altcoin risk-off, BTC relatively more resilient.

events.whatItIs: Destatis's monthly survey of new manufacturing orders in Germany, the demand-side lead on Wednesday's industrial production print.
events.whyItMatters: July jumped 2.5% after three months of gains. Consensus looks for a 0.9% give-back in August. A deeper drop would say the factory rebound is stalling the morning before industrial production, and would sell the euro into Tuesday's retail sales. A surprise hold in positive territory would keep the German activity bid alive after Friday's hot HICP.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.5%: the July rebound is extending. EUR bids, German cyclicals supported.
events.ifLower: Below -2.0%: orders are rolling over. EUR sold, a softer setup for Wednesday's IP.

events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the Bank of Japan Governor, the first named BoJ voice since the September 18 hike to 1.25%.
events.whyItMatters: The BoJ lifted to 1.25%, the highest policy rate since 1995, and the yen's reaction was soft. Ueda speaks into a China-holiday Asia tape and before Williams. Any line that another hike is live would bid the yen. A patient, data-dependent tone would sell it, especially if he treats last week's Tankan as enough confirmation that 1.25% is being absorbed.
events.ifHigher: Ueda treats another 2026 hike as live or flags sticky prices: JPY bids, Nikkei softer.
events.ifLower: Patient, one-and-done language: JPY sold, a dovish overlay on Tuesday's US speakers.

events.whatItIs: S&P Global's UK construction purchasing managers' index. Above 50 is expansion. The UK has been in contraction for months.
events.whyItMatters: Construction is the weak UK sector heading into Bailey's Thursday speech. Consensus looks for a small bounce to 45.4, still deep in contraction. A drop back through 44 would be another housing-and-rates hit after 7%-plus UK mortgage costs. A jump toward 48 would be the first sign the BoE's hold at 3.75% is feeding through to building.
events.ifHigher: Above 48: the contraction is easing. GBP bids, UK homebuilders supported.
events.ifLower: At 43 or below: construction is still shrinking. GBP sold into Bailey on Thursday.

events.whatItIs: Eurostat's monthly change in euro-area retail sales volumes, the main official read on household spending across the bloc.
events.whyItMatters: July fell 0.6%. Consensus looks for a 0.4% bounce in August, the first consumer print after the ECB's second hike to 2.50%. A miss back into negative territory would say households are already feeling 2.50% plus 3.8% inflation, and would fade October ECB odds. A beat above 0.7% would say the consumer is still spending through the hikes.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.7% MoM: the July drop was noise. EUR bids, European retailers supported.
events.ifLower: Another decline, or below -0.2%: the consumer is rolling over. EUR sold, October ECB odds fade.

events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau and BEA goods-and-services trade balance for August, released at 12:30 UTC. Exports, imports, and the goods deficit are the lines inside.
events.whyItMatters: July's deficit was $88.6 billion. Consensus looks for a wider $89.8 billion hole as imports outpace exports. This is a second-tier print next to ISM and the minutes, but a blowout toward $100 billion would be a dollar-and-growth tell into Williams at 13:05 UTC. A narrower deficit would be a small USD bid on the export side.
events.ifHigher: Deficit narrower than $85B: exports held up. Modest USD bid.
events.ifLower: Deficit wider than $95B: imports surged or exports slumped. USD mixed, a growth overlay on the speakers.

events.event: New York Fed President John Williams Speaks
events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the New York Fed president, who runs the desk that implements policy, at 13:05 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Williams is the most important named voice before Wednesday's minutes. He speaks after ISM and before Bowman. Payrolls at 29,000 and core PCE at 3.0% have pulled October 28 hike odds down. A line that the September hike was enough would confirm that fade. A line that inflation is still too high, or that one print does not make a trend, would re-open October before the minutes recap a more hawkish room.
events.ifHigher: Williams backs another 2026 hike or stresses broad inflation: USD bids, October odds jump, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Patient, data-dependent, labour-cooling language: October odds fade further, gold and duration bid.

events.event: Fed Vice Chair Michelle Bowman Speaks
events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the Vice Chair for Supervision at 14:45 UTC, the second named Board voice of Tuesday.
events.whyItMatters: Bowman speaks 90 minutes after Williams. If the two disagree -- Williams patient, Bowman still hawkish, or the reverse -- the minutes become a two-camp document rather than a recap of a united September hike. She has been on the hawkish side of bank-regulation questions. Any macro line on October 28 will be parsed as a Board signal, not a regional one.
events.ifHigher: Bowman treats October as live or flags sticky services prices: USD bids, a hawkish overlay on Wednesday's minutes.
events.ifLower: Supervision-only, or a data-dependent macro line: October odds stay down, gold bid.

events.event: Constellation Brands (STZ) Fiscal Q2 2027 Earnings (after close)
events.whatItIs: Constellation Brands' fiscal second-quarter results, the beer-and-spirits consumer print of the week, reported after the US cash close. Consensus is about $3.55 of EPS and $2.54 billion of revenue.
events.whyItMatters: STZ is the first large consumer staple of Q3 season, a day before Levi's and two days before PepsiCo. US beer volumes, Modelo, and the Mexico supply chain are the lines. A miss on US beer would say the high-7% mortgage and 4.2% unemployment household is trading down before Thursday's PepsiCo print. A beat would be the first sign the consumer is still buying premium.
events.ifHigher: EPS and US beer volumes beat: STZ and consumer staples bid overnight.
events.ifLower: A US beer miss or a guide-down: STZ sold, a consumer-crack overlay on PepsiCo Thursday.

events.event: API Weekly Crude Oil Stock Change (week ending October 2)
events.whatItIs: The American Petroleum Institute's unofficial weekly estimate of US commercial crude stocks, released at 20:30 UTC, the day before the EIA report.
events.whyItMatters: API sets the positioning for Wednesday's 14:30 UTC EIA print. Last week's API was a 1.0 million-barrel build. Another build would lean on a crude market that has already given back the $100 handle. A large draw would put $95 back in play overnight into EIA and the minutes.
events.ifHigher: A build of 3 million barrels or more: the surplus is growing. WTI sold overnight.
events.ifLower: A draw of 2 million barrels or more: the fade from $100 stalls. WTI bids into EIA.

events.whatItIs: Destatis's monthly industrial production index for Germany, covering manufacturing, mining, and energy. Tuesday's factory orders are the demand lead.
events.whyItMatters: July fell 1.1%. Consensus looks for a 1.4% rebound in August. A miss would confirm that the factory rebound is stalling the same morning EIA and the FOMC minutes dominate New York. A beat above 2% would be a European activity offset to Friday's hot HICP, and would bid the euro into the US session.
events.ifHigher: Above +2.0% MoM: German industry is recovering. EUR bids, European cyclicals supported.
events.ifLower: Another decline, or below 0%: the July drop is extending. EUR sold, a growth overlay on the minutes.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending October 2)
events.previous: +0.92 million barrels (week ending September 25; stocks 427.3 million)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly change in commercial crude stocks, excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, released at 14:30 UTC. Gasoline and distillate stocks print in the same report.
events.whyItMatters: WTI faded from last week's $100 handle toward the high $80s into payrolls. Last week's official print was a 0.92 million-barrel build, with stocks at 427.3 million. Another build would lean on a market that is already giving back the Hormuz spike, hours before the FOMC minutes. A large draw would put $95 back in play and would feed the inflation story the minutes are about to recap.
events.ifHigher: A build of 3 million barrels or more: the surplus is growing. WTI sold, a small relief bid for duration into the minutes.
events.ifLower: A draw of 2 million barrels or more: the fade from $100 stalls. WTI bids, inflation-sensitive equities soften into 18:00 UTC.

events.whatItIs: The Federal Reserve's detailed record of the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, released three weeks after the decision at 18:00 UTC, covering the debate behind the 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's fulcrum. The Committee hiked for the first time since 2023, Chair Kevin Warsh sounded hawkish on inflation, and the projections showed most participants wanted at least one more 2026 move. The catch is staleness: August core PCE printed 3.0% year over year and September payrolls printed 29,000 with 4.2% unemployment after that meeting. Markets have already pulled October 28 hike odds down. A hawkish recap can reprice the front end for an hour. The durable question is whether a 'sizable number' still wanted another hike, or whether the centre was already data-dependent.
events.ifHigher: Minutes show broad sympathy for a second 2026 hike, or Warsh leaning that way: October odds reprice higher. USD bids, gold and BTC sold.
events.ifLower: Minutes show the hike was a close call and the centre wanted to wait: October odds fade further. Gold and duration bid, USD sold.

events.whatItIs: PepsiCo's third-quarter results, the large-cap consumer staple that opens Q3 season proper, released before the US cash open. Consensus is about $2.30 of EPS and $24.97 billion of revenue. Options were pricing a move of about 3.9%.
events.whyItMatters: PepsiCo is the pricing-power print of the week. Organic volume, Frito-Lay margin, and the overseas mix land the same morning as jobless claims. A volume miss next to a price beat would say households are still paying more for fewer bags, the mix that keeps services inflation sticky into next week's CPI. A clean volume beat would be the first sign the 4.2% unemployment consumer is still buying. Delta follows Friday.
events.ifHigher: Revenue and organic volume beat with margin held: PEP and staples bid, a consumer-resilience overlay on claims.
events.ifLower: A volume miss or a margin guide-down: PEP sold, a consumer-crack overlay on Friday's Delta and Michigan.
events.learnMore:
PepsiCo reports as a single print covering Frito-Lay North America, beverages, and the overseas snack businesses. The line markets trade first is organic volume versus price. A company that is still raising prices while volumes fall is passing inflation through to households. That is supportive for nominal sales and uncomfortable for the Fed, because it is the same mechanism that keeps core services sticky. A company that is holding volume and giving up price is the disinflation mix.

Q3 is the first full quarter after the September hike and after oil spent weeks near or above $90. Input costs for frying oil, packaging, and freight are the margin tell. Guidance on 2026 net revenue and core operating margin will move the staple complex more than the penny on EPS. The stock is a $170 billion name, so the tape impact is broader than STZ on Tuesday. Treat it as the consumer read heading into next Wednesday's CPI, not as a single-name event.

events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the Bank of England Governor, the first named BoE voice of the week, at 12:15 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The BoE held at 3.75% on September 17 on a 6-3 split. Construction PMI is still in the mid-40s and UK house prices are soft. Bailey speaks the same morning as PepsiCo and claims. A line that another hike is live would bid sterling. A patient, labour-cooling tone would sell it, especially if he treats the September hold as the peak.
events.ifHigher: Bailey treats another 2026 hike as live or flags sticky UK services prices: GBP bids, gilts sold.
events.ifLower: Patient, data-dependent, or peak-rate language: GBP sold, gilts bid.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of first-time unemployment filings, released at 12:30 UTC, plus continuing claims for the week ending September 26.
events.whyItMatters: Claims have been sitting under 200K even as Friday's payrolls slowed to 29,000. That split -- still-low weekly filings, weak monthly hiring -- is the labour story the minutes recapped.
