A jump toward 230K would be the first weekly confirmation that the 29,000 print was a trend, and would fade October 28 odds further. Another sub-200K print would say layoffs have not started and would keep the debate on hiring, not firing, into next week's CPI.
events.ifHigher: Above 230K: the first real crack in weekly filings. Gold and duration bid, October odds fade.
events.ifLower: Below 190K: still tight. USD bids, the 29,000 payrolls print looks like a one-month miss.

events.event: Delta Air Lines (DAL) Q3 2026 Earnings (before open)
events.whatItIs: Delta's third-quarter results, the first large US airline of earnings season, released before the US cash open. Consensus is about $1.88 of EPS and $17.62 billion of revenue. Options were pricing a move of about 7%.
events.whyItMatters: Delta is the premium-travel and fuel-cost print of the week. Unit revenue, corporate travel, and the jet-fuel line land the morning after PepsiCo and the same session as Michigan sentiment. A unit-revenue miss would say the high-fare consumer is cracking. A beat with fuel guidance that does not blow up would be a risk-on open into a quiet Friday. WTI in the high $80s to $90s is the cost overlay the company cannot control.
events.ifHigher: Unit revenue and EPS beat with fuel guidance contained: DAL and transports bid, a consumer-resilience open.
events.ifLower: A unit-revenue miss or a fuel-cost warning: DAL sold, a travel-demand overlay on Michigan at 14:00 UTC.

events.whatItIs: Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey: employment change, the unemployment rate, and participation, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the first full month of Canadian jobs data since US Section 338 tariffs took effect on August 22. August lost about 42,000 jobs with unemployment stuck at 6.4%. RBC looks for a modest 5,000 rebound and a steady 6.4% rate. A second decline, or unemployment at 6.6%, would say the tariff hit is showing up in hiring and would sell the loonie into a WTI tape that has already faded. A bounce above +25K would say domestic demand is offsetting the trade shock.
events.ifHigher: Jobs above +25K with unemployment at 6.3% or below: the tariff hit is not in the labour market yet. CAD bids.
events.ifLower: Another decline, or unemployment at 6.6%+: tariffs are landing on hiring. CAD sold, oil-linked Canada names softer.

events.event: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (October preliminary)
events.whatItIs: The University of Michigan's preliminary October survey of household confidence, including 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations, released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Sentiment has been sitting near the lows around 48 after September's drop from 51.7. The inflation-expectation lines are the ones the Fed still reads: 4.6% at one year and 3.4% at five years. A jump in 5-year expectations toward 3.6% would be a hawkish overlay on next Wednesday's CPI. A drop in the headline toward 45 would confirm that 4.2% unemployment and 7% mortgages are hitting morale into a quiet Friday.
events.ifHigher: Headline above 51, or 5-year expectations down to 3.2%: households are stabilising. Modest equity bid, a calmer setup for next week's CPI.
events.ifLower: Headline under 46, or 5-year expectations at 3.6%+: morale is cracking or inflation psychology is worsening. Equities sold, a hawkish overlay on October 14 CPI.

2026-10-12.summary: September CPI, JPMorgan-led bank earnings, and Warsh at the IMF.

events.event: Columbus Day -- US bond market closed (NYSE and Nasdaq open)
events.whatItIs: A US federal holiday. The Treasury market, Fedwire, and most government statistical releases are shut. NYSE and Nasdaq stay open.
events.whyItMatters: Bond-market closure thins the rate tape the day before bank earnings and two sessions before CPI. Equities still trade, so index futures can gap on geopolitics or Asia without a cash Treasury bid to absorb it. EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report is delayed to Thursday 16:00 UTC because of the holiday.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- market holiday.
events.ifLower: N/A -- market holiday.

events.event: Canada Thanksgiving Day -- TSX and Canadian cash markets closed
events.whatItIs: Canadian Thanksgiving. The TSX, Canadian bond market, and CAD cash session are shut.
events.whyItMatters: Friday's Canada jobs report lost 68,300 positions with unemployment at 6.5%. There is no onshore CAD response until Tuesday. Oil-linked Canada names in New York will do the work, and Governor Macklem speaks into Wednesday's US CPI from the IMF meetings.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- market holiday.
events.ifLower: N/A -- market holiday.

events.event: Japan Sports Day -- Tokyo cash markets closed
events.whatItIs: A Japanese national holiday. The TSE, OSE, and onshore JGB session are shut. Japan PPI prints Tuesday morning (23:50 UTC Monday).
events.whyItMatters: A closed Tokyo cash tape leaves the yen and Nikkei futures to absorb any IMF or oil headline overnight. Tuesday's 7.6% PPI reprint is the first Japan inflation read of the week once the cash market reopens.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- market holiday.
events.ifLower: N/A -- market holiday.

events.event: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack Speaks (NABE)
events.whatItIs: A keynote at the National Association for Business Economics annual meeting in Cleveland. Hammack is a 2026 FOMC voter.
events.whyItMatters: This is the first named Fed voice of a holiday-thinned Monday, two days before CPI. October 28 hike odds still sit near 17 to 20% after the 29,000 payrolls print. Any line that another hike is the base case would reprice the front end with bonds shut. A patient, data-dependent tone would leave Wednesday's CPI as the only live event.
events.ifHigher: Hammack leans into another 2026 hike: USD bids into a bonds-shut session, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Patient, wait-for-CPI language: October odds stay in the high teens. Gold holds the $4,200 area.

events.whatItIs: The Bank of Japan's corporate goods price index, the factory-gate inflation print released at 23:50 UTC on Tuesday October 13.
events.whyItMatters: Japan producer prices have been stuck at 7.6% year over year on the same energy impulse that is lifting US and euro-area headlines. A hold at 7.6% keeps BoJ tightening talk alive into a Sports Day-reopening Tuesday. A drop toward 7.0% would be the first sign the pipeline is cooling and would sell the yen into Wednesday's US CPI.
events.ifHigher: Above 8.0%: energy is still accelerating at the factory gate. JPY bids, JGBs sold.
events.ifLower: At 7.0% or below: the pipeline is cooling. JPY sold, a softer overlay on US CPI.

events.whatItIs: The Reserve Bank of Australia's minutes of the October 6 meeting, published two weeks after the decision, covering the debate behind the 25bp hike to 4.60%.
events.whyItMatters: The Board hiked to a 15-year high of 4.60% and Governor Bullock left a further move on the table if Middle East energy keeps inflation hot. These minutes are the first look at how close a second hike was, the morning before Australia's September jobs report on Thursday. Hawkish minutes bid AUD into that labour print. A pause-biased recap would sell it.
events.ifHigher: Minutes show a live November bias or little dissent on 4.60%: AUD bids into Thursday's jobs report.
events.ifLower: Minutes show a close call and a desire to wait: AUD sold, a dovish setup for +20K jobs consensus.

events.whatItIs: Destatis's final national consumer-price print, confirming or revising the preliminary September reading that already fed the eurozone HICP flash.
events.whyItMatters: The flash was +0.6% on the month. Final revisions are usually tenths. A downward revision would take heat off Friday's eurozone HICP final (seen confirming 3.8%) the morning before US CPI. An upward revision would be a two-region inflation shock into Wednesday.
events.ifHigher: Revised above +0.8% MoM: German inflation is still accelerating. EUR bids, Bunds sold.
events.ifLower: Revised to +0.4% or below: the flash overstated the impulse. EUR sold into Wednesday's US CPI.

events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from a Board voter, at 07:45 UTC, the morning of bank earnings and the day before CPI.
events.whyItMatters: Waller is one of the more market-moving governors and he speaks into a bonds-open Tuesday after Monday's holiday. October 28 is still 15 days away. A hawkish overlay on last week's 29,000 payrolls would firm the dollar into Wednesday. A labour-cooling line would fade the remaining 17 to 20% hike odds before CPI can do the work.
events.ifHigher: Waller treats another hike as live: USD bids, a firmer setup for Wednesday's CPI.
events.ifLower: Patient, payrolls-aware language: October odds fade, gold bids the $4,200 handle.

events.whatItIs: OPEC's monthly assessment of global oil demand, supply, and the 2026-27 balance, released around 10:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: WTI last printed about $91.67 on Friday with Brent at $104.72. Last week's OPEC+ meeting held November quotas. The Monthly Oil Market Report is the demand-side follow-up: any cut to 2026 demand, or a higher non-OPEC supply line, would lean on crude into Thursday's delayed EIA print. A tighter balance would put $95 back in play the morning of bank earnings.
events.ifHigher: A tighter 2026 balance or a demand upgrade: WTI bids toward $95, a hotter energy overlay on Wednesday's CPI.
events.ifLower: A demand cut or a non-OPEC supply upgrade: WTI sold, a small relief bid for duration into CPI.

events.event: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, UnitedHealth, Johnson & Johnson Q3 earnings (before open)
events.forecast: JPM EPS about $5.90; GS about $14-$15; C about $2.70; WFC about $1.86; UNH about $4.12; JNJ about $2.66
events.whatItIs: The opening cluster of S&P 500 Q3 reports, released before the US cash open. JPMorgan, Goldman, Citi and Wells are the money-center tape. UnitedHealth and Johnson & Johnson are the healthcare tape.
events.whyItMatters: This is the first look at whether the 5.24% 10-year and last week's 29,000 payrolls print have hit bank net interest income, trading, and credit. UnitedHealth is the managed-care read after a year of cost pressure. A clean beat across the banks would be a risk-on open into Wednesday's CPI. A credit-quality miss would sell financials and put a growth overlay on the inflation print.
events.ifHigher: NII and EPS beat with credit costs contained: XLF and the S&P bid, a firmer open into CPI.
events.ifLower: A credit miss or a guide-down on NII: banks sold, a growth-scare overlay on Wednesday.

events.whatItIs: The National Association of Realtors' count of completed sales of previously owned homes, released at 14:00 UTC, plus the median price and months of supply.
events.whyItMatters: Mortgage rates near 7.5% have kept existing sales stuck under 4 million. Consensus is a small step down to 3.96 million. A drop through 3.90 million would say the housing channel is still frozen the afternoon after bank earnings, and would be a growth overlay on Wednesday's shelter line in CPI. A bounce above 4.05 million would be the first sign listings are clearing at these mortgage rates.
events.ifHigher: Above 4.05 million: housing is clearing. Modest equity bid, a calmer shelter setup for CPI.
events.ifLower: Below 3.90 million: sales are still frozen. Homebuilder and bank stocks sold, a soft overlay on shelter.

events.whatItIs: The National Bureau of Statistics' monthly consumer and producer price indexes, released at 01:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: China CPI is expected to accelerate to 1.1% from 0.8% and PPI to 4.4% from 3.8% as the same energy impulse that is lifting US headline CPI shows up in the factory gate. A hotter pair would bid commodity currencies and add an Asia inflation overlay hours before the US print. A miss back toward 0.8% CPI would say domestic demand is still too weak to pass energy through, and would sell AUD into Thursday's Australia jobs report.
events.ifHigher: CPI above 1.3% or PPI above 5.0%: energy is passing through. AUD and metals bid, a hotter overlay on US CPI.
events.ifLower: CPI at 0.8% or below: demand is still too weak. China proxies and AUD sold.

events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the ECB President, the first named euro-area policy voice of the week, at 02:10 UTC Wednesday.
events.whyItMatters: Eurozone HICP flashed at 3.8% last week and Friday's final is seen confirming that print. The ECB hiked to 2.50% in September. Lagarde speaks hours before US CPI. A line that another hike is live would bid the euro into the US print. A patient tone would leave Friday's 3.8% confirmation as a non-event.
events.ifHigher: Lagarde treats another 2026 hike as live: EUR bids, Bunds sold.
events.ifLower: Patient, data-dependent language: EUR sold, a quieter setup for Friday's HICP final.

events.previous: Surplus $119.1 billion; exports +25.0% YoY; imports +28.2% YoY (August 2026)
events.forecast: Surplus about $114.5 billion; exports +25.3% YoY; imports +23.5% YoY
events.whatItIs: China's monthly customs trade release in US dollar terms: the goods surplus, plus export and import growth. Timing is tentative around 3:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Exports are still running at a 25% year-over-year clip. Consensus looks for a slightly smaller surplus as import growth cools from 28.2% to about 23.5%. A sharp export miss would sell AUD, copper, and China ADRs the morning of US CPI. A hold near 25% exports would say the tariff overlay has not yet broken the goods impulse.
events.ifHigher: Exports above 27% or a surplus above $125 billion: goods demand is still hot. AUD and metals bid.
events.ifLower: Exports under 20%: the impulse is breaking. China proxies sold into the US session.

events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the Bank of England Governor, at 05:30 UTC, hours before US CPI and the day before UK August GDP.
events.whyItMatters: The BoE held at 3.75% on September 17 on a 6-3 split. Thursday's UK GDP is seen at -0.1% on the month after +0.4%. Bailey speaking into that print, and into US CPI, is the sterling event of Wednesday. A hike-live line would bid GBP. A growth-scare line would sell it into Thursday's contraction.
events.ifHigher: Bailey treats another 2026 hike as live or flags sticky UK services prices: GBP bids, gilts sold.
events.ifLower: Patient, peak-rate, or GDP-aware language: GBP sold into Thursday's -0.1% GDP consensus.

events.event: Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, BlackRock, ASML Q3 earnings (before open)
events.forecast: BAC EPS about $1.16; MS about $3.00; BLK about $14.35; ASML about $12.59
events.whatItIs: The second Q3 earnings cluster, released before the US cash open and two hours before CPI. Bank of America and Morgan Stanley complete the money-center set. BlackRock is the asset-manager print. ASML is the European semiconductor-equipment print.
events.whyItMatters: These names land in the same cash session as September CPI. A bank miss would already have the S&P on the back foot when the inflation number hits. ASML is the AI-capex tell after last week's OpenAI revenue scare: a bookings beat would bid semis into CPI, a miss would stack a growth scare on the inflation print.
events.ifHigher: BAC/MS beat and ASML bookings hold: financials and semis bid, a firmer tape into 12:30 UTC CPI.
events.ifLower: A bank miss or an ASML bookings warning: the S&P sold into CPI, a growth-and-inflation mix.

events.event: CPI (September 2026) -- headline and core, MoM and YoY
events.previous: +0.4% MoM / +3.4% YoY headline; +0.3% MoM / +2.4% YoY core (August 2026)
events.forecast: +0.6% MoM / +3.6% YoY headline; +0.2% MoM / +2.5% YoY core
events.actual: +0.6% MoM / +3.7% YoY headline; +0.3% MoM / +2.6% YoY core
events.whatItIs: The BLS Consumer Price Index: the monthly change in what urban consumers pay for a fixed basket of goods and services, reported both including and excluding food and energy, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's fulcrum and the last major inflation print before the October 27-28 FOMC. Headline is expected to accelerate to 3.6% on a 0.6% monthly jump as fuel from the Hormuz disruption hits the September basket, while monthly core is expected to slow to 0.2%. Last week's 29,000 payrolls print and 3.0% core PCE already pulled October hike odds to 17 to 20%. A hot core would put those odds back in play. A cool core would tell the Committee the September hike is still working and would leave Warsh's Friday IMF remarks as colour rather than a live hike signal.
events.ifHigher: Core at +0.4% MoM or the annual rate above 2.6%: disinflation stalled. USD bids, gold and BTC sold, October odds jump.
events.ifLower: Core at +0.1% MoM or below: the energy impulse is not leaking into core. Gold and duration bid, October odds fade further.

events.whatItIs: The Federal Reserve's anecdotal survey of economic conditions across the 12 districts, released at 18:00 UTC, two weeks before the October 27-28 FOMC.
events.whyItMatters: The Beige Book lands six hours after CPI. Traders will read it for whether district contacts are already seeing the 29,000 payrolls cooling and the energy impulse in prices. Hawkish colour on prices after a hot CPI would firm October odds into Thursday's PPI. Soft labour anecdotes after a cool CPI would fade them.
events.ifHigher: Districts report accelerating prices and still-tight labour: a hawkish overlay on whatever CPI just did. USD bids.
events.ifLower: Districts report cooling hiring and contained prices: a dovish recap. Gold and duration bid.

events.event: API Weekly Crude Oil Stock Change (week ending October 9)
events.previous: -3.19 million barrels (EIA, week ending October 2; stocks 424.1 million)
events.whatItIs: The American Petroleum Institute's unofficial weekly estimate of US commercial crude stocks, released at 20:30 UTC, the afternoon before the holiday-delayed EIA report.
events.whyItMatters: EIA does not print on Wednesday this week because of Columbus Day. API is the only inventory number on the normal day, and it sets positioning for Thursday's 16:00 UTC official print. Last week's EIA was a 3.19 million-barrel draw with WTI back to $91.67. Another large draw overnight would put $95 in play into Thursday. A build would lean on crude after OPEC's monthly report.
events.ifHigher: A build of 3 million barrels or more: the surplus is growing. WTI sold overnight.
events.ifLower: A draw of 2 million barrels or more: last week's draw is extending. WTI bids into Thursday's EIA.

events.whatItIs: The Australian Bureau of Statistics' Labour Force Survey: employment change, the unemployment rate, and the full-time versus part-time split, released at 00:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The RBA hiked to 4.60% last week. This is the first labour print after that move. Consensus looks for a slowdown to +20,000 with unemployment unchanged at 4.6%. A second +30,000-plus gain would keep a November hike live and bid AUD into the US PPI/retail window. A drop in employment, or unemployment at 4.8%, would make last week's hike look like the cycle top.
events.ifHigher: Jobs above +35,000 with unemployment at 4.5% or below: the hike is not cooling labour. AUD bids.
events.ifLower: Jobs below zero, or unemployment at 4.8%+: the hike is landing. AUD sold.

events.whatItIs: The ONS monthly GDP estimate, plus industrial production, manufacturing, construction, and the goods trade balance, released at 06:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Consensus is a 0.1% contraction after July's 0.4% gain. Bailey speaks around this window. A deeper drop would sell sterling into the US 12:30 UTC inflation-and-spending bundle and would support the September hold as the peak. A surprise hold in positive territory would bid GBP and keep a 2026 hike live.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.2% MoM: the July rebound is extending. GBP bids, gilts sold.
events.ifLower: Below -0.3%: the economy contracted more than priced. GBP sold, a dovish overlay on Bailey.

events.whatItIs: Eurostat's monthly industrial production index for the euro area, covering manufacturing, mining, and energy.
events.whyItMatters: July was -0.1%. Consensus looks for a 0.1% rebound. A miss would be a growth overlay on Friday's 3.8% HICP final and would sell the euro into the US PPI/retail window. A beat above 0.5% would keep the modest European activity bid alive after last week's hot inflation flash.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.5% MoM: industry is recovering. EUR bids, European cyclicals supported.
events.ifLower: Another decline: the factory fade is extending. EUR sold into the US session.

events.event: TSMC, Charles Schwab, PNC, US Bank Q3 earnings (before open)
events.whatItIs: The Thursday Q3 cluster: Taiwan Semiconductor is the foundry print, Charles Schwab is the brokerage and net-interest print, and PNC and US Bank extend the regional-bank tape.
events.whyItMatters: TSMC is the AI-capex confirmation after ASML on Wednesday. A bookings or guidance beat would bid semis into the 12:30 UTC data window. Schwab, PNC and US Bank are the second-wave bank read: if Tuesday's money-center names beat and these miss, the story becomes 'only the giants are fine.'
events.ifHigher: TSMC guidance holds and the regionals beat: semis and XLF bid into PPI and retail sales.
events.ifLower: A TSMC guide-down or a regional-bank credit miss: growth scare into the 12:30 UTC bundle.

events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's advance monthly sales of retail and food services, released at 12:30 UTC in the same window as PPI, claims, and the Philadelphia Fed survey.
events.whyItMatters: August jumped 1.2%. Consensus looks for a slowdown to 0.3% as that spike pays back. The control group (ex-autos, gasoline, building materials, and food services) is the line that feeds GDP goods consumption. A second 1-handle print would say the consumer is still spending through 7% mortgages and 4.2% unemployment, and would stack a hot-demand story on Wednesday's CPI. A miss below zero would be the first real crack in the spending impulse the FOMC hiked into.
events.ifHigher: Headline above +0.7%, or control still near +1.0%: the consumer is not slowing. USD bids, equities mixed with PPI.
events.ifLower: Headline at 0.0% or below: spending rolled over. Duration bid, a growth overlay on whatever PPI just did.

events.event: PPI (September 2026) -- final demand, MoM and YoY
events.forecast: +0.5% MoM headline; +0.3% MoM core; about +5.3% YoY
events.whatItIs: The BLS Producer Price Index for final demand: what domestic producers receive for their output, measured before those costs reach the consumer, released at 12:30 UTC with retail sales and claims.
events.whyItMatters: PPI is the upstream cross-check on Wednesday's CPI and several of its components feed the PCE deflator the Fed targets. Headline is seen at +0.5% after +0.4%, with core at +0.3% after +0.2%, as the same energy impulse works through the factory gate. A hot core PPI the morning after a hot core CPI would reopen October 28. A miss would confirm that yesterday's energy was contained in headline.
events.ifHigher: Core at +0.5% MoM or the annual rate back toward 6%: pipeline inflation is accelerating. USD bids, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Core at +0.1% or below: the pipeline is cooling. Gold and duration bid, October odds fade.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of first-time unemployment filings, released at 12:30 UTC in the same window as retail sales and PPI.
events.whyItMatters: Claims have been sitting under 200,000 even as September payrolls slowed to 29,000. A jump toward 230,000 in a Columbus Day week would be the first weekly confirmation that the payrolls miss was a trend, and would fade October odds even if PPI is hot. Another sub-200,000 print would say layoffs have not started and would keep the debate on hiring, not firing.
events.ifHigher: Above 230K: the first real crack in weekly filings. Gold and duration bid.
events.ifLower: Below 190K: still tight. USD bids, the 29,000 payrolls print looks like a one-month miss.

events.whatItIs: The Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia's monthly survey of regional manufacturers, covering general activity, new orders, employment, and prices, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: September's 37.8 was a very hot print. Consensus looks for a payback to 26.5, still firmly expansionary. The prices-paid and employment sub-indexes are the ones that matter the morning after CPI: a second 30-handle with prices still hot would confirm that factory inflation is not done. A drop toward 10 with employment negative would be the growth half of a busy morning window.
events.ifHigher: Above 35 with prices paid still elevated: factory inflation is extending. USD bids.
events.ifLower: Below 10, or employment negative: the September spike was a one-month print. Equities mixed, a growth overlay on retail sales.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending October 9) -- delayed for Columbus Day
events.previous: -3.19 million barrels (week ending October 2; stocks 424.1 million)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly change in commercial crude stocks, excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. Columbus Day delays the usual Wednesday 14:30 UTC print to Thursday 16:00 UTC, with the full report at 18:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: WTI last printed about $91.67 with Brent at $104.72. Last week's official print was a 3.19 million-barrel draw, stocks at 424.1 million. API on Wednesday is the only preview. A second large draw would put $95 back in play and would feed the energy overlay on whatever CPI and PPI just did. A build would lean on a market that has already given back the $100 handle.
events.ifHigher: A build of 3 million barrels or more: the surplus is growing. WTI sold, a small relief bid for duration.
events.ifLower: A draw of 2 million barrels or more: last week's draw is extending. WTI bids, inflation-sensitive equities soften.

events.whatItIs: A scheduled Arbitrum (ARB) vesting release of about 93 million tokens, estimated around $19 million, the largest named unlock of this week.
events.whyItMatters: Bitcoin last printed about $82,358 on Friday, well off the mid-$80,000s from a week earlier. A $19 million ARB cliff is not an $856 million HYPE event, but it is the week's largest named supply print and it lands the same session as Chair Warsh at the IMF. A clean hold in ARB and BTC is constructive. A break that pulls ETH beta is a small supply test into a data-heavy week.
events.ifHigher: ARB absorbs the unlock and BTC holds $82,000: demand matched the supply. Constructive for L2 names.
events.ifLower: ARB breaks and pulls ETH beta: the overhang hits a thin Friday tape. Altcoin risk-off, BTC relatively more resilient.

events.event: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Speaks (IMF meetings, Bangkok)
events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the Federal Reserve Chair at the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, at 03:30 UTC Friday.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's second fulcrum after CPI. Warsh hiked to 3.75-4.00% on September 16 and called inflation too high. He now speaks after Wednesday's CPI, Thursday's PPI and retail sales, and into a 17 to 20% October 28 hike market. A hawkish read of a hot CPI would reprice the front end overnight. A labour-aware, wait-and-see line would confirm that October 28 is a hold unless the data reversed.
events.ifHigher: Warsh leans into another hike, or treats a hot CPI as not enough progress: USD bids, gold and BTC sold, October odds jump.
events.ifLower: Patient, data-dependent, or payrolls-aware language: October odds fade. Gold and duration bid.

events.forecast: +3.8% YoY headline; +2.5% YoY core (unrevised from the flash)
events.whatItIs: Eurostat's final harmonised consumer-price index for the euro area, confirming or revising last week's flash.
events.whyItMatters: The flash jumped to 3.8% on energy. Final revisions are usually tenths. A downward revision would take heat off the ECB after Lagarde's Wednesday remarks. An upward revision to 4.0% would be a late-week euro bid into a US session that has already traded CPI, PPI, and Warsh.
events.ifHigher: Revised to 4.0% or above: the flash understated the impulse. EUR bids, Bunds sold.
events.ifLower: Revised to 3.6% or below: the flash overstated it. EUR sold, October ECB odds fade.

events.whatItIs: The BLS import and export price indexes, the traded-goods inflation print, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Import prices are the pipeline from oil, the dollar, and China goods into US consumer prices. Consensus is +0.6% after +0.7%. A second hot print the morning after CPI and PPI would say the energy impulse is still arriving at the dock. A miss would be a quiet confirmation that pipeline pressure is rolling over into the FOMC blackout that starts next week.
events.ifHigher: Above +1.0% MoM: imported inflation is still accelerating. USD bids, a late hawkish overlay.
events.ifLower: At 0.0% or below: the pipeline is cooling. Modest gold bid, a quieter setup for next week's housing data.

events.whatItIs: The Federal Reserve's monthly index of factory, mine, and utility output, plus the capacity-utilisation rate, released at 13:15 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: August was flat. Consensus looks for a 0.4% rebound. A miss back to negative would stack a growth miss on whatever Warsh said overnight and would sell cyclicals into the weekend. A beat above 0.8% would say factories are still expanding through 4.2% unemployment, and would be a modest USD bid after a data-heavy week.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.8% MoM: factories are rebounding. Cyclicals bid, a small USD bid.
events.ifLower: Negative again: industry is stalling. Cyclicals sold, a growth overlay on Warsh.

2026-10-19.summary: UK CPI, Tesla + Meta earnings, and Friday flash PMIs headline a Fed-blackout week.

events.event: FOMC blackout in force through October 29 -- no Fed speakers
events.whatItIs: The Federal Reserve's communications blackout for the October 27-28 FOMC. It opened at 04:00 UTC on Saturday October 17, the second Saturday before the meeting, and runs through Thursday October 29.
events.whyItMatters: Warsh's Friday IMF appearance was the last named Fed voice before the decision. October hike odds sit near 14 to 15% after he declined to signal a move, even with CPI at 3.7% and PPI at 6.3%. Every reprice this week happens on China GDP, UK CPI, flash PMIs, and Tesla-Meta, not on a governor's podium. A hot UK CPI or a still-hot US services PMI would have to do the work that a Warsh line did last week.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- no Fed communication this week. Data and earnings set the tape into October 28.
events.ifLower: N/A -- no Fed communication this week. Data and earnings set the tape into October 28.

events.event: China GDP (Q3 2026), Industrial Production, Retail Sales, Fixed-Asset Investment (September)
events.previous: GDP +4.3% YoY / +0.9% QoQ (Q2); IP +5.2% YoY; retail +0.4% YoY; FAI -7.2% YTD (August)
events.forecast: GDP +4.4% YoY / +1.1% QoQ; IP +5.4%; retail +0.5%; FAI -7.3% YTD
events.actual: GDP +4.5% YoY / +1.2% QoQ; IP +5.5%; retail +1.1%; FAI -7.2% YTD
events.whatItIs: The National Bureau of Statistics' quarterly GDP print plus the September activity dump: industrial production, retail sales, and year-to-date fixed-asset investment, released at 02:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the first look at whether China's Q3 held the 4-handle after a 4.3% Q2, and it lands the morning the Fed goes quiet. Retail sales are still crawling at 0.4% and FAI is still contracting near 7%. A GDP miss toward 4.0% with another sub-0.5% retail print would sell AUD, copper, and China ADRs into a US session that has no Fed speaker to offset it. A 4.6% beat with IP above 6% would be the Asia bid Tesla and Meta have to open into on Wednesday.
events.ifHigher: GDP at 4.6%+ or IP above 6.0%: the impulse is holding. AUD and metals bid, a firmer Asia tape into Tesla and Meta.
events.ifLower: GDP at 4.0% or below, or retail still near 0.0%: demand is still too weak. China proxies and AUD sold.

events.event: Canada CPI (September 2026) -- headline and BoC core measures
events.previous: -0.1% MoM / +3.0% YoY headline; common-CPI 2.6%, trimmed 1.9%, median 2.0% (August 2026)
events.forecast: +0.2% MoM / about +3.2% YoY; common-CPI 2.6%, trimmed 1.9%, median 2.0%
events.whatItIs: Statistics Canada's monthly Consumer Price Index, plus the Bank of Canada's three preferred core measures (common, trimmed, and median CPI), released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The BoC meets next Wednesday October 28, the same day as the FOMC. Headline is seen bouncing 0.2% after a 0.1% decline, taking the annual rate up toward 3.2% as energy feeds through. The three core measures are expected unchanged, still clustered around 2.0 to 2.6%. A hot core cluster would reopen a BoC hold-versus-hike debate the same week the Fed is in blackout. A miss back toward 2.8% headline would keep October 28 as a hold and would sell the loonie into WTI at $101.
events.ifHigher: Headline at 3.4%+ or common-CPI above 2.8%: energy is leaking into core. CAD bids, a hawkish overlay on next week's BoC.
events.ifLower: Headline at 2.8% or below, or common-CPI under 2.4%: the energy impulse is contained. CAD sold, October 28 BoC hold locked.

events.event: Bank of Canada Business Outlook Survey (Q3 2026)
events.whatItIs: The BoC's quarterly survey of firms' sales, investment, hiring, and inflation expectations, released at 15:30 UTC, three hours after CPI.
events.whyItMatters: This is the anecdotal companion to the 12:30 UTC CPI print and the last full BoC colour before the October 28 decision. Traders will read it for whether firms are already seeing the US 3.7% CPI energy impulse in their own prices, and whether hiring intentions cooled after last month's 68,300 jobs miss. Hawkish price-expectation colour after a hot CPI would firm CAD into next week. Soft sales and hiring colour after a cool CPI would lock the hold.
events.ifHigher: Firms report accelerating output prices and still-tight labour: a hawkish overlay on whatever CPI just did. CAD bids.
events.ifLower: Firms report cooling sales and contained prices: a dovish recap. CAD sold, October 28 hold firmer.

events.whatItIs: The People's Bank of China's monthly loan prime rates, the reference rates for new corporate (1-year) and mortgage (5-year) lending, typically published around 01:15 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Monday's GDP dump will already have set the China tone. A hold at 3.00 / 3.50% is fully priced. A surprise 5-year cut would be the property-easing signal after FAI contracted 7.2%, and would bid China ADRs into Tuesday's US housing data. A hold after a GDP miss would confirm Beijing is not ready to ease further and would leave AUD offered.
events.ifHigher: A hike (not the base case): CNY bids, a hawkish shock. Extremely unlikely against 0.5% retail sales.
events.ifLower: A 5-year cut: property easing is back. China proxies and AUD bid, a softer CNY.

events.whatItIs: A scheduled LayerZero (ZRO) vesting release of about 23.6 million tokens, estimated around $46 million, going to team and advisors, the largest named unlock of this week.

A $46 million ZRO cliff is not last month's $856 million HYPE event, but it is the week's largest named supply print and it lands the morning of Netflix and two days before Tesla and Meta. A clean hold in ZRO and BTC is constructive. A break that pulls ETH beta is a small supply test into an earnings-heavy tape.
events.ifHigher: ZRO absorbs the unlock and BTC holds $81,000: demand matched the supply. Constructive for infra names.
events.ifLower: ZRO breaks and pulls ETH beta: the overhang hits a thin Tuesday tape. Altcoin risk-off, BTC relatively more resilient.

events.event: UK Unemployment Rate and Average Earnings (August 2026, three-month)
events.previous: Unemployment 4.9%; average earnings incl. bonus +3.9% 3m/y; claimant count +27,800 (July 2026)
events.forecast: Unemployment 5.0%; earnings +3.8%; claimant count about +19,000 to +20,000
events.actual: Unemployment 4.7%; regular earnings +3.7%; total pay +3.7%; payrolls +13,000; vacancies 691,000
events.whatItIs: The ONS labour-market package: the ILO unemployment rate, three-month average weekly earnings including and excluding bonuses, and the claimant-count change, released at 06:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the labour half of a two-day UK inflation-and-jobs cluster, 24 hours before Wednesday's CPI. Unemployment is seen rising to 5.0%, the highest since March, with earnings slowing to 3.8%, the weakest since 2020. A second 5-handle with earnings still at 4% would be a hawkish-dovish split into tomorrow's 3.4% CPI consensus. A drop back to 4.8% with earnings at 4.1% would keep a 2026 BoE hike live and bid sterling into the CPI print.
events.ifHigher: Unemployment at 5.2%+ or earnings under 3.5%: the labour market is rolling over. GBP sold, a dovish setup for Wednesday CPI.
events.ifLower: Unemployment at 4.8% or below with earnings at 4.1%+: labour is still tight. GBP bids, a hotter overlay on tomorrow's CPI.

events.event: Germany and Eurozone ZEW Economic Sentiment (October 2026)
events.whatItIs: The ZEW Institute's monthly survey of financial analysts' six-month outlook for Germany and the euro area, released at 09:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: ZEW has risen for five months. Consensus is the first pullback, to about 31 in Germany and 24 in the euro area, as energy costs and the 3.8% HICP hangover weigh on expectations. A drop toward 20 would be a growth overlay on Friday's flash PMIs. A hold above 34 would say analysts are looking through the energy spike, and would be a modest euro bid into Wednesday's UK CPI.
events.ifHigher: Germany above 35: the streak extends. EUR bids, a firmer setup for Friday's PMIs.
events.ifLower: Germany under 25: expectations are cracking. EUR sold, a soft overlay on Friday's flash.

events.event: GE Aerospace, General Motors, 3M, RTX Q3 earnings (before open)
events.forecast: GE EPS about $2.01; GM about $3.52 to $3.70; 3M about $2.39; RTX about $1.73 to $1.79
events.whatItIs: The Tuesday Q3 industrial cluster, released before the US cash open. GE Aerospace is the commercial-engine and defense print. GM is the auto and EV print. 3M and RTX are the diversified-industrial and defense-prime prints.
events.whyItMatters: Friday's S&P closed 7,659.44 with the Nasdaq off 4.5% on the week as AI-capex names sold off. These four are the non-AI open of Q3: engines, trucks, industrials, and defense. A clean GE and RTX beat would bid the Dow into Netflix after the close and Tesla-Meta on Wednesday. A GM guide-down on US pricing or inventory would sell cyclicals into a blackout week that has no Fed put.
events.ifHigher: GE and RTX beat with GM holding US pricing: industrials and the Dow bid, a firmer open into Netflix.
events.ifLower: A GM guide-down or a GE margin miss: cyclicals sold, a growth overlay on Wednesday's Tesla-Meta tape.

events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's monthly count of new residential construction: housing starts (foundations poured) and building permits (authorisations), released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Mortgage rates are still near 7.5% and existing sales are stuck under 4 million. Consensus looks for starts to rebound to 1.30 million after a 2.6% August drop, with permits roughly unchanged at 1.40 million. A starts print under 1.20 million would say the housing channel is still frozen the morning of Netflix, and would be a growth overlay on Friday's PMIs. A bounce above 1.35 million would be the first sign builders are clearing lots at these mortgage rates.
events.ifHigher: Starts above 1.35 million: housing is clearing. Homebuilders bid, a calmer growth setup for Friday's PMIs.
events.ifLower: Starts under 1.20 million: the freeze is extending. Homebuilders sold, a soft overlay on Tesla and Meta.

events.whatItIs: The National Association of Realtors' index of signed contracts on existing homes, a one-to-two-month lead on completed existing-home sales, released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: August's 0.3% gain was the first positive print in a weak run. Consensus is flat to slightly down. A drop of 2% or more would confirm that 7.5% mortgages are still blocking closings, two hours after the starts print, and would weigh on homebuilders into Netflix. A bounce above 1% would be a second month of contract activity and a small bid for the housing complex.
events.ifHigher: Above +1.0%: contracts are clearing. Modest homebuilder bid.
events.ifLower: Below -2.0%: the pipeline is freezing again. Homebuilders sold.

events.forecast: EPS about $0.82 to $0.84; revenue about $13.1 billion; live interview 20:45 UTC
events.whatItIs: Netflix's third-quarter results, posted around 20:01 UTC, with a live video interview at 20:45 UTC. Paid-membership growth, operating margin, and 2026 guidance are the lines the tape trades.
events.whyItMatters: Netflix is the first mega-cap consumer-tech print of this week, 24 hours before Tesla and Meta. Friday's Nasdaq lost 4.5% as AI-capex names sold off; Netflix is a cash-flow and engagement story, not a capex story. A membership beat with a margin hold would be a bid for consumer tech into Wednesday. A guide-down on 2026 operating margin would extend the Nasdaq fade into Tesla and Meta.
events.ifHigher: Membership and margin beat with 2026 guide held: consumer tech bids, a firmer Nasdaq setup for Tesla and Meta.
events.ifLower: A membership miss or a 2026 margin cut: Nasdaq sold overnight, a weaker open into Wednesday's mega-cap cluster.

events.whatItIs: The American Petroleum Institute's unofficial weekly estimate of US commercial crude stocks, released at 20:30 UTC, the afternoon before the official EIA report.
events.whyItMatters: WTI last printed about $101.41 with Brent at $109.86 after last week's 8.6 million-barrel official draw. API is the positioning print for Wednesday's 14:30 UTC EIA. Another large draw overnight would put $105 in play into Tesla and Meta. A build would lean on a market that has already reclaimed $100 and would take some energy heat off Friday's PMIs.
events.ifHigher: A build of 3 million barrels or more: the surplus is growing. WTI sold overnight.
events.ifLower: A draw of 3 million barrels or more: last week's draw is extending. WTI bids toward $105 into Wednesday's EIA.

events.whatItIs: The Ministry of Finance's monthly customs trade release: the yen-denominated goods balance, plus export and import growth, released at 23:50 UTC on Wednesday.
events.whyItMatters: August's deficit blew out past 1 trillion yen on energy imports. Consensus looks for a narrowing toward 250 billion as export volumes recover. A still-wide deficit next to Thursday night's Japan CPI (core seen 2.1%) would keep the yen offered into the BoJ's next meeting. A surprise surplus would be a small JPY bid the morning of UK CPI.
events.ifHigher: A surplus, or a deficit under 100 billion yen: exports are recovering. JPY bids.
events.ifLower: A deficit still near 1 trillion yen: energy imports are still dominating. JPY sold.

events.actual: +0.4% MoM / +3.5% YoY headline; core +2.8% YoY; services +3.7%; CPIH +3.6%
events.whatItIs: The ONS Consumer Price Index, including the core measure that excludes energy, food, alcohol, and tobacco, plus RPI, released at 06:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the sterling event of the week and the last major G7 inflation print before next week's FOMC, BoC, and ECB cluster. Headline is seen at 3.4%, a nine-month high, with core at 2.7%, the highest since March, as the same energy impulse that took US CPI to 3.7% hits the UK basket. The BoE held at 3.75% on September 17 on a 6-3 split. A 3.4 / 2.7 print with Tuesday's unemployment at 5.0% is a hawkish-prices, dovish-labour mix. A core print at 2.9% would reopen a 2026 hike and bid gilts-sold sterling into Tesla and Meta.
events.ifHigher: Headline at 3.6%+ or core at 2.9%+: energy is leaking into core. GBP bids, gilts sold, 2026 BoE hike odds jump.
events.ifLower: Headline at 3.1% or below with core at 2.5%: the impulse is contained. GBP sold, the September hold looks like the peak.

events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the Bank of England Governor, in the hours after the CPI print and before the US EIA window.
events.whyItMatters: Bailey is the only G7 policy voice of Wednesday in a Fed-blackout week. He speaks after the 3.4% CPI consensus and Tuesday's labour package. A hike-live line after a 2.9% core would bid sterling into Tesla and Meta. A labour-aware, peak-rate line after a 5.0% unemployment print would sell it. There is a second Bailey appearance Thursday around 10:50 UTC if the first is colourless.
events.ifHigher: Bailey treats another 2026 hike as live or flags sticky services prices: GBP bids, gilts sold.
events.ifLower: Patient, peak-rate, or unemployment-aware language: GBP sold, a quieter setup for Friday's UK PMI.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending October 16)
events.previous: -8.6 million barrels (week ending October 9; stocks 415.6 million, 3% below the five-year average)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly change in commercial crude stocks, excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, released at 14:30 UTC, covering crude, gasoline, distillates, and Cushing.
events.whyItMatters: WTI last printed about $101.41 with Brent at $109.86, tagging $110 for the first time since May. Last week's official print was an 8.6 million-barrel draw, stocks at 415.6 million. API on Tuesday is the only preview. A second large draw would put $105 in play the afternoon Tesla and Meta report, and would feed the energy overlay on last week's 3.7% CPI. A build would lean on a market that has already reclaimed $100 and would take heat off Friday's PMIs.
events.ifHigher: A build of 3 million barrels or more: the surplus is growing. WTI sold, a small relief bid for duration into Tesla and Meta.
events.ifLower: A draw of 3 million barrels or more: last week's draw is extending. WTI bids toward $105, inflation-sensitive equities soften into the close.

events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the ECB President, the named euro-area policy voice of a Fed-blackout Wednesday, ahead of next Thursday's ECB decision.
events.whyItMatters: Eurozone HICP is running at 3.8%. The ECB hiked to 2.50% in September and meets October 29. Lagarde speaks hours after UK CPI and two hours after EIA, into the Tesla-Meta close. A line that another hike is live would bid the euro into that close. A patient tone would leave Friday's flash PMIs as the only euro-area event that can move October 29 odds.
events.ifHigher: Lagarde treats another 2026 hike as live: EUR bids, Bunds sold.
events.ifLower: Patient, data-dependent language: EUR sold, a quieter setup for Friday's PMIs and next week's ECB.

events.event: Tesla, Meta, IBM, Texas Instruments Q3 earnings (after close)
events.forecast: Meta EPS about $6.31 to $6.35, revenue about $64.6 billion; Tesla EPS about $0.21 to $0.45; IBM and TXN N/A; Meta call 20:30 UTC, Tesla 21:30 UTC
events.whatItIs: The Wednesday after-close mega-cap cluster. Meta is the advertising and Reality Labs print. Tesla is the deliveries, auto-margin, and energy-storage print. IBM is the mainframe and software print. Texas Instruments is the analog-chip print.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's equity fulcrum. Friday's Nasdaq lost 4.5% as CoreWeave dropped 12% and the AI-capex complex unwound. Meta is the ad-cycle and capex-guide tell: a Reality Labs spend cut would bid the complex, a raise would extend the fade. Tesla is the EV-margin and robotaxi-narrative tell after a year of delivery pressure, with consensus EPS well below last year's $0.37. IBM and TXN are the old-economy tech tape. A Meta beat with a Tesla miss is a split Nasdaq overnight. A double miss into a Fed-blackout Thursday is the growth scare Friday's PMIs would then have to trade.
events.ifHigher: Meta beats and holds the capex guide, Tesla holds auto margin: Nasdaq bids overnight, a firmer setup for Friday's PMIs.
events.ifLower: A Meta capex raise or a Tesla margin break: Nasdaq sold overnight, a growth-scare overlay on Friday's flash PMIs.

events.forecast: EPS about $1.89 versus $1.99 a year ago; webcast 12:30 UTC
events.whatItIs: Procter & Gamble's quarterly results, released before the US cash open, covering organic sales, pricing versus volume, and the consumer-staples margin.
events.whyItMatters: P&G is the household-spending tell the morning after Tesla and Meta. Last week's retail sales jumped 0.8%. Organic sales that hold on volume, not just price, would say the consumer is still filling the cart through 7.5% mortgages and 3.7% CPI. A volume miss would be the first staples crack and a soft overlay on Friday's Michigan final.
events.ifHigher: Organic sales beat on volume: the consumer is holding. Staples and the Dow bid.
events.ifLower: A volume miss or a guide-down: the household is trading down. Staples sold, a growth overlay on Friday's PMIs.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of first-time unemployment filings, plus continuing claims, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Claims have been sitting under 200,000 even as September payrolls slowed to 29,000. A jump toward 230,000 the morning after Tesla and Meta would be the first weekly confirmation that the payrolls miss was a trend, and would fade the remaining 14 to 15% October hike odds inside blackout. Another sub-200,000 print would say layoffs have not started and would keep Friday's PMIs as an activity story, not a labour story.
events.ifHigher: Above 230K: the first real crack in weekly filings. Gold and duration bid, October odds fade further.
events.ifLower: Below 190K: still tight. USD bids, the 29,000 payrolls print still looks like a one-month miss.

events.forecast: Headline about +2.1% to +2.3% YoY; core +2.1% YoY
events.whatItIs: The Statistics Bureau's national consumer-price index, including the Bank of Japan's preferred core measure that excludes fresh food, released at 23:30 UTC on Friday.
events.whyItMatters: Core is seen accelerating to 2.1%, the highest this year, as the same energy impulse that lifted US and UK headlines shows up in the Japan basket. Last week's Japan PPI held 7.6%. A 2.1% core print keeps BoJ tightening talk alive into a week when the Fed, BoC, and ECB all meet. A miss back at 1.7% would sell the yen into Friday's Japan and global flash PMIs.
events.ifHigher: Core at 2.3%+ : energy is passing through. JPY bids, JGBs sold, a hotter overlay on next week's BoJ watch.
events.ifLower: Core at 1.7% or below: the pipeline is not reaching households. JPY sold.

events.event: GRAM (TON) Token Unlock (~$49 million) and Humanity (H) Unlock (~$17 million)
events.whatItIs: Two scheduled Friday vesting releases: GRAM on TON, about 36.6 million tokens estimated around $49 million (1.2% of supply, rewards), and Humanity (H), about 293 million tokens estimated around $17 million (7.3% of supply, team, advisors, and investors).
events.whyItMatters: GRAM is the week's largest dollar unlock, slightly ahead of Tuesday's ZRO print. Humanity is the week's largest percentage unlock at 7.3% of supply. They land the same morning as Japan CPI, UK retail, and the global flash PMI cluster. A clean hold in both, with BTC still above $81,000, is constructive into the PMI window. A GRAM break that pulls TON beta, or an H break that pulls small-cap alts, is a supply test on a data-heavy Friday.
events.ifHigher: Both absorb the unlock and BTC holds $81,000: demand matched the supply. Constructive into the PMI window.
events.ifLower: GRAM or H breaks and pulls alt beta: the overhang hits a data-heavy Friday. Altcoin risk-off, BTC relatively more resilient.

events.whatItIs: The ONS monthly estimate of retail spending, including and excluding auto fuel, released at 06:00 UTC, two hours before the UK flash PMI.
events.whyItMatters: Wednesday's CPI is seen at 3.4%. A 0.1% sales print is a payback after August's 0.5% and a real-spending miss if prices jumped. A second 0.5% gain would say UK households are still spending through 5.0% unemployment and would bid sterling into the PMI cluster. A drop below zero would stack a growth miss on whatever CPI just did and would sell GBP into the US PMI window.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.4% MoM: the consumer is holding. GBP bids, a firmer setup for the UK PMI.
events.ifLower: Below 0.0%: spending rolled over. GBP sold, a growth overlay on the 08:30 UTC PMI.

events.event: Germany S&P Global Flash PMI (October 2026) -- manufacturing, services, composite
events.forecast: Manufacturing about 54.0; services about 53.1; composite about 53.0
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary October survey of German purchasing managers, covering manufacturing and services, released at 07:30 UTC, 30 minutes before the eurozone flash.
events.whyItMatters: Germany is the factory half of Friday's European PMI cluster. Consensus is a hold in the low-54s for manufacturing and a small step-up in services. A drop back through 50 would be the first contraction signal of the autumn and would sell the euro into the eurozone print. A 55-handle would say German industry is looking through the energy spike, and would be a modest EUR bid into the US 13:45 UTC window.
events.ifHigher: Manufacturing above 55: the factory rebound is extending. EUR bids, European cyclicals supported.
events.ifLower: Manufacturing under 50: Germany is contracting again. EUR sold into the eurozone flash.

events.event: Eurozone S&P Global Flash PMI (October 2026) -- manufacturing, services, composite
events.forecast: Manufacturing about 52.8; services about 52.8; composite about 52.3
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary October survey of euro-area purchasing managers, the first look at October activity, released at 08:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the euro-area event of the week and the last activity read before next Thursday's ECB decision. Consensus is a modest slowdown, still firmly above 50. A composite drop through 50 would be the first contraction since the summer and would sell the euro into a Fed-blackout US session. A hold at 53 with services at an eight-month high would keep October 29 as a live hike tail after 3.8% HICP.
events.ifHigher: Composite above 53.5 with services still rising: the expansion is extending. EUR bids, Bunds sold, October 29 hike odds firm.
events.ifLower: Composite under 50: the expansion stalled. EUR sold, October 29 hold locked.

events.event: UK S&P Global Flash PMI (October 2026) -- manufacturing, services, composite
events.forecast: Manufacturing about 51.8; services about 51.9; composite about 51.7
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary October survey of UK purchasing managers, released at 08:30 UTC, 30 minutes after the eurozone flash.
events.whyItMatters: The UK PMI closes a three-print sterling week: Tuesday labour, Wednesday CPI, Friday activity. Consensus is a small step-down, still above 50. A services drop through 50 next to 5.0% unemployment and 3.4% CPI would be the growth half of a stagflation mix and would sell GBP into the US window. A 53-handle would say Wednesday's inflation impulse is landing on an economy that is still expanding.
events.ifHigher: Composite above 53: activity is holding up. GBP bids, a firmer overlay on whatever CPI just did.
events.ifLower: Composite under 50: the UK is contracting. GBP sold, a dovish overlay on a hot CPI.

events.event: Canada Retail Sales (August 2026 final / September preliminary)
events.forecast: August final about +1.3%; September preliminary about +0.3%
events.whatItIs: Statistics Canada's monthly retail-sales print, released at 12:30 UTC, covering the August final and a September advance.
events.whyItMatters: Monday's CPI is the inflation half of the BoC week. This is the spending half, five days before the October 28 decision. A second month of gains would say Canadian households are still spending through 6.5% unemployment and would be a modest CAD bid into the US PMI. A September miss below zero would stack a growth miss on whatever Monday's CPI did and would lock next week's BoC as a hold.
events.ifHigher: September above +0.8%: the consumer is holding. CAD bids into next week's BoC.
events.ifLower: September at 0.0% or below: spending rolled over. CAD sold, October 28 hold locked.

events.event: US S&P Global Flash PMI (October 2026) -- manufacturing, services, composite
events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary October survey of US purchasing managers, covering manufacturing and services, released at 13:45 UTC, the last major US activity print before the October 28 FOMC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the US event of the week. September's 58.4 composite was very hot. Consensus is a modest slowdown, still in the high-57s, firmly expansionary. The prices-paid and employment sub-indexes are the ones the blackout Committee will read: a second 58-handle with prices still hot would reopen the 14 to 15% October hike tail that Warsh just closed. A drop toward 54 with employment negative would confirm the 29,000 payrolls cooling and would lock October 28 as a hold. Tesla and Meta will already have set the Nasdaq overnight; this print decides whether that earnings tape trades as tech or as the whole economy.
events.ifHigher: Composite above 58.5 with prices paid still elevated: activity is not slowing. USD bids, October odds bounce off the mid-teens.
events.ifLower: Composite under 55, or employment negative: the September spike is fading. Gold and duration bid, October 28 hold locked.

events.event: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (October final)
events.whatItIs: The University of Michigan's final October survey of household confidence, including 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations, released at 14:00 UTC, 15 minutes after the flash PMI.
events.whyItMatters: The preliminary print fell to 46.3 from September's 48.1 final, with 1-year inflation expectations at 4.7% and 5-year at 3.5%. Final revisions are usually tenths. The inflation-expectation lines are the ones the blackout Committee still reads: a jump in 5-year expectations toward 3.7% after last week's 3.7% CPI would be a hawkish overlay on whatever the PMI just did. A drop in the headline toward 44 would confirm that 4.2% unemployment and 7.5% mortgages are hitting morale into the weekend.
events.ifHigher: Headline above 48, or 5-year expectations down to 3.3%: households are stabilising. Modest equity bid, a calmer setup for October 28.
events.ifLower: Headline under 44, or 5-year expectations at 3.7%+: morale is cracking or inflation psychology is worsening. Equities sold, a hawkish overlay on the PMI.

2026-10-26.summary: FOMC, Microsoft + Alphabet + Amazon, and Q3 GDP plus PCE headline the week.

events.event: FOMC blackout in force through October 29 -- no Fed speakers until Friday
events.whatItIs: The Federal Reserve's communications blackout for the October 27-28 FOMC. It opened at 04:00 UTC on Saturday October 17 and runs through 03:59 UTC on Thursday October 29.
events.whyItMatters: Every reprice into Wednesday's statement happens on data and earnings, not on a governor's podium. October hike odds sit near 8 to 10% after Warsh declined to signal a move, even with CPI at 3.7% and PPI at 6.3%. Durable goods, consumer confidence, Australia CPI, the UK Budget, and the BoC all print inside blackout. Friday's Daly and Musalem appearances are the first named Fed voices after the window lifts.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- no Fed communication until the Wednesday statement. Data, the BoC, and mega-cap earnings set the tape into October 28.
events.ifLower: N/A -- no Fed communication until the Wednesday statement. Data, the BoC, and mega-cap earnings set the tape into October 28.

events.event: New Zealand Labour Day -- NZX and NZ cash markets closed
events.whatItIs: A New Zealand public holiday. The NZX, NZ government-bond market, and onshore NZD cash session are shut.
events.whyItMatters: The RBNZ hikes-or-holds at 01:00 UTC Wednesday, 10 days before the November 7 general election. A closed Monday cash tape leaves NZD and NZ futures to absorb any weekend oil or US-index headline without an onshore bid. Tuesday is the first full NZ session into that decision.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- market holiday.
events.ifLower: N/A -- market holiday.

events.event: CPC Fifth Plenum (October 26-29) -- 15th Five-Year Plan framework
events.whatItIs: The Chinese Communist Party's Fifth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee, the meeting that sets the framework for the 15th Five-Year Plan covering 2026-2030.
events.whyItMatters: Last week's China Q3 GDP printed 4.5% year over year and 1.2% quarter on quarter. The Plenum is the growth-and-industrial-policy colour of the week, running through Thursday beside FOMC, GDP, and the ECB. A growth-at-all-costs communique would bid copper, iron ore, and China ADRs into the US decision. A security-and-self-reliance draft would leave the Asia cyclical bid on hold until the Saturday NBS PMIs.
events.ifHigher: A growth-and-stimulus-heavy communique: CNH and China cyclicals bid, a modest risk-on overlay on Wednesday's FOMC.
events.ifLower: A security-first, low-stimulus draft: CNH offered, copper and iron ore sold, a softer Asia setup into Friday's BoJ.

events.whatItIs: The Ifo Institute's monthly survey of German firms' current conditions and six-month expectations, released at 09:00 UTC, the first German sentiment print of a five-bank week.
events.whyItMatters: Friday's German flash manufacturing PMI printed 54.2, above the 53.5 consensus, while the eurozone composite cooled to 51.9. Consensus is a hold at 89.8. A drop through 88 would say German industry is not looking through $117 Brent and would sell the euro into Tuesday's Lagarde appearance. A bounce above 91 would keep October 29 as a live ECB hike tail after 3.8% HICP.
events.ifHigher: Above 91: German firms are looking through energy. EUR bids, Bunds sold, a firmer setup for Thursday's ECB.
events.ifLower: Under 88: the factory rebound is stalling. EUR sold, October 29 hold locked.

events.whatItIs: Verizon's third-quarter results, released before the US cash open, covering wireless service revenue, postpaid net additions, and fiber.
events.whyItMatters: Verizon is the week's first large-cap print and the telecom tell after last week's AI-capex hangover. A clean service-revenue beat would bid defensive telcos into Tuesday's Coca-Cola and Boeing cluster. A postpaid miss would be a consumer-wireless crack the morning of durable goods.
events.ifHigher: Service revenue and postpaid beat: telcos and the Dow bid, a firmer open into Tuesday.
events.ifLower: A postpaid miss or a fiber guide-down: telcos sold, a soft overlay on Tuesday's consumer-confidence print.

events.event: Coca-Cola, Boeing, UPS Q3 earnings (before open)
events.whatItIs: The Tuesday before-open cluster. Coca-Cola is the global beverage and pricing print. Boeing is the commercial-delivery and defense-backlog print. UPS is the package-volume and industrial-shipping print.
events.whyItMatters: Friday's S&P closed 7,623.68 with oil at $103 and the Nasdaq still digesting last week's Tesla-Meta tape. These three are the non-AI open of the mega-cap week: consumer pricing, aircraft deliveries, and freight. A clean Coca-Cola beat with Boeing deliveries holding would bid the Dow into Visa after the close. A UPS volume miss would sell cyclicals the morning of durable goods and consumer confidence.
events.ifHigher: Coca-Cola holds pricing and Boeing deliveries hold: the Dow bids, a firmer open into Visa and the FOMC.
events.ifLower: A UPS volume miss or a Boeing delivery slip: cyclicals sold, a growth overlay on Wednesday's Fed day.

events.forecast: +1.4% MoM headline; core capital goods +0.7%; core durables about +0.6%
events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's monthly report on new orders for manufactured durable goods, including the core capital-goods line that feeds business-investment estimates in GDP, released at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the last factory-orders read before Wednesday's FOMC and Thursday's Q3 GDP. Consensus is a 1.4% bounce after August's 0.1% dip, with core capital goods cooling to 0.7% from 1.6%. A core miss below zero would be a capex crack the morning of Microsoft and Alphabet, and would lean on the 3.0% GDP consensus. A 2% headline with core still at 1% would say equipment demand is holding through 7.5% mortgages and $103 oil.
events.ifHigher: Headline above +2.0% with core capital goods still positive: equipment demand is holding. USD bids, a firmer growth setup for Thursday's GDP.
events.ifLower: Core capital goods at 0.0% or below: capex is rolling over. Equities sold, a soft overlay on Wednesday's FOMC hold.

events.event: Conference Board Consumer Confidence (October) and New Home Sales (September)
events.whatItIs: The Conference Board's monthly household-confidence survey, plus the Census Bureau's count of new single-family houses sold, both released at 14:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Confidence is seen easing to 80.4 from 81.9. New home sales are seen dropping to 650,000 after August's 684,000, with mortgage rates still near 7.4%. A confidence drop through 78 next to a sales print under 620,000 would say 3.7% CPI and $103 oil are hitting households the afternoon before the FOMC. A confidence hold above 82 would be a small bid into Wednesday.
events.ifHigher: Confidence above 82, or sales above 700,000: households and builders are holding. Modest equity bid into the FOMC.
events.ifLower: Confidence under 78, or sales under 620,000: morale and housing are cracking. Equities sold, a soft overlay on Wednesday's hold.

events.whatItIs: Scheduled remarks from the ECB President, the named euro-area policy voice of a Fed-blackout Tuesday, 20 hours before the FOMC and two days before the ECB decision.
events.whyItMatters: Eurozone HICP is running at 3.8%. The ECB hiked to 2.50% in September and is 96% priced to hold Thursday. Lagarde speaks after durable goods and consumer confidence, into Visa after the close. A line that another hike is live in December would bid the euro into Wednesday's Fed day. A patient, France-aware tone would leave Thursday's decision as a hold-and-wait.
events.ifHigher: Lagarde treats a December hike as live: EUR bids, Bunds sold.
events.ifLower: Patient, data-dependent, or financial-conditions-aware language: EUR sold, Thursday's hold locked.

events.whatItIs: Visa's fiscal fourth-quarter results, posted around 20:01 UTC. Payments volume, cross-border yield, and 2027 guidance are the lines the tape trades.
events.whyItMatters: Visa is the global-spend tell the night before FOMC, Microsoft, and Alphabet. A payments-volume beat with cross-border holding would bid financials and the consumer-tech complex into Wednesday. A volume miss would be the first card-spend crack after last week's 0.8% retail-sales bounce, and would sit on the tape through the Fed statement.
events.ifHigher: Volume and cross-border beat with 2027 guide held: payments and the Nasdaq bid overnight into the FOMC.
events.ifLower: A volume miss or a yield cut: financials sold overnight, a weaker open into Wednesday's mega-cap cluster.

events.event: API Weekly Crude Oil Stock Change (week ending October 23)
events.previous: -4.93 million barrels (API, week ending October 16); EIA official -3.06 million
events.whatItIs: The American Petroleum Institute's unofficial weekly estimate of US commercial crude stocks, released at 20:30 UTC, the afternoon before the official EIA report.
events.whyItMatters: WTI last printed $103.27 with Brent at $116.72, the highest since April, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia and Iran strike threats. API is the positioning print for Wednesday's 14:30 UTC EIA, which lands two and a half hours before the FOMC statement. Another large draw overnight would put $105 in play into the Fed. A build would lean on a market that has already reclaimed $100.
events.ifHigher: A build of 3 million barrels or more: the surplus is growing. WTI sold overnight into the FOMC.
events.ifLower: A draw of 3 million barrels or more: last week's draw is extending. WTI bids toward $105 into Wednesday's EIA and the Fed.

events.event: Australia CPI (September 2026) -- headline and trimmed mean
events.previous: +0.4% MoM / +4.0% YoY headline; trimmed mean +0.2% MoM / +3.6% YoY (August 2026)
events.forecast: +0.7% MoM / +4.2% YoY headline; trimmed mean +0.3% MoM
events.whatItIs: The Australian Bureau of Statistics monthly consumer-price index, including the RBA's preferred trimmed-mean measure, released at 00:30 UTC, six days before the November 3 RBA decision.
events.whyItMatters: The RBA hiked to 4.60% in October. Headline is seen accelerating to 4.2% as the same energy impulse that took US CPI to 3.7% hits the Australian basket. Trimmed mean at 0.3% on the month would keep November 3 as a live hike. A 4.0% hold with trimmed mean still at 0.2% would let the RBA wait, and would sell the Aussie into the RBNZ an hour later.
events.ifHigher: Headline at 4.4%+ or trimmed mean at 0.5%+: energy is leaking into core. AUD bids, November 3 RBA hike odds jump.
events.ifLower: Headline at 4.0% or below with trimmed mean at 0.2%: the impulse is contained. AUD sold, November 3 hold firmer.

events.whatItIs: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand's Monetary Policy Review, OCR decision, and Governor Anna Breman's statement, released at 01:00 UTC, 10 days before the November 7 general election.
events.whyItMatters: Q3 CPI printed 0.7% quarter on quarter and 3.7% year over year, a touch below the RBNZ's 3.9% forecast, but core measures firmed and oil has risen about 20% since the September meeting. Markets price about 21bp of a 25bp hike to 3.00%, the third consecutive increase. A hold 10 days before the election would be the shock. A hike with a December move still live would bid the kiwi into the FOMC.
events.ifHigher: Hike to 3.00% with December still live, or a 50bp move: NZD spikes, front-end NZ yields jump.
events.ifLower: Hold at 2.75%, or a hike framed as the last of 2026: NZD sold, a softer dollar-bloc setup into the FOMC.

events.whatItIs: The GfK monthly survey of German household income expectations, willingness to buy, and economic outlook, released at 07:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Monday's Ifo is the firm half of German sentiment. This is the household half, the same morning as the UK Budget and hours before the FOMC. Consensus is a modest improvement to -29.1. A drop back through -32 next to $117 Brent would say German households are not looking through energy, and would sell the euro into Lagarde's Thursday decision. A bounce above -27 would be a small EUR bid into the Fed.
events.ifHigher: Above -27: households are stabilising. Modest EUR bid into the FOMC.
events.ifLower: Under -32: morale is cracking on energy. EUR sold, a softer setup for Thursday's ECB.

events.event: UK Autumn Budget 2026 -- Chancellor John Healey / OBR forecasts
events.whatItIs: The first Budget of the Burnham government. Chancellor John Healey presents tax, spending, and gilt-issuance plans, with the Office for Budget Responsibility publishing a full forecast the same afternoon, around 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the sterling event of the week and it lands four and a half hours before the FOMC. Gilt dealers look for about £3.4 billion of extra issuance, taking the gilt remit toward £249.6 billion, with the long-dated share the lowest since 1990. The 10-year gilt last yielded about 5.38%. A tax-and-spend package that adds to the remit would sell gilts and sterling into the Fed. A tighter remit with a credible OBR path would bid both.
events.ifHigher: A larger gilt remit, or OBR forecasts that lift borrowing: gilts sold, GBP offered into the FOMC.
events.ifLower: A tighter remit with a credible OBR consolidation path: gilts bid, GBP supported, a calmer sterling overlay on the Fed.

events.event: Bank of Canada Rate Decision + Monetary Policy Report + Macklem Press Conference (14:30 UTC)
events.forecast: Hike 25bp to 2.50% (~75 to 85% priced); Reuters 19 of 34 economists
events.whatItIs: The Bank of Canada's policy-rate announcement at 13:45 UTC, the quarterly Monetary Policy Report, and Governor Tiff Macklem's press conference at 14:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This would be the BoC's first hike in a year. Overnight swaps price about 75 to 85% of a move to 2.50% after Macklem said the inflation outlook is 'quite a bit higher' and September CPI printed 3.1%. A hold against that strip would sell the loonie into the FOMC two hours later. A hike with an MPR that lifts the inflation track would bid CAD and put a hawkish overlay on a Fed that is priced to sit still.
events.ifHigher: Hike to 2.50% with a hawkish MPR, or a 50bp move: CAD bids, USD/CAD sold, a hawkish North American overlay on the FOMC.
events.ifLower: Hold at 2.25%, or a hike framed as one-and-done: CAD sold, a quieter setup for a Fed hold.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending October 23)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly change in commercial crude stocks, excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, released at 14:30 UTC, covering crude, gasoline, distillates, and Cushing.
events.whyItMatters: WTI last printed $103.27 with Brent at $116.72, tagging the highest close since April after Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities. Last week's official print was a 3.06 million-barrel draw. API on Tuesday is the only preview. A second large draw would put $105 in play two and a half hours before the FOMC statement and would feed the energy overlay on last week's 3.7% CPI. A build would take some heat off the hold.
events.ifHigher: A build of 3 million barrels or more: the surplus is growing. WTI sold, a small relief bid for duration into the FOMC.
events.ifLower: A draw of 3 million barrels or more: last week's draw is extending. WTI bids toward $105, inflation-sensitive equities soften into the statement.

events.event: FOMC Rate Decision + Warsh Press Conference (18:30 UTC)
events.whatItIs: The Federal Open Market Committee's policy decision at 18:00 UTC, followed by Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 18:30 UTC. This is a non-projection meeting: no dot plot and no updated Summary of Economic Projections accompany the statement.
events.whyItMatters: A hold is the base case after September's 25bp hike. Futures price only about an 8 to 10% chance of another quarter-point, with December still the live meeting at roughly 75 to 85%. Warsh has declined to give forward guidance, so the entire reaction hinges on the statement diff and the vote split. Any dissent for a hike would be read as December being locked. Microsoft and Alphabet report two hours later; a hawkish hold next to a capex-raise from either is the mix that extends last week's AI fade.
events.ifHigher: Surprise hike, or a hold with explicit hawkish dissents: USD spikes, gold and BTC sold, December odds jump, equities de-risk into Microsoft and Alphabet.
events.ifLower: Hold with softened inflation language or a unanimous patient vote: relief rally in gold, duration, and risk; USD gives back; December odds unwind.

events.event: Microsoft and Alphabet Q3 earnings (after close)
events.forecast: Microsoft EPS about $4.71 (year-ago $4.13), revenue guided $89.85 to $90.95 billion, call 21:30 UTC; Alphabet EPS about $2.94 (year-ago $2.87), call 20:30 UTC
events.whatItIs: The Wednesday after-close mega-cap pair. Microsoft is the Azure, Intelligent Cloud, and FY27 AI-capex print. Alphabet is the Search, YouTube, Cloud, and capex-guide print. Both report a few hours after the FOMC statement.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's equity fulcrum, and it lands on a Fed night. Last week's Nasdaq lost 0.7% as the AI-capex complex unwound after Tesla and Meta. Azure's growth rate and both firms' 2027 capex guides are the lines the tape trades. A beat with a capex hold would bid the complex overnight into Amazon. A beat with a capex raise would extend the fade: earnings quality, spend still going up, the same mix that punished the complex last week.
events.ifHigher: Azure holds the guide and both capex lines stay contained: Nasdaq bids overnight, a firmer setup for Amazon and Thursday's GDP.
events.ifLower: An Azure miss or a capex raise from either name: Nasdaq sold overnight, a growth-scare overlay on Thursday's GDP, PCE, and Amazon.

events.event: Eli Lilly and Mastercard Q3 earnings (before open)
events.forecast: Lilly EPS about $5.38 (year-ago $7.02), call 14:00 UTC; Mastercard EPS about $5.14
events.whatItIs: The Thursday before-open pair. Eli Lilly is the GLP-1 volume, pricing, and pipeline print. Mastercard is the payments-volume and cross-border print, the companion to Tuesday's Visa.
events.whyItMatters: Lilly is the largest healthcare name of the week and a Dow-adjacent mega-cap the morning of GDP and PCE. Consensus EPS is well below last year's $7.02, so the event is volume and 2027 guidance, not the beat. Mastercard is the second-look at card spend after Visa. A Lilly guide-down next to a Mastercard volume miss would sell healthcare and payments into the 12:30 UTC GDP window.
events.ifHigher: Lilly holds 2027 guide and Mastercard volume beats: healthcare and payments bid, a firmer open into GDP.
events.ifLower: A Lilly guide-down or a Mastercard volume miss: both sold, a softer overlay on GDP, PCE, and Amazon.

events.event: Falcon Finance (FF) Token Unlock (~$7.5 million ecosystem, ~2.2% of float)
events.whatItIs: A scheduled Falcon Finance (FF) vesting release of 75 million tokens for the ecosystem, estimated around $7.5 million (about 2.2% of circulating supply) at 11:52 UTC. A separate vesting model projects a larger combined release across allocations the same day.
events.whyItMatters: Bitcoin last printed about $81,260 on Friday, well off last week's $83,000s, into a Nasdaq that is about to trade GDP, PCE, the ECB, and Amazon. A $7.5 million FF cliff is not last month's $856 million HYPE event, but it is the week's largest named unlock on the Tokenomist / DefiLlama calendars. A clean hold in FF and BTC is constructive. A break that pulls ETH beta is a small supply test on a data-heavy Thursday.
events.ifHigher: FF absorbs the unlock and BTC holds $81,000: demand matched the supply. Constructive for mid-cap alts into Amazon.
events.ifLower: FF breaks and pulls ETH beta: the overhang hits a data-heavy Thursday. Altcoin risk-off, BTC relatively more resilient.

events.event: Q3 GDP (advance) -- real GDP, consumption, GDP price index
events.forecast: +3.0% annualized; consumption about +3.4%; GDP price index about +3.5%
events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's first look at third-quarter real GDP, released at 12:30 UTC, covering output, consumption, investment, net exports, and the GDP price index.
events.whyItMatters: This is the growth half of Thursday's double BEA dump, 18 hours after the FOMC. Consensus is 3.0% after Q2's 2.2%, with the Atlanta Fed GDPNow nearer 3.5%. A 3.5% print the morning after a Fed hold would say the Committee is not tightening into weakness and would bid the dollar into the ECB. A miss at 2.0% or below would be the growth scare Amazon then has to trade, and would pull December hike odds down.
events.ifHigher: Above +3.5% with consumption still firm: the expansion is accelerating. USD bids, December hike odds firm, equities mixed into PCE.
events.ifLower: Under +2.0%, or consumption rolling over: growth is cooling. Gold and duration bid, December odds fade, a softer setup for Amazon.

events.event: Core PCE, Personal Income, and Personal Spending (September 2026)
events.previous: Core PCE +0.2% MoM / +3.0% YoY; headline PCE +0.3% MoM / +3.4% YoY; income +0.2%; spending +0.9% (August 2026)
events.forecast: Core PCE +0.3% MoM / +3.1% YoY; headline PCE +0.5% MoM / +3.6% YoY; income +0.3%; spending +0.3% (real about +0.1%)
