events.actual: Headline +0.5% MoM / +3.6% YoY; core +0.3% MoM / +3.1% YoY; income +0.2%; spending +0.5%
events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's Personal Income and Outlays report: the core PCE price index the FOMC targets, plus headline PCE, personal income, and personal spending, released at 12:30 UTC in the same window as advance GDP.
events.whyItMatters: This is the inflation event of the week, and it lands the morning after the FOMC rather than before it. Core is seen at 0.3% on the month and 3.1% on the year after last week's 3.7% CPI and 0.3% monthly core. A 0.4% core print would reopen December as a near-lock the day after an October hold. A 0.2% hold would confirm Warsh's wait-and-see and would bid gold into the ECB.
events.ifHigher: Core at +0.4% MoM or +3.3% YoY: energy is leaking into the Fed's target. USD bids, December hike odds jump, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Core at +0.2% MoM or below: the impulse is contained. Gold and duration bid, December odds fade, a calmer setup for Amazon.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly count of first-time unemployment filings, plus continuing claims, released at 12:30 UTC in the same window as GDP and PCE.
events.whyItMatters: Claims have been sitting under 200,000 even as September payrolls slowed to 29,000. A jump toward 230,000 the morning after the FOMC would be the first weekly confirmation that the payrolls miss was a trend, and would fade December hike odds. Another sub-200,000 print would say layoffs have not started and would keep PCE as an inflation story, not a labour story.
events.ifHigher: Above 230K: the first real crack in weekly filings. Gold and duration bid, December odds fade.
events.ifLower: Below 190K: still tight. USD bids, the 29,000 payrolls print still looks like a one-month miss.

events.event: ECB Rate Decision + Lagarde Press Conference (13:45 UTC)
events.forecast: Hold at 2.50% (~96% priced); December hike still live
events.whatItIs: The ECB Governing Council's policy decision at 13:15 UTC, covering the deposit facility, main refinancing, and marginal lending rates, followed by President Christine Lagarde's press conference at 13:45 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: A hold is fully priced after the September hike. Eurozone HICP is running at 3.8%, Friday's composite PMI cooled to 51.9, and French spreads have done some of the tightening for the Council. The live issue is December. A Lagarde line that another hike is live would bid the euro into Amazon. A France-aware, energy-look-through press conference would sell it. US GDP and PCE will already be on the tape.
events.ifHigher: Surprise hike, or a hold that treats December as live: EUR bids, Bunds sold.
events.ifLower: Hold with patient, financial-conditions-aware language: EUR sold, December odds fade, a quieter setup for Friday's eurozone GDP.

events.whatItIs: Amazon's third-quarter results, posted around 20:01 UTC, covering AWS growth, North America retail margin, advertising, and 2027 capex. The call starts at 21:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Amazon closes the hyperscaler trio the night after Microsoft and Alphabet and the same day as GDP, PCE, and the ECB. AWS growth and the capex guide are the lines. A beat with a capex hold would bid the Nasdaq into Friday's ECI and BoJ. A capex raise after whatever Microsoft and Alphabet just did would extend the AI-spend fade into the weekend, against oil still above $100.
events.ifHigher: AWS beats and capex is contained: Nasdaq bids overnight, a firmer setup for Friday's ECI and energy earnings.
events.ifLower: An AWS miss or a capex raise: Nasdaq sold overnight, a growth-scare overlay on Friday's BoJ, ECI, and Exxon.

events.whatItIs: The Statistics Bureau's Tokyo consumer-price index, the lead on the national CPI, including the Bank of Japan's preferred core measure that excludes fresh food, released at 23:30 UTC on Friday, three and a half hours before the BoJ decision.
events.whyItMatters: Core is seen easing a tenth to 2.6%. Last week's national CPI and a still-hot PPI kept BoJ tightening talk alive. A 2.8% core print the morning of the decision would reopen an October hike that markets have only about 5% on. A drop to 2.4% would lock the hold and sell the yen into Ueda's Outlook Report.
events.ifHigher: Core at 2.8%+: energy is passing through. JPY bids, JGBs sold, October hike odds bounce off the single digits.
events.ifLower: Core at 2.4% or below: the pipeline is not reaching Tokyo households. JPY sold, Friday's hold locked.

events.event: BoJ Rate Decision + Quarterly Outlook Report
events.whatItIs: The Bank of Japan's policy decision after the October 29-30 meeting, including the Statement on Monetary Policy and The Bank's View of the Quarterly Outlook Report, released around 03:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: A hold is the base case after September's 25bp hike to 1.25%, the highest policy rate since 1995. Markets price only about 5% of another October move, with December at 1.50% the majority case. Governor Ueda has said underlying inflation is near 2% and that the Bank will not tolerate an overshoot. A hike against a 5% strip would spike the yen into the US ECI window. A hold with an Outlook Report that lifts the inflation track would still bid JPY.
events.ifHigher: Surprise hike, or a hold that treats December as live with a lifted inflation track: JPY bids, JGBs sold.
events.ifLower: Hold with a downgraded inflation track or a dovish dissent: JPY sold, USD/JPY tests the 157s into the US session.

events.whatItIs: Destatis's first estimate of German real GDP for the third quarter, released at 07:00 UTC, three hours before the eurozone flash.
events.whyItMatters: Germany is the factory half of Friday's European GDP cluster. Consensus is a slowdown to 0.1% after Q2's 0.3%. Friday's flash manufacturing PMI at 54.2 argued the factory rebound is intact; a 0.1% GDP print would say that has not yet shown up in output. A contraction would sell the euro into the eurozone print and into a Fed-blackout-lifted US session. A 0.3% hold would keep the German activity bid alive after Thursday's ECB hold.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.3% QoQ: the rebound is in the accounts. EUR bids, European cyclicals supported.
events.ifLower: 0.0% or a contraction: Germany stalled. EUR sold into the eurozone flash.

events.event: Eurozone GDP (Q3 2026, flash) and Unemployment Rate (September)
events.whatItIs: Eurostat's first estimate of euro-area real GDP for the third quarter, plus the September unemployment rate, released at 10:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the euro-area growth print the morning after the ECB hold. Consensus is a slowdown to 0.2% after a 0.6% Q2, with unemployment unchanged at 6.4%. Friday's composite PMI cooled to 51.9. A 0.0% print would confirm that cooling in the accounts and would sell the euro into the US ECI window. A 0.4% hold would say the PMI dip was a one-month miss and would keep December as a live ECB hike.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.4% QoQ with unemployment still at 6.4%: the expansion is holding. EUR bids, December hike odds firm.
events.ifLower: 0.0% or a contraction, or unemployment at 6.6%+: growth stalled. EUR sold, December hold firmer.

events.event: Exxon Mobil and Chevron Q3 earnings (before open)
events.forecast: Exxon EPS about $3.96 (year-ago $1.88), call 13:30 UTC; Chevron N/A
events.whatItIs: The Friday before-open energy pair. Exxon is the upstream-volume, refining-margin, and buyback print. Chevron is the companion supermajor print. Both report against WTI at $103 and Brent at $117.
events.whyItMatters: Energy is the inflation overlay on the whole week. A clean Exxon beat with a buyback hold would bid the oil complex into ECI and German CPI. A production miss or a buyback cut would lean on a market that has already tagged six-month highs, and would take some energy heat off the December Fed-hike debate. Amazon will already have set the Nasdaq overnight; these two set the energy half of the Friday open.
events.ifHigher: Exxon beats with buybacks held: energy and the Dow bid, a firmer open into ECI.
events.ifLower: A production miss or a buyback cut: energy sold, a small relief bid for duration into ECI and German CPI.

events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' quarterly index of total compensation for civilian workers, covering wages and benefits, released at 12:30 UTC, the last major US labour-cost print before December's FOMC.
events.whyItMatters: The ECI is the wage gauge the FOMC trusts more than average hourly earnings, because it is not distorted by mix shifts. Consensus is a cooling to 0.8% from 0.9%. A 1.0% print the morning after a 0.3% core PCE would reopen December as a near-lock and would bid the dollar into Daly and Musalem. A 0.6% miss would say the 29,000 payrolls cooling is showing up in pay, and would fade December odds.
events.ifHigher: Above +1.0%: pay is not cooling. USD bids, December hike odds jump, gold sold.
events.ifLower: At +0.6% or below: wage growth is rolling over. Gold and duration bid, December odds fade.

events.event: Germany CPI (October 2026, preliminary) -- MoM and YoY
events.whatItIs: Destatis's flash estimate of German consumer prices, including the HICP measure that feeds eurozone inflation, released at 13:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the first national inflation print after Thursday's ECB hold. Consensus is a slowdown to 0.1% on the month and about 3.1% on the year as the September energy spike rolls. A 0.4% monthly print would say $117 Brent is still in the German basket and would reopen December as a live ECB hike. A 0.0% or negative print would confirm the look-through case Lagarde just made.
events.ifHigher: MoM at +0.4% or YoY at 3.4%+: energy is still in the basket. EUR bids, December ECB hike odds jump.
events.ifLower: MoM at 0.0% or below: the impulse is rolling off. EUR sold, December hold firmer.

events.whatItIs: The ISM-Chicago monthly survey of purchasing managers in the Chicago area, a diffusion index where 50 separates expansion from contraction, released at 13:45 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Friday's national flash PMI printed 56.0 manufacturing and 57.6 composite. Chicago is the regional follow-up, seen cooling to 55.9 from a very hot 58.8. A hold above 58 would be a hawkish overlay on whatever ECI just did. A drop through 50 would be the first contraction signal of the autumn and would fade December odds into Daly and Musalem.
events.ifHigher: Above 58: the September spike is not fading. USD bids, a hawkish overlay on ECI.
events.ifLower: Under 50: Chicago is contracting. Gold bid, December odds fade.

events.event: Fed's Daly and Musalem Speak -- first named voices after blackout
events.whatItIs: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly gives introductory remarks at 16:00 UTC. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem delivers a keynote at 16:30 UTC. Both are the first named Fed voices after the October 29 blackout ends.
events.whyItMatters: Warsh will have given the press conference on Wednesday with no forward guidance. Daly and Musalem are the first chance the tape gets to hear how the rest of the Committee reads a hold next to Thursday's GDP and PCE. A hike-live line after a 0.4% core PCE would lock December. A patient, labour-aware line after a 0.8% ECI would let December odds sit. Midterms are four sessions later.
events.ifHigher: Either treats a December hike as live or flags sticky wages: USD bids, gold sold, December odds jump.
events.ifLower: Patient, data-dependent, or labour-cooling language: USD sold, a quieter setup for next week's ISM and NFP.

2026-11-02.summary: October NFP, BoE and RBA hikes, and US midterms headline the week.

events.previous: November quotas held at September levels (Oct 4 meeting)
events.forecast: Hold December quotas; no change widely expected
events.actual: December quotas held at September 2026 levels
events.whatItIs: The monthly virtual meeting of the seven OPEC+ countries that still manage voluntary output adjustments: Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman.
events.whyItMatters: WTI settled Friday at $104.12 and Brent at $117.64, still at April highs, after Houthi attacks and Iran strike threats. Reuters sources on October 27 said the group is likely to keep December targets unchanged, the same hold it delivered for November, because Gulf members are still pumping well below paper quotas while the Iran war disrupts exports. A surprise output hike against $104 oil would be the only supply relief on the tape. A hold, or language that 2027 quota talks are delayed again, leaves energy as an inflation overlay on Tuesday's midterms and Friday's payrolls.
events.ifHigher: A surprise quota increase, or language that extra barrels are coming in December: WTI sold, a small relief bid for duration into NFP.
events.ifLower: Hold, or a cut, or a statement that 2027 capacity talks are delayed: WTI bids toward $105-110, a hawkish overlay on the BoE and December Fed pricing.

events.event: Japan Culture Day -- TSE and Japan cash markets closed
events.whatItIs: A Japanese national holiday. The Tokyo Stock Exchange, JGBs, and onshore JPY cash session are shut.
events.whyItMatters: The BoJ held at 1.25% on Friday on an 8-1 vote, with Takata dissenting for 1.50%, and USD/JPY last sat near 157.6. A closed Tokyo cash tape leaves the yen to absorb Sunday's OPEC+ headline and Monday's China RatingDog PMI without an onshore bid. Tuesday is the first full Japan session into the RBA decision.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- market holiday.
events.ifLower: N/A -- market holiday.

events.whatItIs: The S&P Global / RatingDog (formerly Caixin) survey of private-sector manufacturers in China, weighted toward smaller coastal exporters, released at 01:45 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Saturday's official NBS manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 from 50.1, missing 50.0, the fastest contraction in three months, with new export orders at 48.7. RatingDog is the private-sector follow-up, seen easing to 51.6 from 52.1. A drop through 50 would confirm that official weakness is not just SOEs and would sell copper, iron ore, and CNH into Tuesday's RBA. A hold above 52 would say the private export complex is still expanding even as the official print contracted.
events.ifHigher: Above 52.5: private factories are still expanding. CNH and China cyclicals bid, a firmer Asia setup into the RBA.
events.ifLower: At 50.0 or below: the official contraction is showing up in private exporters. CNH offered, copper and iron ore sold.

events.whatItIs: The final HCOB / S&P Global euro-area manufacturing PMI, confirming or revising Friday's 52.4 flash, released at 09:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Friday's flash at 52.4 held the expansion, with Germany at 54.2. The ECB held at 2.50% on Thursday and left December as a live hike after 3.8% HICP. A downward revision through 51 would say the factory rebound is stalling next to $117 Brent and would sell the euro into Wednesday's flash CPI. A revision up through 53 would keep December as a live ECB meeting.
events.ifHigher: Final above 53: the factory rebound is firming. EUR bids, a firmer setup for Wednesday's CPI.
events.ifLower: Final at 51 or below: the flash overstated the rebound. EUR sold, December ECB hold firmer.

events.whatItIs: The final S&P Global UK manufacturing PMI, confirming or revising Friday's 52.8 flash, released at 09:30 UTC, three days before the Bank of England decision.
events.whyItMatters: The BoE is about 99% priced to hike to 4.00% on Thursday after September CPI at 3.5%. A final PMI that holds 52.8 says factories are expanding into that hike. A revision down through 51 would be the activity crack that lets the 7-2 vote-split talk (Dhingra and Taylor holding) leak into sterling.
events.ifHigher: Final above 53.5: UK factories are holding. Modest GBP bid into Thursday's hike.
events.ifLower: Final at 51 or below: activity is rolling over into a hike. GBP offered, a softer overlay on the MPC.

events.whatItIs: The Institute for Supply Management's monthly survey of US factory purchasing managers. A reading above 50 signals expansion. The prices-paid subindex is the inflation line the FOMC reads.
events.whyItMatters: This is the first US activity print after Wednesday's hawkish hold. Friday's S&P Global flash manufacturing PMI was 56.0 and Chicago PMI cooled to 55.3 from 58.8. Consensus is a small rise to 54.7. A drop through 52 next to prices paid still above 75 would be the stagflation mix into Tuesday's JOLTS and Friday's payrolls. A 56-handle with prices paid rolling off would be the Goldilocks mix that lets December odds sit.
events.ifHigher: Above 56 with prices paid still hot: factories and pipeline inflation are both firming. USD bids, December hike odds jump.
events.ifLower: Under 52, or prices paid rolling toward 60: the factory rebound is stalling. Gold bid, December odds fade into JOLTS.

events.whatItIs: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee moderates a discussion at 16:15 UTC, the first named Fed voice of a post-FOMC, post-blackout week.
events.whyItMatters: The Committee held 3.75-4.00% on a 10-2 vote Wednesday. Logan on Friday called for two more hikes. Goolsbee is a 2026 voter and tends to be the labour-aware voice. A hike-live line after ISM would lock December into Tuesday's midterms. A patient, labour-cooling line after a 29,000 payrolls hangover would let December odds sit through JOLTS.
events.ifHigher: Treats a December hike as live or flags sticky prices paid: USD bids, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Patient, data-dependent, or labour-cooling language: USD sold, a quieter setup for JOLTS and NFP.

events.event: Apple and Palantir Q4/Q3 earnings (after close)
events.forecast: Apple EPS about $1.98 (year-ago $1.85), call 22:00 UTC; Palantir EPS about $0.33 (year-ago $0.18), call 22:00 UTC
events.whatItIs: The Monday after-close pair. Apple is the iPhone, Services, and FY27 capex print. Palantir is the US commercial and AIP-adoption print. Both report against a Nasdaq that just lost 2.9% on Intel and Amazon.
events.whyItMatters: Apple is about $5 trillion of market cap and the consumer-hardware tell after Friday's AI-spend fade. Services growth and the 2027 capex line are what the tape trades, not the $1.98 EPS. Palantir is the software-AI companion after last week's Microsoft-Alphabet-Amazon cluster. A clean Apple beat with capex contained would bid the Nasdaq into Tuesday's midterms. A capex raise, or an iPhone miss, would extend Friday's fade into AMD on Tuesday.
events.ifHigher: Apple holds Services and capex, Palantir beats US commercial: Nasdaq bids overnight into midterms and AMD.
events.ifLower: An iPhone miss or a capex raise: Nasdaq sold overnight, a growth overlay on Tuesday's JOLTS and the election tape.

events.event: US midterm elections -- House, Senate, and gubernatorial races
events.whatItIs: The 2026 US midterm elections. All 435 House seats, 35 Senate seats, and 36 governorships are on the ballot. Stock and bond markets are open as usual. Polls close from 23:00 UTC; meaningful counts run overnight into Wednesday.
events.whyItMatters: This is the political event of the week and it lands the same day as JOLTS, the RBA, and AMD. Polls have pointed to Democrats having a path to the House and a chance at the Senate, which would constrain the Trump administration's remaining legislative agenda. A Republican hold of both chambers would be read as continuity on tariffs, energy, and the fiscal path. A Democratic House would be read as a check on further tax and tariff moves, a modest bid for duration, and a question mark over 2027 fiscal expansion. Futures will reprice into the Wednesday cash open.
events.ifHigher: Republican hold of House and Senate: tariff-and-fiscal continuity. USD mixed-to-firmer, energy and financials bid, a smaller check on the administration.
events.ifLower: Democratic House, or a Senate flip: divided government. Duration bid, tariff-sensitive cyclicals sold, a quieter fiscal overlay on Friday's NFP.

events.event: RBA Rate Decision + Statement on Monetary Policy + Press Conference (04:30 UTC)
events.forecast: Hike 25bp to 4.85%; about 70% priced; all four majors now on a hike
events.actual: Hiked 25bp to 4.85%; 6-3 vote (three for a hold)
events.whatItIs: The Reserve Bank of Australia's cash-rate decision at 03:30 UTC, the quarterly Statement on Monetary Policy with fresh forecasts, and Governor Michele Bullock's press conference at 04:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This would be the fifth RBA hike of 2026, taking the cash rate to an 18-year high. Q3 headline CPI printed 4.3% and trimmed mean 3.7%. CBA and NAB flipped from hold to hike after that print and after Bullock told the Senate that some inflation risks had materialised. A hold against a 70% strip would sell the Aussie into US midterms. A hike that lifts the inflation track would bid AUD and put a hawkish dollar-bloc overlay on a Fed that just held.
events.ifHigher: Hike to 4.85% with a hawkish SoMP, or a 50bp move: AUD bids, a hawkish overlay on US midterms and the BoE.
events.ifLower: Hold at 4.60%, or a hike framed as the last of 2026: AUD sold, a quieter dollar-bloc setup into NFP.

events.whatItIs: The Swiss Federal Statistical Office's monthly consumer-price index, released at 07:30 UTC, the SNB's target gauge.
events.whyItMatters: Swiss inflation is still the G10 low at 1.0%, against euro-area HICP at 3.8% and US CPI at 3.7%. Consensus is a rise to 1.3% as the energy impulse that has not fully hit the Swiss basket starts to. A jump through 1.5% would reopen SNB hike talk from a 0.00% policy rate. A hold at 1.0% would keep the franc as the G10 real-rate outlier into Wednesday's eurozone CPI.
events.ifHigher: YoY at 1.5%+: energy is arriving. CHF bids, SNB hike talk returns.
events.ifLower: YoY at 1.0% or below: still contained. CHF offered, SNB on hold into year-end.

events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey: the stock of unfilled positions on the last business day of September, plus hires, quits, and layoffs.
events.whyItMatters: This is the labour-demand print three days before October payrolls, and the first JOLTS since September's +29K NFP miss. Consensus is a small rise to 7.10 million. A drop through 6.8 million would say the payrolls miss was demand, not a one-month quirk, and would fade December hike odds into the election overnight. A hold above 7.3 million would say firms are still posting and would keep Friday's wage line as an inflation event.
events.ifHigher: Above 7.3 million: labour demand is holding. USD bids, December odds firm, a hawkish overlay on NFP.
events.ifLower: Under 6.8 million: openings are rolling over. Gold and duration bid, December odds fade into Friday.

events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's monthly report on new orders for manufactured goods, including the final durable-goods revision, released at 15:00 UTC with JOLTS.
events.whyItMatters: Tuesday's durable-goods preliminary last week printed +1.8% against +1.4% seen, led by transportation. Consensus for the broader factory-orders print is +1.2%. A miss at 0.0% would say last week's bounce was aircraft, not underlying capex, the morning of AMD. A 2% hold would keep the equipment-demand bid into ISM Services.
events.ifHigher: Above +2.0% with core capital goods still positive: equipment demand is holding. Modest USD and cyclical bid.
events.ifLower: At 0.0% or below, or core capital goods revised down: last week's bounce was aircraft. Cyclicals sold into AMD.

events.whatItIs: Advanced Micro Devices' third-quarter results, posted around 21:01 UTC, covering data-center GPU, CPU, and 2027 AI-accelerator guidance. The call starts at 22:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: AMD is the semiconductor tell the night of US midterms, after Friday's Intel plunge and the Microsoft-Alphabet-Amazon capex cluster. Data-center GPU growth and the MI300/MI350 guide are the lines. A beat with a contained capex-customer comment would bid semis into Wednesday's ISM Services. A guide-down, or a comment that hyperscaler spend is slipping, would extend the AI-fade into Uber and Qualcomm.
events.ifHigher: Data-center beats and the 2027 accelerator guide holds: semis bid overnight, a firmer Nasdaq setup into Wednesday.
events.ifLower: A GPU miss or a hyperscaler-spend warning: semis sold overnight, a growth overlay on ADP and ISM Services.

events.event: API Weekly Crude Oil Stock Change (week ending October 30)
events.previous: EIA official -1.892 million barrels (week ending October 23)
events.whatItIs: The American Petroleum Institute's unofficial weekly estimate of US commercial crude stocks, released at 21:30 UTC, the afternoon before the official EIA report.
events.whyItMatters: WTI last printed $104.12 with Brent at $117.64 after Sunday's OPEC+ hold. API is the positioning print for Wednesday's 15:30 UTC EIA. Another large draw overnight would put $105-108 in play into ISM Services and the refunding announcement. A build would lean on a market that has already tagged six-month highs.
events.ifHigher: A build of 3 million barrels or more: the surplus is growing. WTI sold overnight into EIA.
events.ifLower: A draw of 3 million barrels or more: last week's draw is extending. WTI bids toward $108 into Wednesday's EIA.

events.event: Eurozone Flash CPI (October 2026) -- headline and core HICP
events.whatItIs: Eurostat's first estimate of euro-area consumer prices for October, including the HICP the ECB targets and the core measure that excludes energy, food, alcohol, and tobacco, released at 10:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the inflation event of the European week, six days after the ECB held at 2.50% and left December live. Consensus is a tenth higher at 3.9% as energy stays in the basket, with core unchanged at 2.5%. Friday's German national CPI already printed -0.2% month on month and +2.8% year on year, cooler than the 3.1% forecast, so the euro-area print could undershoot. A 4.1% headline or a 2.7% core would lock a December ECB hike. A 3.6% headline would let Lagarde look through energy.
events.ifHigher: Headline at 4.1%+ or core at 2.7%+: energy is leaking into core. EUR bids, December ECB hike odds jump.
events.ifLower: Headline at 3.6% or below, or core at 2.3%: the German cooling is euro-area wide. EUR sold, December hold firmer.

events.event: Uber Q3 earnings (before open); Qualcomm after the close
events.forecast: Uber EPS about $0.94, call 13:00 UTC; Qualcomm after close, call in the evening
events.whatItIs: The Wednesday earnings pair. Uber reports before the open: mobility trips, delivery, and bookings. Qualcomm reports after the close: handset silicon, automotive, and the data-center/AI mix.
events.whyItMatters: Uber is the consumer-mobility tell the morning of ADP and ISM Services, against a Nasdaq that is still digesting Intel and Amazon. Bookings and the 2027 margin guide are the lines. Qualcomm is the Android-and-AI-silicon companion to Tuesday's AMD print. A clean Uber beat with Qualcomm holding the handset guide would bid consumer-tech into the BoE. An Uber bookings miss next to a Qualcomm guide-down would extend the growth fade into NFP.
events.ifHigher: Uber bookings beat and Qualcomm holds the guide: consumer-tech and semis bid into Thursday.
events.ifLower: An Uber bookings miss or a Qualcomm guide-down: both sold, a softer overlay on the BoE and NFP.

events.whatItIs: ADP's monthly estimate of private-sector payrolls, released at 13:15 UTC, two days before the official BLS Employment Situation.
events.whyItMatters: September official payrolls printed only +29K, with private +46K. ADP printed +90K that month, so the two have been diverging. Consensus is a cooling to +75K. A miss below +30K would be the first private-payroll confirmation of the BLS slowdown and would fade December odds into ISM Services. A hold above +100K would say the BLS miss was the outlier and would bid the dollar into Friday.
events.ifHigher: Above +100K: private hiring is holding. USD bids, the +29K BLS print looks like a one-month miss.
events.ifLower: Below +30K: ADP is catching down to BLS. Gold bid, December odds fade into NFP.

events.whatItIs: The Treasury's quarterly announcement of coupon-auction sizes for the November-January refunding, covering 3-year, 10-year, and 30-year supply, released around 13:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The 10-year last yielded about 4.93% after Friday's risk-off bid. Dealers look for whether Treasury lifts coupon sizes after a quarter of heavy bill issuance and a still-wide deficit. A surprise increase in 10-year or 30-year supply would cheapen the long end into ISM Services and EIA. An unchanged or smaller coupon package would be the duration bid the 4.93% 10-year has been waiting for.
events.ifHigher: Larger 10-year or 30-year coupons: duration sold, a modest USD bid, a tighter overlay on NFP.
events.ifLower: Unchanged or smaller coupons: duration bid, a calmer long-end setup into Friday.

events.whatItIs: The Institute for Supply Management's monthly survey of US services-sector purchasing managers. Services are about 70% of the economy; a reading above 50 signals expansion.
events.whyItMatters: This is the demand-side companion to Monday's ISM manufacturing print, and it lands two days before payrolls. Friday's S&P Global flash services PMI was 57.9. Consensus is a hold at 54.8. A drop through 52 with a hot prices-paid line would be the stagflation mix into NFP. A 56-handle would say the consumer-services complex is still expanding through 7.4% mortgages and $104 oil, and would keep Friday's wage print as an inflation event.
events.ifHigher: Above 56: services demand is holding. USD bids, December odds firm, a hawkish setup for NFP.
events.ifLower: Under 52: the services expansion is stalling. Gold bid, December odds fade into Friday.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending October 30)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's weekly change in commercial crude stocks, excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, released at 15:30 UTC, covering crude, gasoline, distillates, and Cushing.
events.whyItMatters: WTI last printed $104.12 with Brent at $117.64 after Sunday's OPEC+ hold. Last week's official print was a 1.89 million-barrel draw, the latest in a four-week stretch of draws that took commercial stocks to 410.6 million barrels. API on Tuesday is the only preview. A fifth draw would put $108 in play two days before payrolls and would feed the energy overlay on Wednesday's eurozone CPI. A build would take some heat off the BoE hike and December Fed pricing.
events.ifHigher: A build of 3 million barrels or more: the surplus is growing. WTI sold, a small relief bid for duration into the BoE and NFP.
events.ifLower: A draw of 3 million barrels or more: the draw streak is extending. WTI bids toward $108, inflation-sensitive equities soften into Thursday.

events.event: BoE Rate Decision + Monetary Policy Report + Bailey Press Conference (12:30 UTC)
events.previous: 3.75% (held through 2026; last change was a cut)
events.forecast: Hike 25bp to 4.00%; about 99% priced; 7-2 vote seen (Dhingra, Taylor hold)
events.whatItIs: The Bank of England's Bank Rate announcement at 12:00 UTC, the quarterly Monetary Policy Report with fresh forecasts, and Governor Andrew Bailey's press conference at 12:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This would be the first BoE hike in more than three years. September CPI printed 3.5%, services inflation 3.7%, and 22 of 25 research houses plus 54 of 63 Reuters economists look for 4.00%. Markets price it as a done deal. The live issue is the vote and the MPR inflation track: a 9-0 hike with a 4%+ 2027 forecast would bid sterling and lock February as live. A 5-4 split, or an MPR that treats this as insurance, would sell GBP into US claims and Friday's NFP.
events.ifHigher: Hike with a hawkish MPR or an 8-1 / 9-0 vote: GBP bids, gilts sold, February hike odds jump.
events.ifLower: Hold against a 99% strip, or a 5-4 hike framed as one-and-done: GBP sold, a quieter sterling overlay on NFP.

events.event: Initial Jobless Claims (week ending October 31) and Q3 Productivity (preliminary)
events.previous: Claims 194K (week ending October 24); productivity +1.4% Q2; unit labor costs +1.2% Q2
events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly first-time unemployment filings, plus the BLS preliminary third-quarter productivity and unit-labor-cost estimates, all released at 13:30 UTC, the morning after the BoE and the day before NFP.
events.whyItMatters: Claims have been sitting under 200,000 even as September payrolls slowed to 29,000. A jump toward 230,000 the day before NFP would be the weekly confirmation that the payrolls miss is a trend. Productivity is seen jumping to 3.1% after Q3 GDP printed 3.4%; that would cap unit labor costs and take some wage heat off Friday. A productivity miss next to claims at 230K would be the labour-and-efficiency soft mix into NFP.
events.ifHigher: Claims above 230K, or productivity under 2.0%: labour is loosening and efficiency is not offsetting. Gold bid, December odds fade.
events.ifLower: Claims below 190K with productivity at 3.0%+: still tight, and Q3 output per hour is rising. USD bids into NFP.

events.whatItIs: The federal government's annual budget, covering spending, tax, and the deficit path, typically presented in the afternoon Ottawa time.
events.whyItMatters: The Bank of Canada hiked to 2.50% last week, the first increase in a year, and Canada reports October jobs on Friday (seen +16.1K after September's -68.3K). A budget that adds to the deficit would sell the loonie and Canadas into that jobs print. A tighter consolidation path would bid CAD and take some fiscal heat off a BoC that just started hiking.
events.ifHigher: A larger deficit or a spending surprise: CAD offered, Canadas sold, a softer overlay on Friday's Canada jobs.
events.ifLower: A tighter consolidation path: CAD bid, a calmer CAD setup into Friday's labour print.

events.actual: 180,000 HYPE to core contributors (~1.8% of modeled 9.92M)
events.whatItIs: The monthly Hyperliquid core-contributor vesting date. Trackers model about 9.92 million HYPE (on the order of $770 million to $920 million at recent prices). Actual team claims have run far below that modeled ceiling; Hyperliquid Labs has pointed to a much smaller team distribution around this date.
events.whyItMatters: This is the largest named unlock on the November calendar and it lands the same morning as US payrolls. Bitcoin last printed about $76,800 on Friday after a Binance security incident, well off the $81,000s. Tokenomist still lists a ~$923 million HYPE line for November 6; prior months show the team claiming a fraction of the modeled 9.92 million, and October's batch was sold OTC. A clean hold in HYPE and BTC through the NFP window is constructive. A break that pulls ETH beta is a supply test on the week's biggest macro print.
events.ifHigher: HYPE absorbs the unlock and BTC holds $76,000 through NFP: demand matched whatever actually moved. Constructive for mid-cap alts.
events.ifLower: HYPE breaks and pulls ETH beta into a hot or very weak NFP: the overhang hits a data-heavy Friday. Altcoin risk-off, BTC relatively more resilient.

events.event: Nonfarm Payrolls, Unemployment Rate, and Average Hourly Earnings (October 2026)
events.actual: +165K payrolls; private +159K; unemployment 4.1%; average hourly earnings +0.4% MoM / +3.1% YoY
events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' Employment Situation: net payroll change, the unemployment rate, and average hourly earnings, released at 13:30 UTC, the first jobs print since the October FOMC hold.
events.whyItMatters: This is the week's fulcrum and the first labour-quantity read the Committee will take into December. September's +29K was a stall. Consensus is a bounce to +65K with unemployment unchanged at 4.2% and wages re-accelerating to 0.3% after a soft 0.1%. A 20K miss with wages still at 0.3% is the stagflation mix that bids the dollar and gold for different reasons. A 120K beat with wages at 0.4% would lock December as a near-certain hike. A 20K miss with wages at 0.1% would fade December and bid duration.
events.ifHigher: Payrolls above +120K or AHE at +0.4% MoM: labour is not cooling. USD bids, gold sold, December hike odds jump.
events.ifLower: Payrolls below +20K or unemployment at 4.4%+: the September stall is a trend. Gold and duration bid, December odds fade.

events.event: Canada Employment Change and Unemployment Rate (October 2026)
events.whatItIs: Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey for October: net employment change and the unemployment rate, released at 13:30 UTC, the same stamp as US NFP.
events.whyItMatters: The BoC hiked to 2.50% last week, the first increase in a year, with unemployment already at 6.5%. September's -68.3K was a sharp drop. Consensus is a bounce to +16K with unemployment unchanged. A second large miss would say the Bank hiked into a deteriorating labour market and would sell the loonie. A +50K bounce would confirm last month was noise and would bid CAD into a US NFP that prints alongside it.
events.ifHigher: Jobs above +50K with unemployment steady or falling: September was a one-month drop. CAD bids, BoC hike path firmer.
events.ifLower: Jobs below 0 or unemployment at 6.7%+: the BoC hiked into weakness. CAD sold, a softer overlay on oil-correlated assets.

events.event: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (November preliminary)
events.whatItIs: The University of Michigan's preliminary November survey of household sentiment, including 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations, released at 15:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: October's 48.0 final was the second-lowest on record after May's 44.8, with 1-year inflation expectations at 4.7% and 5-year at 3.5%. Consensus is a further dip to 47.2. A drop through 45 next to a hot NFP wage print would say households are not looking through $104 oil. A bounce above 50 would be the first sentiment relief of the autumn and a small equity bid into the weekend.
events.ifHigher: Above 50, or 1-year inflation expectations rolling off: morale is stabilising. Modest equity bid.
events.ifLower: Under 45, or 1-year inflation expectations at 5.0%+: households are cracking on prices. Equities sold, a hawkish overlay on whatever NFP just did.

events.event: Fed's Williams, Musalem, Logan, and Bowman Speak
events.whatItIs: A post-NFP cluster of Fed voices. New York's John Williams and St. Louis's Alberto Musalem are on the Friday docket, Dallas's Lorie Logan and Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman also speak. Williams is a permanent voter; Logan voted this cycle.
events.whyItMatters: Logan on Friday already called for two more hikes after the hold. This is the first chance the rest of the Committee gets to react to October payrolls in public. A Williams line that December is live after a 0.4% wage print would lock the meeting. A labour-aware, wait-for-CPI line after a 20K miss would let December odds sit into next week's CPI.
events.ifHigher: Williams or Logan treats December as live after a firm wage print: USD bids, gold sold, December odds jump.
events.ifLower: Patient, CPI-wait, or labour-cooling language after a weak payrolls print: USD sold, a quieter setup for next week's CPI.

2026-11-09.summary: October CPI, UK GDP, and PPI test a 165K payrolls, December-hike tape.

events.actual: CPI +0.7% YoY / 0.0% MoM; PPI +5.7% YoY / +0.7% MoM
events.whatItIs: The National Bureau of Statistics monthly consumer and producer price indexes, released at 01:30 UTC, covering food, energy, and factory-gate prices.
events.whyItMatters: China CPI has been stuck under 1% even as PPI jumped to +5.0% in September on energy and metals. Consensus is a small CPI fade to +0.8% and a further PPI rise to +5.3% as oil and industrial prices stay firm. A CPI miss next to hotter PPI is the stagflation mix for CNH, copper, and iron ore into Tuesday's US CPI. A CPI hold at 0.9% with PPI rolling off would say the factory-gate impulse is not reaching households.
events.ifHigher: CPI at 1.0%+ or PPI at 5.6%+: energy is landing in China prices. CNH offered, a firmer commodity overlay on Tuesday's US CPI.
events.ifLower: CPI at 0.6% or below, or PPI rolling toward 4.5%: demand is still soft. Copper and iron ore sold, a quieter Asia setup into US CPI.

events.whatItIs: Destatis's monthly goods trade surplus: exports minus imports, seasonally adjusted, released at 07:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Germany's surplus has held near EUR 19-22B even as the Iran war raised energy import costs. Consensus is a small fade to EUR 19.2B. A drop through EUR 16B would say energy imports are eating the surplus and would sell the euro into Tuesday's US CPI. A hold above EUR 21B would keep German exporters as a support for the euro-area Q3 GDP revision on Friday.
events.ifHigher: Surplus above EUR 21B: exporters are holding. Modest EUR bid into US CPI.
events.ifLower: Surplus at EUR 16B or below: energy imports are biting. EUR sold, a softer overlay on Friday's eurozone GDP.

events.event: Fed's Bowman, Goolsbee, and Barkin Speak
events.whatItIs: A Monday cluster of FOMC voices. Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman discusses community banking in Boston at 13:40 UTC. Chicago's Austan Goolsbee is in a moderated Q&A at 15:00 UTC. Richmond's Thomas Barkin speaks to the Greater Greer Chamber at 17:15 UTC, with audience questions expected.
events.whyItMatters: October payrolls printed +165K with wages +0.4%, and December hike odds sit near 78%. Bowman, Goolsbee, and Barkin are the first named Fed voices after that beat, one day before CPI. A hike-live line from Goolsbee or Barkin would lock Tuesday's CPI as a confirmation print. A labour-aware, wait-for-CPI line would let December odds sit overnight.
events.ifHigher: Treats a December hike as live after 165K payrolls: USD bids, gold sold, a hawkish setup for Tuesday CPI.
events.ifLower: Patient, CPI-wait, or labour-cooling language: USD sold, a quieter overnight into the inflation print.

events.whatItIs: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey's first public remarks after Thursday's 25bp hike to 4.00%.
events.whyItMatters: The MPC hiked 8-1, with Catherine Mann dissenting for 50bp, and the Monetary Policy Report now sees inflation near 5% by mid-2027. Bailey said the move should not be read as the first in an inevitable sequence, but that more hikes are likely if the Iran war persists. Sterling last sat near 1.335 after Friday's dollar bid. A 'further increase is live' line would bid GBP into Thursday's Q3 GDP. A one-and-done, oil-has-fallen line would sell the pound after an already-hawkish vote.
events.ifHigher: Flags another hike as live or defends the 5% inflation track: GBP bids, gilts sold, a hawkish overlay on Thursday's GDP.
events.ifLower: Treats Thursday as insurance, or leans on the oil drop from $104 toward $90: GBP sold, a quieter sterling setup into GDP.

events.event: Constellation Energy, KKR, Occidental, and Take-Two earnings
events.forecast: CEG EPS about $3.90 BMO; KKR about $1.50 BMO; OXY about $1.43 after close; TTWO about $0.96 after close
events.whatItIs: Monday's large-cap cluster. Constellation Energy and KKR report before the open. Occidental Petroleum and Take-Two Interactive report after the close, with Trade Desk also after hours.
events.whyItMatters: This is a quiet-macro Monday into Tuesday CPI, so single-name prints will set overnight risk. CEG is the nuclear-and-AI-power tell after last week's capex fade. OXY is the $90-oil producer print after WTI dropped from $104. Take-Two is the GTA-cycle consumer-discretionary tell. A clean CEG beat with OXY holding FCF at $90 crude would bid utilities and energy into CPI. An OXY cut next to a TTWO miss would sell cyclicals overnight.
events.ifHigher: CEG holds the power guide and OXY holds FCF at $90 oil: utilities and energy bid overnight into CPI.
events.ifLower: An OXY guide-down or a TTWO bookings miss: cyclicals sold overnight, a growth overlay on Tuesday's inflation print.

events.event: BoJ Summary of Opinions and Current Account (September 2026)
events.forecast: Current account about JPY 2.81T to JPY 3.35T; opinions from the late-October meeting
events.whatItIs: The Bank of Japan's anonymised Summary of Opinions from the October 29-30 meeting, released with the September current-account print at 23:50 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The BoJ held at 1.25% on an 8-1 vote, with Takata dissenting for 1.50%, and USD/JPY last sat near 158. The summary is the first look at whether the majority is still waiting on wages or whether more members now see a hike as live. Hawkish opinions next to a still-large current-account surplus would bid the yen into Tuesday's US CPI. A patient majority would leave 158 as the default into Japan Q3 GDP next week.
events.ifHigher: Several opinions flag a hike as live, or the surplus holds above JPY 3.2T: JPY bids, a modest yen overlay on US CPI.
events.ifLower: Patient majority, or the surplus drops hard: JPY offered, 158 holds into next week's Japan GDP.

events.whatItIs: Governor Christopher Waller delivers a keynote at 09:00 UTC, the first Board voter on the tape the morning of CPI.
events.whyItMatters: Waller is a 2026 voter and has been the AI-and-inflation voice on the Board. Payrolls at +165K and wages at +0.4% already lifted December odds to about 78%. A hike-live line four hours before CPI would lock the print as confirmation. A wait-for-the-data line would leave the 13:30 UTC release as the event.
events.ifHigher: Treats December as live after the payrolls beat: USD bids into CPI.
events.ifLower: Patient, data-dependent language: USD quieter, CPI remains the day's fulcrum.

events.whatItIs: The National Federation of Independent Business monthly survey of small-firm optimism, compensation plans, and price plans, released at 11:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: NFIB has been stuck in the high-97s as oil and borrowing costs bite. Consensus is a small bounce to about 98.2. The price-plans and compensation-plans lines are the CPI overlay two hours before the BLS print. A jump in price plans would be a hawkish pre-headline. A drop through 96 with price plans rolling off would be a small dovish leak into 13:30 UTC.
events.ifHigher: Index above 99 or price plans firming: small firms are still raising prices. Modest USD bid into CPI.
events.ifLower: Index at 96 or below with price plans rolling off: the oil-and-rate squeeze is landing. Small gold bid into the print.

events.previous: +0.6% MoM / +3.7% YoY headline; +0.3% MoM / +2.6% YoY core (September 2026)
events.forecast: +0.3% MoM headline; +0.2% MoM core (FactSet about +0.24% / +0.2%). YoY may not be published because of the 2025 shutdown data gap.
events.actual: +0.4% MoM headline; +0.3% MoM core. No YoY rate published (shutdown data gap).
events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index for October: the all-items monthly change and core CPI excluding food and energy, released at 13:30 UTC. This is the last CPI before the December 8-9 FOMC.
events.whyItMatters: September printed +0.6% headline and +0.3% core, with gasoline +9.1% doing most of the headline work. Consensus is a cooler +0.3% / +0.2% as gasoline flattens and used cars ease. October payrolls already printed +165K with wages +0.4%, so a core print at 0.3% or hotter would lock December as a near-certain hike. A 0.1% core miss is the only mix that pulls those 78% odds down. BLS may skip annual rates because October 2025 collection was disrupted by the federal shutdown, which makes the month-on-month core line the one the tape will trade.
events.ifHigher: Headline at +0.4%+ or core at +0.3%+: inflation is not cooling. USD bids, gold sold, December hike odds jump toward fully priced.
events.ifLower: Headline at +0.1% or core at +0.1%: the September spike was energy. Gold and duration bid, December odds fade.

events.event: Bank of Canada Summary of Deliberations (October 28 decision)
events.whatItIs: The Bank of Canada's anonymised account of the October 28 Governing Council meeting, released at 18:30 UTC, two weeks after the decision.
events.whyItMatters: The BoC hiked to 2.50% on October 28, the first increase in a year. Friday's Canada jobs print then missed: -4.7K and unemployment 6.7% against +16K / 6.5% seen. A summary that treats the hike as the start of a campaign would bid the loonie even after the jobs miss. A summary that already sounds one-and-done would sell CAD into Wednesday's holiday-thinned tape.
events.ifHigher: Several members flag another hike as live: CAD bids, a firmer overlay on US CPI follow-through.
events.ifLower: Patient majority, or labour-cooling language that fits Friday's miss: CAD sold.

events.event: McDonald's, Charles Schwab, and CoreWeave earnings
events.whatItIs: Tuesday's large-cap and AI-infrastructure cluster. McDonald's is the global-traffic consumer tell. Schwab is the rates-and-NII tell after the 10-year bid to 4.86%. CoreWeave is the neocloud print the Street has been trading as the second-order AI-spend test after last week's Intel and Amazon fade.
events.whyItMatters: These land the evening of CPI, so the overnight tape will mix inflation with growth. A McDonald's traffic beat with Schwab holding net interest income would bid consumer and financials. A CoreWeave miss, or a comment that hyperscaler demand is slipping, would extend last week's AI-fade into Wednesday's holiday session and Thursday's Cisco-Applied pair.
events.ifHigher: McDonald's holds traffic and CoreWeave holds the AI-cloud guide: consumer and semis bid overnight.
events.ifLower: A CoreWeave guide-down or a McDonald's traffic miss: growth sold overnight into a bond-market holiday.

events.event: API Weekly Crude Oil Stock Change (week ending November 6)
events.previous: EIA official -0.865 million barrels (week ending October 30)
events.whatItIs: The American Petroleum Institute's unofficial weekly estimate of US commercial crude stocks, released at 21:30 UTC. Veterans Day delays the official EIA print to Thursday 17:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: WTI last printed about $90.50 with Brent near $98, a sharp drop from the $104 / $117 area of the prior Friday as the midterm result took some war premium out. Last week's official print was a 0.87 million-barrel draw to 409.8 million, still about 4% below the five-year average. API is the only inventory look before Thursday's delayed EIA. A large draw overnight would put $93-95 back in play into a CPI day. A build would lean on a market that has already given back $14.
events.ifHigher: A build of 3 million barrels or more: the surplus is growing. WTI sold overnight into Thursday's EIA.
events.ifLower: A draw of 3 million barrels or more: last week's draw is extending. WTI bids toward $93-95 into the delayed official print.

events.event: Veterans Day -- stock market open, bond market closed
events.whatItIs: A US federal holiday. NYSE and Nasdaq cash equities are open. The Treasury market, US banks, and Federal Reserve statistical releases scheduled for Wednesday print on Thursday instead. Canada observes Remembrance Day with a similar stocks-open, bonds-closed split.
events.whyItMatters: Tuesday's CPI will have a thinner rates market to digest it. EIA inventories, normally Wednesday 15:30 UTC, move to Thursday 17:00 UTC. Fed statistical releases due Wednesday also shift. Equity index futures still trade, so a CPI surprise can gap stocks without the usual Treasury hedge. Thin holiday liquidity into Thursday's UK GDP, claims, existing home sales, and the Cisco-Applied pair is the setup.
events.ifHigher: N/A -- market holiday for Treasuries; equities remain open.
events.ifLower: N/A -- market holiday for Treasuries; equities remain open.

events.previous: Flash -0.2% MoM / +2.8% YoY; core flash +2.1% YoY (October 2026)
events.forecast: Confirm flash: -0.2% MoM / +2.8% YoY; HICP -0.1% MoM / +2.8% YoY
events.whatItIs: Destatis's final October consumer-price index, confirming or revising the October 30 flash, released at 07:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The flash already cooled from September's +3.3% to +2.8% as energy inflation slowed from +14.9% to +12.2%. A downward revision would reinforce the euro-area disinflation case into Friday's GDP second estimate. An upward revision toward 3.0% would say the flash understated the oil impulse and would bid the euro on a US holiday.
events.ifHigher: Final at 3.0%+ YoY: the flash understated prices. Modest EUR bid on a thin holiday tape.
events.ifLower: Final at 2.6% or below: German cooling is confirmed. EUR offered, a quieter setup for Friday's eurozone GDP.

events.whatItIs: OPEC's Monthly Oil Market Report: demand, supply, and inventory estimates, typically posted around 10:00 UTC, covering the first full month after the November 1 quota hold.
events.whyItMatters: OPEC+ held December quotas on November 1. WTI has since dropped from $104 toward $90 as the midterm result took some Hormuz premium out. The MOMR demand track and the call on OPEC crude are the first official supply-demand rewrite of that hold. A demand upgrade that keeps the 2027 deficit intact would bid oil into Thursday's delayed EIA. A demand cut that treats $90 as demand destruction would extend the selloff.
events.ifHigher: Demand upgraded or the call on OPEC raised: WTI bids toward $93-95 into Thursday EIA.
events.ifLower: Demand cut or inventories raised: WTI sold, a softer energy overlay on Friday PPI.

events.event: Pump.fun (PUMP) team and investor unlock (~$27M); Allora (ALLO) ~$26M
events.whatItIs: Wednesday's named vesting cluster. Pump.fun unlocks about 6.88 billion PUMP (around $27 million, about 1.3% of circulating supply) to team and existing investors at 12:44 UTC. Allora unlocks about $26 million the same morning, a much larger share of its float.
events.whyItMatters: These are the largest named unlocks of the CPI week, landing on a US bond-market holiday with bitcoin closing Friday (6 Nov) near $75,800. PUMP's dollar size is moderate; ALLO's percentage of float is the sharper supply test. A clean hold in BTC through a holiday session is constructive. A break that pulls ETH beta is a supply overlay on a tape that is still digesting Tuesday's CPI.
events.ifHigher: PUMP and ALLO absorb the unlocks and BTC holds $75,000 through the holiday session: demand matched the supply. Constructive for mid-cap alts.
events.ifLower: ALLO or PUMP breaks and pulls ETH beta on a bond-market holiday: the overhang hits thin liquidity. Altcoin risk-off, BTC relatively more resilient.

events.event: UK GDP first quarterly estimate (Q3 2026), monthly GDP, and industrial production
events.previous: Q2 GDP +0.5% QoQ (revised); GDP 3-month to August +0.7%; industrial production +1.6% YoY (August)
events.forecast: Q3 GDP about +0.5% QoQ (UniCredit/Bloomberg); 3-month to September +0.4%; YoY about +1.7%
events.actual: Q3 GDP +0.7% QoQ (Q2 +0.5%); +1.9% YoY; September GDP +0.2% MoM
events.whatItIs: The ONS first quarterly estimate of UK real GDP for July-September, published with monthly GDP for September, industrial production, construction, and the trade balance, at 07:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The BoE hiked to 4.00% on Thursday on an 8-1 vote and lifted the inflation track toward 5% in mid-2027. Monthly GDP through August already implied a strong Q3 if September was merely flat: some houses have 0.7% QoQ in play, well above the Bank's 0.4% staff view. A 0.6%+ print would confirm the economy can take the hike and would bid sterling. A 0.2% miss would say the Bank hiked into a stall and would sell GBP into US claims 90 minutes later.
events.ifHigher: Q3 at +0.6%+ or the 3-month at +0.6%+: activity can take the hike. GBP bids, December BoE odds firm.
events.ifLower: Q3 at +0.2% or below, or monthly September a sharp drop: the Bank hiked into a stall. GBP sold, a softer overlay on US claims.

events.whatItIs: The Department of Labor's weekly first-time unemployment filings, released at 13:30 UTC, two days after the 165,000 October payrolls beat.
events.whyItMatters: Claims printed 189K last week, still historically low, even as September payrolls had looked soft. October then bounced to +165K. A jump toward 230K the morning after CPI would be the first weekly sign that the payrolls beat is not a hiring trend. A hold under 190K would confirm the labour market is still tight into December.
events.ifHigher: Claims above 230K: labour is loosening on the flow. Gold bid, a small fade in December odds after CPI.
events.ifLower: Claims below 190K: still tight after 165K payrolls. USD bids, December odds hold.

events.event: Fed's Hammack, Goolsbee, Daly, and Williams Speak
events.whatItIs: A post-CPI cluster. Cleveland's Beth Hammack is in a moderated conversation at 14:00 UTC. Chicago's Austan Goolsbee is on Yahoo Finance at 16:30 UTC. San Francisco's Mary Daly delivers keynote remarks at Stanford at 18:10 UTC. New York's John Williams is on a panel at 23:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: This is the first chance the Committee gets to react to Tuesday's CPI in public, on a day the Treasury market is back from Veterans Day. Williams is a permanent voter. Daly has already flagged more hikes. A Williams line that December is live after a 0.3% core print would lock the meeting. A wait-for-PCE line after a 0.1% miss would let December odds sit into Friday PPI.
events.ifHigher: Williams or Daly treats December as live after a firm CPI: USD bids, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Patient, PCE-wait, or labour-cooling language after a soft CPI: USD sold, a quieter setup for Friday PPI.

events.whatItIs: The National Association of Realtors monthly count of completed sales of previously owned homes, including single-family, condos, and co-ops, released at 15:00 UTC with median price and months of supply.
events.whyItMatters: Existing sales have been stuck near 4.0 million as mortgage rates sit near 7.3% on the MBA survey and the 10-year has bid to 4.86% after payrolls. Consensus is a small fade to 3.94 million. A drop through 3.7 million would say high yields are closing the housing channel and would be a dovish overlay on a CPI week. A bounce above 4.1 million would say the labour beat is still supporting demand.
events.ifHigher: Sales above 4.1 million with prices holding: housing is taking 7% mortgages. Modest USD and cyclical bid.
events.ifLower: Sales at 3.7 million or below, or a sharp price drop: rates are shutting the bid. Duration bid, a softer overlay on December.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending November 6) -- Veterans Day delay
events.previous: -0.865 million barrels; commercial stocks 409.8 million (week ending October 30)
events.whatItIs: The Energy Information Administration's Weekly Petroleum Status Report, delayed from Wednesday to Thursday 17:00 UTC because Veterans Day closed the federal government on Wednesday. Covers commercial crude excluding the SPR, plus gasoline, distillates, and Cushing.
events.whyItMatters: WTI last printed about $90.50, down from $104 the prior Friday, after the midterm result took some war premium out. Last week's official print was a 0.87 million-barrel draw, the latest in a five-week stretch that took stocks to 409.8 million, about 4% below the five-year average. API on Tuesday is the only preview. A sixth draw would put $93-95 back in play into Friday PPI. A build would confirm that the $14 drop is barrels as well as geopolitics.
events.ifHigher: A build of 3 million barrels or more: the surplus is growing. WTI sold, a small relief bid for duration into PPI.
events.ifLower: A draw of 3 million barrels or more: the draw streak is extending. WTI bids toward $93-95, a firmer energy overlay on Friday PPI.

events.event: Cisco and Applied Materials Q1/Q4 earnings (after close)
events.forecast: Cisco EPS about $1.32-$1.34 on about $18.1B revenue, call 21:30 UTC; Applied EPS about $4.02-$4.06 on about $10.25B revenue, call 21:30 UTC
events.whatItIs: Thursday's after-close pair. Cisco reports fiscal Q1 2027 networking, security, and AI-infrastructure results. Applied Materials reports fiscal Q4 2026 wafer-fab equipment results and the 2027 WFE guide. Both calls start at 21:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: These are the two largest remaining S&P names of the week, and they land after CPI, UK GDP, and EIA. Cisco guided Q1 to $18.0-18.2B revenue and $1.32-1.34 non-GAAP EPS in August; the Street is at about $1.32 and $18.11B. Applied guided Q4 to $10.25B plus or minus $500M and $4.02 plus or minus $0.20 after a record Q3. A Cisco beat with Applied holding the WFE guide would bid networking and semis into Friday PPI. A Cisco miss next to an Applied China-or-export-control warning would extend last week's AI-fade into Nvidia next week.
events.ifHigher: Cisco holds the $18B guide and Applied holds WFE: networking and equipment bid overnight into PPI.
events.ifLower: A Cisco miss or an Applied China/export warning: semis sold overnight, a growth overlay on Friday PPI and next week's Nvidia print.

events.forecast: Confirm flash +0.4% QoQ / +1.3% YoY (flash beat +0.2% consensus)
events.whatItIs: Eurostat's t+45 flash estimate of euro-area Q3 GDP, adding employment and a first expenditure breakdown, released at 10:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: The October 30 preliminary flash beat at +0.4% against +0.2% seen, but Ireland's +5.5% flattered the headline and France contracted 0.1%. This revision is the one that either confirms the beat or takes Ireland out. A downward revision through +0.2% would sell the euro into US PPI. A hold at +0.4% with employment still firm would keep December as a live ECB meeting after 3.8% HICP.
events.ifHigher: Revised to +0.5%+ or employment firm: the beat is real. Modest EUR bid into US PPI.
events.ifLower: Revised to +0.2% or below: Ireland was the whole beat. EUR sold, December ECB hold firmer.

events.previous: +1.3% MoM headline; +0.7% MoM core; about +6.3% YoY (September 2026)
events.forecast: +0.4% MoM headline; +0.3% MoM core (Briefing.com); YoY about +6.1%
events.whatItIs: The Bureau of Labor Statistics Producer Price Index for final demand, including core PPI excluding food and energy, released at 13:30 UTC, three days after CPI.
events.whyItMatters: September PPI exploded +1.3% headline and +0.7% core, the pipeline print that fed Tuesday's CPI debate. Consensus is a cooler +0.4% / +0.3% as energy wholesale prices ease with WTI down from $104 toward $90. A second 0.7% core print would say the pipeline is still hot even if Tuesday's CPI cooled, and would lock December. A 0.1% miss would confirm that the September spike was energy and would fade hike odds into the weekend.
events.ifHigher: Headline at +0.6%+ or core at +0.5%+: the pipeline is still hot. USD bids, gold sold, December odds jump.
events.ifLower: Headline at +0.2% or core at +0.1%: September was energy. Gold and duration bid, December odds fade.

events.event: Fed's Daly, Williams, and Jefferson Speak
events.whatItIs: A post-PPI cluster. San Francisco's Mary Daly is in a moderated discussion at 17:00 UTC. New York's John Williams is also on the Friday docket. Vice Chair Philip Jefferson speaks at UC San Diego in the evening.
events.whyItMatters: This is the last Fed-voice window of the week after CPI, claims, and PPI. Williams is a permanent voter. Daly has already said more hikes are coming. A Williams line that December is live after a 0.4% PPI would lock the meeting into next week's minutes. A wait-for-PCE line after a soft PPI would let December odds sit through the weekend.
events.ifHigher: Williams or Daly treats December as live after firm PPI: USD bids, gold sold.
events.ifLower: Patient, PCE-wait language after a soft PPI: USD sold, a quieter weekend into next week's retail sales and Nvidia.

2026-11-16.summary: Fed minutes, Warsh, US retail sales, UK CPI, and Nvidia earnings headline the week.

events.previous: Q2 2026 real GDP +0.4% QoQ (seasonally adjusted, this release)
events.forecast: About +0.1% QoQ / +0.3% annualized (Reuters poll); Q2 was +0.4% / +1.4%
events.whatItIs: The Cabinet Office first preliminary estimate of real GDP for July-September 2026, seasonally adjusted, released at 23:50 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: A Reuters poll looked for about +0.1% quarter on quarter and +0.3% annualized. This release printed -0.0% quarter on quarter and -0.1% annualized, with real GDP up 1.1% from a year earlier. The same table shows April-June real GDP at +0.4% quarter on quarter. The miss is the growth read for the yen at the start of the week.
events.ifHigher: At or above about +0.1% QoQ or +0.3% annualized: growth held against the poll. JPY bids.
events.ifLower: Below the poll, including a flat or negative quarter: growth stalled. JPY offered.

events.event: China Industrial Production and Retail Sales (October 2026)
events.whatItIs: The National Bureau of Statistics monthly activity data: factory output and consumer spending, released at 02:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Asia opens the week with the dollar at 18-month highs and commodities under pressure. Firm Chinese activity would support copper, iron ore, and oil demand expectations. A miss would add to the growth worry hitting risk assets.
events.ifHigher: Output and retail sales beat: CNH and AUD firm, copper and oil supported, a modest risk-on start to the week.
events.ifLower: Either print misses: China-cyclicals sold, oil demand fears build, USD stays bid as the safe harbor.

events.whatItIs: Eurostat's monthly measure of output across eurozone factories, mines, and utilities.
events.whyItMatters: EUR/USD has retreated to roughly 1.10, April 2025 levels, on dollar strength and a hawkish Fed repricing. A rebound from August's decline would take some pressure off the euro. Another miss would reinforce the weak-growth read ahead of Tuesday's ZEW survey.
events.ifHigher: A beat above +0.3%: modest EUR support, European cyclicals firmer.
events.ifLower: A second decline: EUR offered toward fresh lows, softer tone for DAX and European industrials.

events.whatItIs: Scheduled vesting releases of Arbitrum (ARB) and, per unlock trackers, Cronos (CRO) tokens, roughly $15M and $60M at current prices.
events.whyItMatters: Bitcoin broke below $70,000 last week on liquidations and sentiment is fragile. Unlocks of this size are unlikely to move the majors alone, but new supply into thin liquidity can pressure the affected tokens.
events.ifHigher: Recipients hold or stake rather than sell: the affected tokens absorb the supply with limited drawdown.
events.ifLower: Recipients sell into weak liquidity: ARB and CRO underperform, with a small risk-off tilt across altcoins.
events.learnMore:
A token unlock is the release of previously locked tokens to team members, investors, or ecosystem funds under a vesting schedule. It adds to circulating supply, which can pressure price if recipients sell.

Impact depends on size relative to circulating supply and on market depth. A cliff unlock of several percent of supply matters far more than a small linear monthly release. Traders watch trackers such as DefiLlama and Token Unlocks, and check amounts there before acting, since schedules and dollar values shift with price.

events.whatItIs: Statistics Canada's monthly consumer price index, with the CPI-trim and CPI-median core measures the Bank of Canada watches.
events.whyItMatters: With global yields surging and the dollar strong, Canadian inflation sets the odds of further Bank of Canada tightening and drives USD/CAD. CPI-trim was 1.8% YoY last month, so core is the number to watch.
events.ifHigher: Above +0.3% MoM or firmer core: CAD bids, Canadian yields rise, BoC tightening odds increase.
events.ifLower: Below +0.3% MoM: CAD sold, USD/CAD higher, BoC stays patient.
events.learnMore:
Canada's CPI measures a basket of consumer goods and services. The Bank of Canada looks past the headline to CPI-trim and CPI-median, which strip out the most extreme price moves, along with the common measure.

CAD trades on the gap between Canadian and US rates and on oil prices. A hot print raises the odds of a BoC hike and supports the loonie. A soft print widens the rate gap with a hawkish Fed and pushes USD/CAD higher.

events.whatItIs: The New York Fed's monthly survey of manufacturers in New York State; above zero signals expansion.
events.whyItMatters: It is the first hard regional read of November. October's 25.5 was strong, and consensus expects a fade to 19.4. A reading well below that would challenge the resilient-growth case behind the hawkish Fed repricing.
events.ifHigher: Above 19.4: growth resilience confirmed, yields and USD supported, December hike odds firm.
events.ifLower: Below 15: factory momentum fading, yields ease slightly, gold and stocks get a small bid.

events.whatItIs: New York Fed President John Williams, a permanent FOMC voter, delivers opening remarks at the New York Fed's FX Market Structure Conference.
events.whyItMatters: Williams speaks twice more this week (Tuesday and Wednesday) as markets debate a December hike. His tone sets the baseline before Warsh at 17:00 UTC and Wednesday's minutes.
events.ifHigher: Hawkish tilt or December hike treated as live: USD and yields up, gold and equities sold.
events.ifLower: Patient, data-dependent language: USD eases, the minutes become the week's main event.

events.whatItIs: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh gives scheduled remarks, the first Chair commentary of the week.
events.whyItMatters: The 10-year yield is near 5.15%, the dollar index is above 103, and some investors price a half-point December hike. Any signal from the Chair on the pace of tightening could reprice the whole curve before Wednesday's minutes.
events.ifHigher: Hawkish remarks or backing for a faster pace: USD and yields jump, gold and bitcoin extend losses, equities fall.
events.ifLower: Pushback on a half-point move: yields and USD retreat, gold and bitcoin bounce, equities rally.
events.learnMore:
The Fed Chair sets the tone for the Committee and for market pricing. Chair remarks outside a post-meeting press conference are rare, so markets read them closely for hints about the next decision.

With the funds rate at 3.75-4.00% after a 10-2 hold in October, the question is how fast and how far the Committee goes. A Chair who embraces a half-point December hike would force a sharp repricing of rates, the dollar, and gold. A Chair who stresses patience would pull yields lower.

events.event: RBA Minutes and Governor Bullock Speaks
events.whatItIs: The Reserve Bank of Australia releases minutes of its latest policy meeting, alongside remarks from Governor Michele Bullock.
events.whyItMatters: The RBA has been hiking, taking its cash rate to 4.85% earlier this month on a split vote. The minutes show how divided the board was and whether more hikes are on the table.
events.ifHigher: Minutes show a hawkish tilt: AUD bids and Australian yields rise.
events.ifLower: Minutes signal a pause: AUD sold, Australian yields dip.

events.whatItIs: The ONS monthly labour report: unemployment rate, average earnings growth, and the claimant count.
events.whyItMatters: The Bank of England hiked to 4.00% in early November on an 8-1 vote. Wage growth and unemployment feed the case for further hikes and set the stage for Wednesday's CPI.
events.ifHigher: Firmer wages or lower unemployment: GBP bids, gilt yields rise, more BoE hikes priced.
events.ifLower: Weaker wages or rising unemployment: GBP sold, gilts rally, BoE hike odds trimmed.
events.learnMore:
The UK labour report combines the ILO unemployment rate, three-month average earnings, and the claimant count. The Bank of England focuses on private-sector regular pay growth, which feeds services inflation.

After a hawkish hike, strong pay data supports the view that the MPC must keep tightening. A softer report supports the one-and-done reading and would pressure sterling.

events.event: German and Eurozone ZEW Economic Sentiment (November 2026)
events.whatItIs: A monthly survey of financial analysts on the six-month economic outlook for Germany and the eurozone.
events.whyItMatters: It is the first forward-looking European sentiment read since the dollar surge and the jump in global yields. A drop would deepen the weak-growth narrative for the euro.
events.ifHigher: Improving sentiment: EUR firms, DAX supported.
events.ifLower: Falling expectations: EUR pressured toward 1.10, European equities soften.

events.event: Home Depot and Disney earnings (before open)
events.whatItIs: Home Depot and Walt Disney report quarterly results before the US open.
events.whyItMatters: Home Depot is a read on housing-linked spending with the 10-year near 5.15%. Disney reads the consumer and streaming economics. Both land hours before retail sales.
events.ifHigher: Beats and steady guidance: consumer-discretionary stocks support the S&P recovery.
events.ifLower: Weak guidance, especially on housing or travel: consumer names sold and growth worries rise.

events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's monthly measure of sales at retailers, restaurants, and online stores, the broadest gauge of consumer spending.
events.whyItMatters: September's +0.8% was strong, and consumers drive about two-thirds of the economy. With the Fed weighing a December hike, another firm print would harden hike pricing, while a sharp slowdown would challenge it.
events.ifHigher: Another strong print: USD and yields rise, December hike odds climb, gold and growth equities pressured.
events.ifLower: A clear slowdown: yields and USD ease, gold and bitcoin bounce, hike pricing cools.
events.learnMore:
Retail sales measures the dollar value of purchases at stores, restaurants, and online. The control group, which excludes autos, gasoline, building materials, and food services, feeds directly into GDP estimates.

The headline is nominal, so higher prices can inflate it even if volumes are flat. Traders compare it with inflation data to judge real consumption.

After a strong September, the market is sensitive to a second hot month, since it would support the argument for a December hike. A weak print would raise stagflation worries given elevated inflation.

events.event: US Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (October 2026)
events.whatItIs: The Federal Reserve's monthly index of output from factories, mines, and utilities, with the share of capacity in use.
events.whyItMatters: September's +0.7% was a big jump, so a pullback is possible. It follows retail sales by 45 minutes and adds to the growth picture driving rate expectations.
events.ifHigher: Another solid gain: supports growth resilience, firmer USD and yields.
events.ifLower: A payback decline: modest yield dip, supports the cooling-growth view.

events.whatItIs: Nvidia reports quarterly results, the key read on AI chip demand and data-centre spending.
events.whyItMatters: Nvidia and chip stocks have driven recent volatility in the Nasdaq, which has been sliding into the print. The result and guidance steer AI-related sentiment across the S&P 500.
events.ifHigher: Beat with strong guidance: chips and the Nasdaq rally, risk appetite improves, bitcoin follows tech higher.
events.ifLower: Miss or cautious guidance: chips sold sharply, Nasdaq drops, broader risk-off tone.
events.learnMore:
Nvidia supplies most of the high-end chips used to train and run AI models, so its quarterly numbers act as a barometer for AI spending by cloud providers and enterprises.

Markets focus on data-centre revenue, gross margin, and next-quarter guidance more than the headline beat. Expectations are high, so a modest beat can still sell off if guidance only meets consensus.

Because Nvidia is one of the largest index weights, its move spills into the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500, and often into risk assets such as bitcoin.

events.whatItIs: The ONS monthly consumer price index, the Bank of England's key inflation gauge.
events.whyItMatters: The MPC hiked to 4.00% on an 8-1 vote and flagged inflation near 5% by mid-2027. October CPI shows whether energy costs are feeding through and whether more hikes are warranted.
events.ifHigher: Above expectations: GBP jumps, gilt yields rise, more BoE tightening priced for December.
events.ifLower: Below expectations: GBP sold, gilts rally, the hike looks like insurance rather than a start.
events.learnMore:
UK CPI measures price changes across a basket of household goods and services. The Bank of England watches services CPI and core CPI closely, since they reflect domestic wage pressure rather than imported energy costs.

October includes the effect of the energy price cap and recent oil moves. Brent near $96 is below the late-October peak, but still high.

A hot number validates the MPC's hawkish vote and keeps December live. A soft number would let markets treat November's hike as a one-off.

events.whatItIs: Eurostat's final estimate of eurozone consumer inflation for October, confirming the flash reading.
events.whyItMatters: Revisions to the flash number are usually small, but a surprise would affect ECB expectations while the euro sits near multi-month lows.
events.ifHigher: An upward revision: EUR supported, ECB hawks gain ground.
events.ifLower: A downward revision: EUR eases, less pressure on the ECB.

events.event: Target, Lowe's, and TJX earnings (before open)
events.whatItIs: Three of the largest US retailers report quarterly results before the open.
events.whyItMatters: They arrive one day after retail sales and give company-level evidence on consumer health, discretionary spending, and housing-linked demand before the holiday season.
events.ifHigher: Solid results and confident holiday guidance: retailers and consumer-discretionary stocks rally.
events.ifLower: Cautious guidance: retail stocks fall, supporting the consumer-slowdown view.

events.event: US Housing Starts and Building Permits (October 2026)
events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's monthly count of new residential construction starts and permits.
events.whyItMatters: Housing is the most rate-sensitive part of the economy, and the 10-year yield has jumped to around 5.15%. Permits are a forward indicator of construction activity.
events.ifHigher: Stronger starts and permits: growth resilience, supports yields and USD.
events.ifLower: Weak construction: rate-sensitivity shows, a slight dovish read for yields.

events.whatItIs: The EIA's weekly estimate of change in US commercial crude oil stockpiles, released Wednesday at 15:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Brent is near $96 with attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure escalating. Inventory draws would reinforce tight supply. Builds could temper the rally.
events.ifHigher: A larger-than-expected build: WTI and Brent dip, energy equities soften.
events.ifLower: A larger-than-expected draw: crude extends gains, energy stocks firm, inflation concerns rise.

events.whatItIs: The detailed record of the Fed's October policy meeting, released three weeks after the decision.
events.whyItMatters: With some investors pricing a half-point December hike and the 10-year near 5.15%, the minutes show how many officials saw a hike as appropriate and how close the dissent was. It is the week's main macro event.
events.ifHigher: Many officials open to hikes or a faster pace: USD and yields jump, gold and bitcoin fall, equities slide.
events.ifLower: Minutes show patience and wide uncertainty: yields and USD ease, gold and bitcoin bounce, equities rally.
events.learnMore:
FOMC minutes summarize the Committee's discussion of the economy, risks, and policy options. They are released three weeks after each meeting and often move markets because they show the balance of opinion behind a decision.

Traders scan for phrases such as 'many participants' or 'several participants' on hikes, and for discussion of balance-sheet policy. The 10-2 vote in October shows two officials dissented, and the minutes explain why.
