Because the meeting is three weeks old, new data such as October CPI can overshadow it. After a hot inflation print, a hawkish tone in the minutes is likely to be read as confirmation.

events.whatItIs: Palo Alto Networks, a major cybersecurity vendor, reports fiscal results after the close.
events.whyItMatters: It is a read on enterprise software spending and sets the tone for software stocks after Nvidia's AI-driven moves.
events.ifHigher: Strong billings and guidance: software and cybersecurity stocks rally.
events.ifLower: Soft guidance: software names sold, a drag on the Nasdaq.

events.whatItIs: The Australian Bureau of Statistics monthly jobs data: employment change and the unemployment rate.
events.whyItMatters: September's -39.3K was a sharp drop, shortly after the RBA hiked to 4.85%. A rebound would support more tightening. Another weak print would challenge it.
events.ifHigher: A solid jobs rebound: AUD bids, RBA tightening odds rise.
events.ifLower: Another decline or higher unemployment: AUD sold, RBA hike odds fall.

events.whatItIs: The largest US retailer reports quarterly results before the open.
events.whyItMatters: Walmart serves consumers across income levels, making it the cleanest read on household spending as high prices and rising yields weigh on budgets. Its holiday guidance reaches the whole retail sector.
events.ifHigher: Strong comps and a raised outlook: retail and staples rally, the resilient-consumer case strengthens.
events.ifLower: Cautious outlook: consumer stocks fall and stagflation worries build.

events.event: US Initial Jobless Claims (week ending November 14)
events.whatItIs: The weekly count of new state unemployment insurance filings, a real-time read on layoffs.
events.whyItMatters: October payrolls were strong at +165K, so claims show whether the labour market is holding up. Low claims support the hike case. A jump would soften it.
events.ifHigher: Rising claims: labour cooling, yields and USD ease, gold bounces.
events.ifLower: Claims stay low: labour strength confirmed, hike odds firm, USD supported.

events.whatItIs: The Philadelphia Fed's monthly survey of manufacturers in its district; above zero signals expansion.
events.whyItMatters: Together with Empire State, it gives the second regional read on November factory activity ahead of the flash PMIs next week.
events.ifHigher: A strong reading: supports growth resilience, USD and yields firmer.
events.ifLower: A drop below zero: factory momentum fading, slight yield dip.

events.whatItIs: Intuit, maker of TurboTax, QuickBooks, and Credit Karma, reports fiscal results after the close.
events.whyItMatters: It is a read on small-business and consumer finance health, and on whether AI is helping or threatening software incumbents.
events.ifHigher: Strong guidance: software stocks supported into Friday.
events.ifLower: Soft guidance: software and fintech names sold.

events.whatItIs: The People's Bank of China's monthly benchmark lending rates for 1-year and 5-year loans.
events.whyItMatters: The market expects no change. A surprise cut would signal easing to support growth, while a hold keeps the focus on the US.
events.ifHigher: Unchanged or hawkish: CNH steady, limited market impact.
events.ifLower: A surprise cut: CNH weaker, China-cyclicals and copper supported.

events.whatItIs: The ONS monthly measure of retail volumes in Great Britain.
events.whyItMatters: It closes a week that includes the UK labour report and CPI, completing the picture of how the consumer is coping after the BoE hike.
events.ifHigher: A firm rise: GBP supported, BoE hawks emboldened.
events.ifLower: A fall: GBP softer, doubts about additional hikes grow.

events.event: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (Final November 2026)
events.whatItIs: The final reading of the University of Michigan consumer survey, with 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations.
events.whyItMatters: Fed officials watch inflation expectations closely. A revision up in the 1-year figure from 4.3% would add to hike arguments.
events.ifHigher: Higher expectations: USD and yields firm, gold pressured, hike odds supported.
events.ifLower: Lower expectations or weaker sentiment: yields ease, gold and equities bounce.

2026-11-23.summary: Core PCE and GDP on Wednesday, flash PMIs Monday, then Thanksgiving closes US markets.

events.event: Japan Labor Thanksgiving Day -- Tokyo markets closed
events.whatItIs: A Japanese national holiday on which the Tokyo Stock Exchange and Japanese cash markets are closed.
events.whyItMatters: Asia opens the week with Friday's global equity rout and a 19-month-high dollar still fresh. With Tokyo shut, liquidity in yen crosses and Asian risk assets is thinner than usual, so moves can be exaggerated.
events.ifHigher: Not a data release, so there is no beat or miss. Thin liquidity can still amplify yen moves if the dollar extends higher.
events.ifLower: Not a data release. Japanese cash markets resume Tuesday and catch up on whatever Europe and the US do on Monday.

events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary November surveys of purchasing managers in Germany (08:30 UTC) and the eurozone (09:00 UTC); a reading above 50 signals expansion.
events.whyItMatters: EUR/USD is under pressure from a strong dollar and a hawkish Fed repricing, and Friday's equity rout hit global growth sentiment. The flash PMIs are the first November read on European demand, so they set the tone for the euro and the DAX at the start of the week.
events.ifHigher: Above the 51.1 composite forecast: EUR firms, DAX and European cyclicals bid, growth-scare fears ease slightly.
events.ifLower: Below 51: EUR offered against a strong dollar, European equities extend the risk-off, defensive assets bid.

events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary survey of UK manufacturing and services purchasing managers; above 50 signals expansion.
events.whyItMatters: Sterling trades against a dollar near multi-month highs. Services dominate UK output, so the services flash tells traders whether domestic demand is holding up as global equities sell off.
events.ifHigher: Services above 52.5: GBP supported, gilt yields firm, FTSE domestics bid.
events.ifLower: Services below 52: GBP sold, growth worries build, gilt yields soften.

events.whatItIs: A scheduled vesting release of Humanity Protocol (H) tokens, about 293 million tokens worth roughly $15M or 6.8% of circulating supply per unlock trackers.
events.whyItMatters: Bitcoin is near a six-month low after a $2B liquidation wave, and liquidity in altcoins is thin. An unlock equal to nearly 7% of circulating supply is large relative to the market, so it can pressure H while the broader tape is weak.
events.ifHigher: Recipients hold or stake: H absorbs the supply with limited drawdown and altcoin sentiment stays stable.
events.ifLower: Recipients sell into thin liquidity: H underperforms and the unlock adds a small risk-off tilt across smaller tokens.
events.learnMore:
A token unlock is the release of previously locked tokens to team members, investors, or ecosystem funds under a vesting schedule. It adds to circulating supply, which can pressure price if recipients sell.

Impact depends on size relative to circulating supply and on market depth. A release of about 7% of circulating supply matters far more than a small linear monthly drip. Trackers such as DefiLlama and Token Unlocks list these events, but amounts and dollar values differ between them and move with price, so check the tracker before acting.

events.whatItIs: S&P Global's preliminary November survey of US manufacturing and services purchasing managers, released at 14:45 UTC; above 50 signals expansion.
events.whyItMatters: After the S&P 500's worst week since April 2025, traders want to know whether the economy is cracking or whether activity is still strong enough to keep the Fed on a December hike path. The prices-paid components also feed the inflation debate ahead of Wednesday's PCE.
events.ifHigher: Composite above 55.6 with firm prices paid: yields and USD rise, December hike odds firm, gold and bitcoin come under pressure, equities stay heavy.
events.ifLower: Composite below 55 or a sharp services miss: yields ease, USD softens, gold and bitcoin bounce, equities get a relief bid on lower hike odds.
events.learnMore:
The S&P Global flash PMIs are the earliest monthly read on private-sector activity. They survey purchasing managers at several hundred firms and publish a diffusion index where 50 separates expansion from contraction. The flash release captures roughly 85% of final responses, which is why it moves markets before the full data arrive.

Traders look beyond the headline composite at new orders, which lead output, and at the input and output price indexes, which hint at where inflation is heading. In a hiking-risk environment, strong activity with rising prices paid is the hawkish combination, while weak activity with easing prices is the dovish one.

Because the survey is released before most hard data for the month, surprises can move yields and the dollar quickly. It is also a diffusion index, so a drop from 55.9 to 55.0 still signals solid expansion.

events.event: BoE's Pill and ECB's Lane Speak
events.whatItIs: Scheduled appearances by Bank of England chief economist Huw Pill and ECB chief economist Philip Lane; exact times were not confirmed at the time of writing.
events.whyItMatters: Both are the economists who frame their banks' policy debates. With the Fed leaning toward a hike, any signal that the BoE or ECB will follow or diverge moves GBP and EUR against the dollar.
events.ifHigher: More hawkish than expected on inflation: GBP or EUR firms, front-end yields rise, equities wobble.
events.ifLower: Cautious on growth or inflation: GBP or EUR softens against the dollar, yields ease.

events.whatItIs: NY Fed President John Williams, a permanent FOMC voter, speaks on the economy, inflation, and interest rates at 21:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: He is the only scheduled Fed speaker this week and speaks right after Friday's 3.7% S&P 500 drop. Markets price a December hike as highly likely, so any hint that the Committee will pause, or that it is ready to move faster, matters more than usual.
events.ifHigher: Signals a December hike or a faster path: yields and USD jump, gold and bitcoin fall, equities extend losses.
events.ifLower: Stresses data dependence or growth risks: December hike odds soften, USD slips, gold and bitcoin bounce, equities steady.

events.event: Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Zoom, and Agilent earnings (after close)
events.whatItIs: Quarterly results from Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Zoom Communications, and Agilent Technologies, all reporting after the US close.
events.whyItMatters: With the Nasdaq negative for 2026 after the AI sell-off, HPE's AI-server and networking commentary is read as a gauge of enterprise AI spending. Zoom and Agilent give a read on software and life-science demand.
events.ifHigher: Beats with firm AI-infrastructure guidance: tech stabilizes after-hours and the risk-on tone improves.
events.ifLower: Misses or cautious guidance: AI-linked names extend the sell-off and equity futures slip.

events.event: Monad (MON) team and investor token unlock
events.whatItIs: The end of the one-year lock on Monad team and investor tokens: roughly 17 billion MON, valued at about $280M-$320M depending on the tracker, with the exact time estimated.
events.whyItMatters: It is the largest unlock of the month, and it lands with bitcoin near a six-month low and altcoin liquidity thin. Trackers show the release as larger than the previously reported circulating supply, so the supply overhang is the story even if holders do not sell.
events.ifHigher: Recipients stake or hold: MON absorbs the supply with a limited drawdown and the unlock fades as a headline.
events.ifLower: Early investors sell into thin liquidity: MON drops sharply and the move spills into other recently launched layer-1 tokens.
events.learnMore:
A cliff unlock releases a large block of tokens at once after a lock-up ends, unlike a linear schedule that drips supply daily. Team and investor allocations are typically cheap to their holders, which raises the incentive to sell.

The key measure is the unlock size relative to circulating supply and to daily trading volume. When the release exceeds the supply already trading, as DefiLlama shows for MON, price often drifts lower into the event as traders hedge. Not every unlock is sold: some holders restake, move tokens to custody, or hold for governance.

Amounts, times, and dollar values differ between trackers and move with price, so confirm them on the tracker before trading.

events.whatItIs: The Ifo Institute's monthly survey of about 9,000 German firms on current conditions and expectations, the country's most-watched business sentiment gauge.
events.whyItMatters: After Monday's flash PMIs, the Ifo shows whether German business sentiment is stabilizing while the euro sits under dollar pressure. A drop below 90 would reinforce the weak-growth narrative in Europe's largest economy.
events.ifHigher: Above 90.2: EUR firms modestly, DAX and German industrials bid.
events.ifLower: Below 90: EUR softens, DAX underperforms, European growth worries build.

events.event: Best Buy, Medtronic, Analog Devices, and Dollar Tree earnings (before open)
events.whatItIs: Quarterly results from a consumer-electronics retailer, a medical-device maker, a chip supplier, and a discount retailer, all before the US open.
events.whyItMatters: With inflation running near 3.8% on the headline PCE and equities in correction, Best Buy and Dollar Tree give an early read on holiday-season consumer demand, while Analog Devices adds a signal on industrial and analog chip demand.
events.ifHigher: Strong holiday guidance: consumer names rebound and equities get a small lift.
events.ifLower: Weak guidance or margin pressure: consumer discretionary slides and fuels the stagflation narrative.

events.whatItIs: ADP's weekly four-week average estimate of private-sector job gains, a high-frequency read ahead of the monthly payrolls report.
events.whyItMatters: It is one of the few labor readings in a holiday week and a preview of the December 4 jobs report. A softening trend would feed the argument that the Fed should not hike into a slowing economy.
events.ifHigher: Stronger job gains: yields and USD firm, December hike odds hold, gold and bitcoin soften.
events.ifLower: Weaker hiring: yields dip, USD eases, gold and bitcoin bounce.

events.whatItIs: The Conference Board's monthly survey of about 3,000 US households on current conditions and expectations, including labor-market perceptions.
events.whyItMatters: October's 91.7 was the first improvement in four months, with better labor-market perceptions. Consumers drive about two-thirds of GDP, and after Friday's equity rout and with inflation near 3.8%, this tests whether spending resilience holds going into the holiday season.
events.ifHigher: Above 92.5: consumers resilient, yields and USD rise, December hike odds firm, equities mixed.
events.ifLower: Below 90: confidence rolling over, yields ease, USD softens, gold gets a bid and consumer stocks lag.
events.learnMore:
The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index is built from a household survey and has two parts: the Present Situation Index, which covers current business and job conditions, and the Expectations Index, which covers the six-month outlook. A reading of Expectations below 80 has historically been associated with recession risk.

The most-watched piece is the labor differential, the gap between households saying jobs are plentiful and those saying jobs are hard to get. It tracks the unemployment rate and often moves before payrolls do.

Markets react to the headline against forecast, but the breakdown matters: a rise driven by stock-market optimism can reverse quickly, while a rise in the labor differential is more durable. In a week with PCE inflation due, a strong confidence print adds to hawkish pricing.

events.event: Bank of Canada Governor Macklem Speaks
events.whatItIs: A public speech by Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem on the economy and monetary policy.
events.whyItMatters: USD/CAD is driven by the rate gap with a hawkish Fed and by oil near $92 Brent. Macklem's tone ahead of the BoC's December meeting guides CAD this week.
events.ifHigher: Hawkish on inflation: CAD firms, Canadian yields rise, USD/CAD dips.
events.ifLower: Dovish or focused on growth risks: CAD sold, USD/CAD higher.

events.event: API Weekly Crude Oil Stock Change (week ending November 20)
events.whatItIs: The American Petroleum Institute's private estimate of the weekly change in US crude stockpiles, released at 21:30 UTC ahead of the official EIA figures.
events.whyItMatters: Brent is near $92.49, down 3.8% on the week, with Middle East developments in focus and OPEC+ meeting Sunday. The API sets the early tone for Wednesday's EIA report.
events.ifHigher: A bigger-than-expected build: crude dips in after-hours trade and energy equities soften.
events.ifLower: A bigger-than-expected draw: crude firms and energy stocks edge higher.

events.event: Dell, Workday, Autodesk, and HP earnings (after close)
events.whatItIs: Quarterly results from Dell Technologies, Workday, Autodesk, and HP Inc. after the US close.
events.whyItMatters: Dell's AI-server orders are a direct read on the AI hardware trade that drove the Nasdaq below its 2026 start. Workday and Autodesk show whether enterprise software demand is holding up.
events.ifHigher: Strong AI-server backlog and firm software guidance: tech stabilizes after the sell-off and risk appetite improves.
events.ifLower: Weak guidance: AI hardware and software names extend losses and equity futures slip.

events.whatItIs: The Australian Bureau of Statistics' monthly consumer price index, with the RBA's trimmed-mean core measure published alongside.
events.whyItMatters: Inflation re-accelerated to 4.3% YoY in September, and local previews flag a high October print because credit-card surcharge pass-throughs add to prices. It sets the odds of further RBA tightening and moves AUD, which is also a proxy for global risk appetite after Friday's sell-off.
events.ifHigher: Hotter headline or trimmed-mean core: AUD jumps, Australian yields rise, RBA hike odds increase.
events.ifLower: Softer than expected: AUD sold, yields ease, RBA stays patient.
events.learnMore:
Australia's CPI measures price changes across a basket of household goods and services. The ABS now publishes a full monthly series, and the RBA watches the trimmed-mean measure, which strips out the most extreme price moves, more closely than the headline.

AUD trades on the gap between Australian and US rates and on China and commodity demand. A hot print raises the odds of an RBA hike and supports the Aussie, while a soft print narrows that gap and pairs with a strong dollar to push AUD/USD lower.

events.whatItIs: A scheduled vesting release of Plasma (XPL) tokens, roughly 89 million tokens or about 1.9% of circulating supply per one tracker; dollar values differ between trackers.
events.whyItMatters: The release is small relative to circulating supply and is unlikely to move the majors. It adds mild supply pressure on XPL while altcoin liquidity is thin and bitcoin is near a six-month low.
events.ifHigher: Recipients hold or stake: XPL absorbs the supply with limited drawdown.
events.ifLower: Recipients sell into thin liquidity: XPL underperforms with a small risk-off tilt in smaller tokens.

events.whatItIs: Quarterly results from Deere & Company, the world's largest farm-equipment maker, before the US open.
events.whyItMatters: Deere is a read on farm incomes, equipment demand, and tariff and commodity-price effects on agriculture. It is the only major earnings report on a week when US markets are open only three and a half days.
events.ifHigher: Strong orders and firm guidance: industrials and ag-linked names lift into the holiday.
events.ifLower: Weak guidance: industrials soften and growth worries get another data point.

events.event: Core PCE Price Index and Personal Income and Spending (October 2026)
events.previous: Core +0.3% MoM / +3.1% YoY; headline +0.5% MoM / +3.6% YoY (September 2026)
events.forecast: Core +0.3% MoM / +3.2% YoY; headline about +3.8% YoY
events.whatItIs: The BEA's measure of consumer-price inflation that the Fed targets, released with personal income and spending, at 13:30 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: It is the week's decisive release. Markets price a 25 basis point hike on December 9 as highly likely, with some odds of a 50 basis point move. Core running at 3.2% and headline near 3.8% would confirm that inflation is still rising, just before the Fed's blackout begins on Saturday.
events.ifHigher: Core above +0.3% MoM or 3.2% YoY: December hike locked in and 50 bp odds rise, yields and USD jump, gold and bitcoin fall, equities extend the correction.
events.ifLower: Core at or below +0.2% MoM or 3.1% YoY: hike odds ease, yields and USD slip, gold and bitcoin rebound, equities get a relief rally.

events.whatItIs: The BEA's second estimate of third-quarter real GDP growth, with revised consumer-spending and price components.
events.whyItMatters: A growth rate near 3.5% is what lets the Fed consider hikes into an equity sell-off. The revision also updates the Q3 inflation components that feed the PCE debate.
events.ifHigher: Revised above +3.5%: growth resilience confirmed, yields and USD rise, hike odds hold, gold and equities soften.
events.ifLower: Revised below +3.2%: growth cooling, yields ease, USD softens, gold gets a bid.

events.whatItIs: The Census Bureau's preliminary report on new orders for long-lasting manufactured goods such as aircraft, machinery, and vehicles.
events.whyItMatters: Orders for capital goods signal business investment. After the AI sell-off, traders will focus on core capital-goods orders for signs that companies are still spending on equipment.
events.ifHigher: Strong orders, especially core capital goods: yields and USD firm, cyclicals bid.
events.ifLower: Weak orders: yields ease, growth worries build and USD slips slightly.

events.whatItIs: The Labor Department's weekly count of new unemployment-insurance filings, released a day early because of Thanksgiving.
events.whyItMatters: It is the only high-frequency labor read this week and arrives with PCE and GDP. A sustained rise would add to the case against a December hike.
events.ifHigher: Claims jump: labor market cooling, yields and USD ease, gold and bitcoin firm.
events.ifLower: Low claims: labor market firm, yields and USD hold, hike odds stay high.

events.event: EIA Crude Oil Inventories (week ending November 20)
events.whatItIs: The EIA's weekly estimate of change in US commercial crude stockpiles, released Wednesday at 15:30 UTC as usual before the holiday.
events.whyItMatters: Brent fell 3.8% last week to $92.49 as the equity and metals sell-off hit demand expectations, with OPEC+ meeting Sunday. This is the last major oil data point before the long weekend.
events.ifHigher: A larger-than-expected build: WTI and Brent dip, energy equities soften.
events.ifLower: A larger-than-expected draw: crude gains, energy stocks firm, inflation concerns rise.

events.whatItIs: The Fed's anecdotal summary of economic conditions in its 12 districts, published about two weeks before each FOMC meeting.
events.whyItMatters: It is the last official Fed publication before the blackout and arrives before the December 8-9 meeting. Language on prices, wages, and consumer spending shapes how hawkish the Committee sounds.
events.ifHigher: Reports of broad price pressures and firm wages: yields and USD rise, gold and bitcoin fall.
events.ifLower: Reports of softer demand and hiring: yields ease, USD slips, equities get a modest lift.
events.learnMore:
The Beige Book compiles anecdotal reports from business contacts in each Federal Reserve district. It is qualitative, so traders scan for changes in tone, such as whether price pressures are described as widespread or moderate, and whether the outlook is pessimistic.

It carries no numbers and rarely surprises, but it gives the Committee a ground-level check on data and arrives before the pre-meeting blackout.

events.event: Thanksgiving: US stock and bond markets closed
events.whatItIs: A US federal holiday on which the NYSE, Nasdaq, and the US bond market are closed.
events.whyItMatters: Cash equities and Treasuries are shut after the worst week since April 2025, so there is no US price discovery for a full day. Futures trade a shortened session and thin liquidity can exaggerate moves in the dollar, crypto, and oil, which keep trading.
events.ifHigher: Not a data release. If risk sentiment improves, thin liquidity can make crypto and FX rallies look larger than they are.
events.ifLower: Not a data release. Bad news overnight cannot be priced in US cash markets until Friday's open, so gaps can build.
events.learnMore:
On US holidays cash equities and the Treasury market close, but futures, FX, and crypto keep trading with far fewer participants. Wide spreads and sudden gaps are more common, and stop orders are more likely to be triggered by small flows.

The session after a holiday also tends to carry catch-up volume. Traders typically reduce position size and avoid starting large new trades into a holiday gap.

events.whatItIs: The Bank of Korea's monetary policy decision, usually announced at 01:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Korea is a bellwether for global chip and trade cycles, and the won is under pressure from a 19-month-high dollar. The decision shows whether Asian central banks are following the Fed's hawkish shift.
events.ifHigher: A hawkish surprise: KRW firms and regional yields rise.
events.ifLower: A dovish hold or cut: KRW sold, USD/KRW higher, Asian risk assets stay soft.

events.whatItIs: GfK's monthly survey of German consumer sentiment and willingness to spend, a forward indicator for household spending.
events.whyItMatters: German household demand has been the weak link in the eurozone recovery, and this is the main European data point on Thanksgiving.
events.ifHigher: Improving sentiment: EUR edges higher and German retail and consumer stocks firm.
events.ifLower: Falling sentiment: EUR softens and growth concerns for Europe's largest economy persist.

events.event: ECB Account of the October Monetary Policy Meeting
events.whatItIs: The detailed record of the ECB Governing Council's discussion at its October meeting, published about four weeks later.
events.whyItMatters: With the Fed leaning toward a hike and EUR/USD weak, traders look for any sign the ECB shares concerns about inflation or growth, which guides the euro's path into the December meeting.
events.ifHigher: Hawkish tone with members open to tightening: EUR firms, euro yields rise.
events.ifLower: Cautious tone focused on growth risks: EUR softens against the dollar.

events.whatItIs: Consumer prices in Tokyo, released 08:30 Friday Tokyo time, a leading indicator for national Japanese inflation.
events.whyItMatters: It is the earliest read on Japanese inflation and shapes expectations for the next BoJ move. With the dollar near 19-month highs, yen traders watch it for signs the BoJ may be pushed to act.
events.ifHigher: Hotter core: JPY firms, JGB yields rise, BoJ tightening bets increase.
events.ifLower: Cooler core: JPY weakens against the dollar, BoJ stays patient.

events.event: Fed communications blackout begins Saturday ahead of the December 8-9 FOMC
events.whatItIs: Fed officials stop commenting on monetary policy from the second Saturday before an FOMC meeting until the day after it ends.
events.whyItMatters: Friday is the last day Fed speakers can sway December expectations. After that, markets lean on data such as PCE and the November jobs report, and on whatever the Beige Book and the weekend press imply.
events.ifHigher: Not a data release. Hawkish repricing from PCE has no Fed pushback until the December 9 decision.
events.ifLower: Not a data release. Dovish repricing is unchallenged by officials until the blackout ends.

events.whatItIs: The National Bureau of Statistics' monthly report on profits at large industrial firms, a gauge of factory-sector health.
events.whyItMatters: It is the last major China data point of November. Weak profits would add to demand worries for copper and oil during a commodity sell-off.
events.ifHigher: Stronger profits: CNH and AUD firm, copper and oil supported.
events.ifLower: Falling profits: China-cyclicals sold, oil and metals soften, USD stays bid.

events.whatItIs: Early national inflation prints for France (07:45 UTC) and Spain (08:00 UTC) that feed into the eurozone flash HICP due next week.
events.whyItMatters: They give the first hint of what next week's eurozone inflation flash will show, which matters for ECB expectations as the euro trades near multi-month lows.
events.ifHigher: Hotter prints: EUR firms and ECB tightening bets rise.
events.ifLower: Cooler prints: EUR softens and euro yields ease.

events.event: US stock markets close early (18:00 UTC); bonds close 19:00 UTC
events.whatItIs: The day after Thanksgiving is a shortened session: stocks close at 18:00 UTC and the bond market at 19:00 UTC.
events.whyItMatters: Liquidity is thin and volume is low, so any large flow can move indices, and S&P Global's France review lands after the close. Traders often avoid new large positions before the weekend.
events.ifHigher: Not a data release. A strong rebound in a thin tape is less reliable than one on full volume.
events.ifLower: Not a data release. Selling in a thin tape can overshoot, and weekend risk adds to caution.

events.event: S&P Global credit rating review of France (after the European close)
events.whatItIs: A scheduled S&P Global review of France's sovereign credit rating, published after European markets close.
events.whyItMatters: Past sovereign rating actions on France have moved the OAT-Bund spread at the next open, and a thin post-holiday tape can exaggerate the first move. Weekend news flow then sets the tone for Monday's open.
events.ifHigher: Rating or outlook affirmed or improved: OAT-Bund spreads tighten and EUR gets a small lift on Monday.
events.ifLower: Downgrade or negative outlook: OAT-Bund spreads widen, French banks and EUR come under pressure on Monday.
